screening_results.reason: This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind) using a Why/How task in healthy adult participants (N=29, 10, and 21 across studies; ages 19–38), so it addresses social-related processing in healthy adults. Group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts are reported (Why>How, How>Why, Belief>Photo) with cluster-level FWE correction and tables of peak coordinates (Tables 2–4 and 3), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Behavioral methods, imaging acquisition, preprocessing, and group analyses are described in detail. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain maps), and I6 (maps reported in tables/figures/text) are met. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample-only, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind for cooperation vs. competition) in healthy adults (N=18, ages 21–38). The task is social-related (dyadic game ‘Shapes’) and uses task-evoked fMRI. The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate contrasts (e.g., coop active > coop passive; comp active > comp passive) with cluster-level correction and supplementary tables/figures, and also reports ROI and MVPA results. Whole-brain results for the healthy participant group are clearly described in the text and supplementary material. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are met: the paper does not report only ROI, connectivity-only, or multivariate-only whole-brain maps, nor is it non-empirical or outside the adult age range. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (social vs non-social cues/feedback) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Results are reported mainly as between-group contrasts (BPD vs HC), ROI analyses (amygdala), and regression/interaction effects; no whole-brain healthy-group univariate activation map is provided in the main text. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E4 met: the manuscript does not report an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. Inclusion I3 met: the study used fMRI during social-related tasks (social incentive delay, emotional face processing, etc.). Inclusion I4 met: the paper includes a healthy adult control group (ages 50–60) with results reported separately. Inclusion I5 NOT met: there is no clear whole-brain, group-level control-only task activation map; reported whole-brain maps are for the entire sample (combined groups) or ROI-focused analyses, and between-group contrasts are provided but no univariate whole-brain healthy-group map is clearly presented. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related, language-based task (listening to film excerpts and inferring characters' mental states), satisfying the review objective. The sample includes a healthy adult group (n=28) reported separately from the schizophrenia group. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and contrasts for healthy controls (one-sample t-test, INT>HIN; Fig.1, Table 2) with voxelwise thresholds and coordinates. Results for the healthy group are clearly described in text, figures, and tables. Full-text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of eligibility. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This fMRI study investigates visual processing of social interactions using task-based fMRI in a healthy adult sample (N=21; ages 18–35). It includes social-related tasks (dynamic dyadic interactions and separate localizer tasks for interaction, bodies, faces, and mentalizing), satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults, satisfying I4. The methods explicitly describe group-level whole-brain analyses for localizer contrasts (e.g., interaction > scrambled interaction; bodies > objects; faces > objects; mentalizing > pain) used to define ROIs via a group-constrained procedure, indicating availability of group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy group, satisfying I5 and I6 (maps/contrasts are described and likely reported in main/supplementary materials). Although the primary reported results emphasize MVPA/ROI analyses and searchlight (multivariate) results, the presence and use of univariate whole-brain localizer contrasts meets the whole-brain reporting requirement. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (observation of dynamic facial expressions — social communication). The sample comprises 51 healthy adult participants (mean age 22.5), and analyses used whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise contrasts (dynamic expressions vs dynamic mosaics) with family-wise error correction; results are reported as statistical maps/tables and figures. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (learning about others’ preference similarity and affiliation) in healthy adults (n=25, mean age 25.1). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation results (cluster-corrected contrasts, peak MNI coordinates, conjunction analyses) and describes voxelwise parametric modulators from model-based GLMs; results are reported for the healthy/control sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside adult range, not MVPA-only, and not non-empirical).

This study reports an fMRI task probing perception and understanding of self and others (body perception task), which is a social-related construct. The sample comprises healthy adults (N=30, ages ~26), reported separately, meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper presents group-level, voxelwise whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., own body > scrambled, same-sex/ opposite-sex > scrambled, parametric analyses) with cluster-forming thresholds and corrected p-values, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are reported in text, figures, and supporting tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or non-adult sample) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

The paper reports resting-state fMRI connectivity analyses and behavioral assessments; it does not use a task-based social fMRI paradigm nor report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (contains a healthy adult control group). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no task-based fMRI during a social-related task), I5 (no whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map from the healthy group). Exclusion criteria triggered: E3 (study reports only resting-state analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion relevant to resting-state analyses.

This empirical fMRI study uses the Animated Triangles Task (a social/ToM paradigm) with a healthy adult control group (matched, ages 18–30) and reports group-level whole-brain univariate task contrasts. The Methods describe voxelwise whole-brain analysis (FLAME, cluster correction), and the Results explicitly describe control-group activations (pSTS, temporal gyrus, etc.) with individual group activations referenced in supplementary material. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply.

Although this paper reports task-based fMRI in a healthy adult sample (N=20) with several social-cognitive contrasts (ToM, faces, biological motion, voices, language) and provides group-level voxelwise results within the STS and peak coordinates (meets I3, I4, I6), the authors explicitly state that second-level (group) analyses were restricted to a bilateral STS mask. The manuscript does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group. Because inclusion criterion I5 requires at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map and this is not provided, the study fails to meet all inclusion criteria and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are directly triggered by the report; the exclusion is due to failure to meet I5.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (Social Detection Task) where participants judged valence of naturalistic social interactions (meets I3). Sample consists of a healthy adult group (final N=38, ages 18–30) with results reported for this healthy group (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses (random-effects, full-factorial ANOVA) and contrasts such as Social > Non-social with cluster-level FWE correction; results are summarized in a table and figures (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, sample is adult, and univariate whole-brain task effects are presented. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures, references). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a Face Matching Task (implicit emotional face perception) which is a social-related task (perception/understanding of others). The sample comprises healthy adults (n=10, mean age 25). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM task-evoked contrasts (one-sample t-tests; results reported with P<0.005, k=10 and referenced in Supplementary Table S2 and Figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group maps. Whole-brain results are described in the text and supplementary materials. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, seed-only/resting-state-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, multivariate-only results, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates an fMRI study of live eye contact (social task) so I3 is likely met. However, the full text is not available to verify participant sample (age range, healthy adults) and to confirm reporting of group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps (I4 and I5). Because I4 and I5 cannot be confirmed from the provided content, the study cannot be judged to meet all inclusion criteria. Exclusion is due to incomplete reporting preventing assessment of required criteria; request full text for reassessment.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (understanding others' regret), meeting the review objective. It uses functional MRI during a social-related task (observation of another's regret and self-play) and tests perception/understanding of others (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (24 females, 24 males across two studies; ages within 19–31), reported separately and meeting the adult sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., IP minus IF, OP minus OF), parametric and conjunction analyses, SPM random-effects maps, thresholding and reported activation foci/coordinates—fulfilling whole-brain evidence (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not MVPA-only, and this is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an fMRI task engaging imitation/spontaneous imitation (a social-related process relevant to perception/understanding of others). The sample consists of healthy adults (N=37; age range 18–25). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric modulation of Urge during imitation) with cluster-corrected thresholds, tables and figures describing activations, and additionally reports PPI connectivity; whole-brain univariate results are clearly presented for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, not between-group-only, adult healthy sample, univariate maps reported). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study used a socio-emotional preferential task (SePT) involving social appraisal of faces ("Do you like this face?"), meeting the social-task requirement (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=13) with results reported alongside patients, satisfying the healthy-sample requirement (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked effects and group-level contrasts (e.g., task effect like>gender; baseline HC>SZ), and lists peak coordinates and cluster results in Supplementary Materials (Table S1, Figures S1–S2), meeting the whole-brain evidence reporting requirements (I5, I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without unmasked healthy-group maps, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) are met. Hence the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (implicit/explicit detection of eye-gaze and self-propelling motion; implicit mental-inference task). Participants are healthy adults (aged 19–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses (one-sample t-tests, voxel-wise contrasts [E–O], [S–X], cluster-size correction) with results presented in figures and tables. These meet the review’s requirements for task-based fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain univariate results clearly attributed to the healthy group.

This fMRI study investigates voice-identity recognition (speaker vs. speech task; vocal vs. non-vocal sounds), which is a social-related process (perception/understanding of others and social communication). It includes a healthy adult control group (two matched control groups, n=16 each; combined n=32; ages ~31) reported separately from the two developmental cases. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for the controls (e.g., vocal>non-vocal; speaker>speech), with statistical maps and tables/figures (and whole-brain results described and supplied in Supplementary tables). Reporting meets acceptable formats. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group healthy whole-brain activations).

Exclusion criteria met: E2 and E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI during a social interaction task — iterated Prisoner's Dilemma) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 18–22). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the manuscript does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group). The reported analyses are ROI-based univariate analyses and task-based gPPI connectivity constrained to predefined ROIs / small-volume masks. No unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group activation maps or coordinate tables for whole-brain contrasts are presented in this full text, and the connectivity results are seed/ROI-based rather than whole-brain task activation, so the study must be excluded under E2 and E3.

This is an fMRI study employing a social-role judgment task (self, friend, celebrity) addressing perception/understanding of self and others, meeting I3. The sample comprises 37 healthy adult participants (mean age 22.9), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (self vs. celebrity; friend vs. celebrity) with coordinates and FDR-corrected thresholds and tabulated activations, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes univariate whole-brain activation maps alongside connectivity analyses).

This empirical fMRI study uses a social decision-making task (modified Prisoner’s Dilemma) engaging Theory-of-Mind/social cognition processes, satisfying I3. Sample comprises 20 healthy adults aged 23–38, meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., conjunction of task>control, COMP>COOP) with cluster-level correction and tables/figures, satisfying I5 and acceptable reporting per I6. No exclusion criteria are triggered: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, not outside adult age range, not multivariate-only, and it is an empirical report. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using a task that manipulates social-cognitive content (agency vs. communion) via valence classification, involving healthy adult participants (N=42, ages 18–25). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (agency vs fixation, communion vs fixation, conjunction, and direct contrasts) with AlphaSim correction and presents results in tables/figures. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=16–17 for primary analyses) performing social-cognitive tasks (explicit emotion attribution and implicit face viewing), which clearly fall under social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). The paper presents group-level whole-brain univariate analyses (e.g., Emotion > Expression, Face > Scramble, conjunctions, and whole-brain target-dependent contrasts) with cluster-level FWE correction and reports whole-brain statistical maps/tables (figures and supplementary tables). Sample ages (21–46) are within adult range and healthy status is explicitly stated. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, multivariate-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI study of social hierarchy processing in healthy adults using task-based paradigms that manipulate social status—clearly a social-related task (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=72 across experiments; social experiments N=48 reported separately; ages within 19–43/19–38 ranges), satisfying the adult healthy-sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise univariate task contrasts (e.g., 'superior player > inferior player', outcome contrasts) with FDR-corrected thresholds and tables/coordinates, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are presented. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Hence the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of self–other processing (a social-related task) with a healthy typically-developing (TD) adult control group and reported within-group whole-brain task activation for the control group. Specifically: (1) the task probes self/other semantic judgments (meets I3); (2) a healthy adult control group is reported (mean age ~21.9, acceptable minor extension below 18 in range) (meets I4); (3) the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-group activation maps for the TD group (meets I5); and (4) results are reported in text/tables/figures (meets I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy maps, not exclusively non-adult sample, and is empirical). The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded for E2 and E3. The study used fMRI during vocal emotional processing (a social-communication task) in healthy adult participants, so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the analyses and results are ROI-based functional connectivity and graph-theoretical measures (Power-264 ROI–ROI FC), and the paper does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked univariate activation maps or coordinate tables/figures clearly identified as healthy-group task effects. Therefore it does not meet I5 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) nor I6 (acceptable forms of whole-brain univariate results). Because it reports only ROI/connectivity analyses without an univariate healthy-group whole-brain task activation map, exclusion criteria E2 (ROI-only) and E3 (connectivity-only without whole-brain task activation) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction perception using task-based fMRI in healthy adult samples (Experiments 1 and 2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., interaction > independent actions) with surface-based random-effects group analysis and FDR-corrected clusters (Experiment 1), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked activation maps. Participants are healthy adults (ages 18–34). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses fMRI during a social-affective cinematic task (meets I3) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (meets I4). However, the manuscript does not present any univariate, whole-brain group-level task activation map or voxelwise task contrast for the healthy group (no statistical maps or coordinate tables reported for a healthy-group task effect). Instead, analyses focus on network-cohesion (connectivity) metrics derived from a priori ROI/network nodes and group comparisons. Therefore it fails I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map) and I6 (no acceptable whole-brain results reported). This places the paper into exclusion categories: E2 (ROI/connectivity focus with no whole-brain results) and E3 (connectivity-only task analyses without healthy-group whole-brain activation), and E4 (results primarily reported as between-group connectivity differences without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (representation of social interaction/social context vs self-generation) in healthy adults. Sample: 24 healthy adults (age 18–28) reported separately — satisfies adult healthy sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (SPM5 random-effects analyses) with tables of activation coordinates and figures (e.g., Table 3, Figs. 3–5) — satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a face-perception task (faces vs houses), which is a social-related process (Perception/Understanding of Others). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (undergraduates, mean age 18.9), with a healthy subgroup (N=22) receiving fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses (contrast images, significant clusters, FWE-corrected maps, and a table of activations); suprathreshold voxel counts in bilateral fusiform gyrus are extracted from whole-brain results. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social task (processing direct vs. averted gaze), includes a typically developing (healthy control) group with adult participants and reports results for that group separately, and provides whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts and coordinates (Table 2) for the control group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. Thus it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction perception in healthy adults that reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain univariate contrasts (voxelwise p<.001, cluster-based p<.05) and coordinate tables/figures. The experiment used fMRI while participants viewed congruent, incongruent, and non-interacting person dyads during a sex-categorization task (a social-perception task). Sample: 12 healthy adult participants (ages 21–31). Whole-brain group analyses and tables of peak coordinates are reported (see Table 3 and whole-brain contrasts described in Results). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a whole-brain task fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 22.3) using a social interaction task (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) that probes retaliatory aggression—clearly a social-related process. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses, corrected statistical maps, and Talairach coordinate tables/figures for task-evoked contrasts and parametric modulations. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given these points, the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This study used task-based fMRI with social stimuli (faces) embedded in an oddball target-detection task, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises 19 healthy adult participants (ages 19.3–47.5) with screening and IQ reporting, meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts (e.g., face targets > novels, shape targets > novels, direct comparisons) with cluster-corrected maps, figures, and a table of MNI coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and should be included in the review.

Exclusion(s) met: E4 (the paper reports primarily between-group contrasts and group differences and does not clearly present an unmasked, whole-brain, healthy-group task-evoked activation map). Inclusion(s) met: I4 (the study includes and reports data from a healthy adult control group, separate from clinical groups). Inclusion(s) not met: I3 (the fMRI task is a low-contrast moving/static concentric-ring visual motion paradigm, not a social-related task), I5 (the manuscript does not clearly provide a whole-brain, group-level task activation map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group; reported results focus on ROIs and between-group comparisons). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for fMRI of social-related processing in healthy adults and is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (20 registered voters, mean age ~35) that used an event-related fMRI paradigm while subjects viewed faces of presidential candidates — a social/other-perception task (political affiliation and social attitude toward others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise activation analyses (e.g., faces vs. rest; candidate contrasts; correlations with ratings) thresholded and presented as statistical maps, tables of coordinates, and figures. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task domain (I3), sample (I4), whole-brain group-level reporting (I5), and acceptable reporting format (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical study). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social interaction task (Cyberball ball-toss) and reports group-level whole-brain univariate activation results. The Methods describe fMRI acquisition and SPM8 whole-brain random-effects analyses; Results report voxelwise clusters with MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction (right ventral striatum and precuneus) and include figures/tables. Sample includes healthy adult participants (n=31 analyzed, ages ~21). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not developmental/geriatric-only, not MVPA-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition using tasks (affective ToM, emotion recognition, face processing) meeting the review topic. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=13) with results reported separately. The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain activation results for single groups (stated as available in Supplementary Tables S1–S4) and describes whole-brain analyses in the text (with thresholds and contrasts), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group, voxelwise task-evoked map; reporting in supplementary material is acceptable per I6. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not non-empirical, adult sample).

Exclusion summary: E3 applies — the study reports only resting-state functional connectivity analyses and does not report any group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked activation maps. Inclusion met: I4 (sample = healthy adults aged 18–22). Inclusion not met: I3 (no conventional fMRI social-related task; study uses resting-state with instruction manipulations rather than a task-evoked social processing paradigm) and I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation map reported). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it does not provide the required whole-brain task activation data for healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (Cyberball social exclusion and subsequent Dictator Game decisions) in healthy adults (n=26, mean age 20.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., exclusion no ball > inclusion ball; Excluders > Includers; Excluders equality > Includers equality) with peak coordinates and tables of clusters (Tables 1–2) and figures, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise whole-brain results. All core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present, and healthy-group results are reported explicitly. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (E2–E7).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (free online imitation) in healthy adults (N=23, females aged 18–30). It reports group-level whole-brain univariate activation contrasts (GLM results; imitating, being imitated, observation vs rest) with correction for multiple comparisons (FWE p<0.05) and provides coordinates/tables and figures. Although the paper also reports PPI connectivity analyses, it also contains univariate whole-brain healthy-group task effects. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text content is incomplete (only title, authors, journal metadata shown). Unable to confirm key inclusion criteria: I3 (unclear whether study uses task-based fMRI for a social-related task versus only resting-state), I4 (cannot verify that a healthy adult control group is present and reported separately), I5 (cannot verify that a whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group is reported), I6 (cannot verify location or format of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) can be positively applied from the supplied content. Excluding because required inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the provided full text; please supply the complete article (methods/results) for reassessment.

This fMRI study investigates Theory of Mind (affective and cognitive), a social cognition task, in a sample of healthy adult participants and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected cluster results and tables). The methods describe whole-brain contrasts (AToM and CToM vs controls), group-level regression with RFQ, and one-sample t-tests; results present cluster-level whole-brain findings (tables/figure). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, not multivariate-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social vs monetary reward processing using an incentive-delay task in healthy adult participants (N=63; ages ~20–36). It reports group-level, task-evoked univariate contrasts (e.g., reward anticipation, social>monetary; feedback contrasts) with whole-brain and ROI analyses and provides whole-brain FWE-corrected results and tables/figures clearly from the healthy cohort. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps/contrasts), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, adult sample, univariate maps present). Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI during a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) probing social processing; (I4) the sample comprises healthy adult participants (ages 18–22) with results reported for the healthy groups; (I5) the paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (whole-brain GLM analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds and reported clusters/tables for CC and CD contrasts) clearly identified as coming from the healthy sample; (I6) whole-brain results are described in the text and figures/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study tests social working memory (a social-related task) in healthy adult participants (N=25, mean age 21.56). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (conjunction analyses and SWM vs CWM contrasts), with tables of clusters and MNI coordinates and figures described in the text. The sample is healthy adults and results are reported for that group. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections, so the provided full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion E2 met: the study reports fMRI analyses constrained to a priori ROIs (5 mm spheres) with FWE correction performed within those ROIs. The reported neural results are from ROI-limited regression analyses and do not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy sample. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI of social processing — physician–patient interaction, empathy/compassion-related constructs) and I4 (healthy adult sample, physicians aged 25–37, N=18). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical map clearly reported for the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult males (ages 18-40) using task-based social cognition paradigms (empathy, ToM, self-reference) with whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses reported (ANOVA contrasts, main effects, interactions). The full text includes methods, participants, scanning, and results with whole-brain contrasts and coordinate tables/figures. Inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2-E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=25; mean age 24) that explicitly manipulated participants' interpretive attitude to LEGO artifacts to elicit social-cognitive processing (meaning-rating task) versus physical processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (e.g., meaning > physical; own > other; interaction effects) analyzed with SPM8 and thresholded with FDR/FWE corrections; results are presented as tables of peak coordinates and figures. The task probes social-related constructs (social meaning, relatedness, self/other distinctions). Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social perception task (passive viewing of facial emotions), meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=27) reported separately from clinical groups, meeting I4. The paper presents whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses (within-group and between-group whole-brain contrasts) and explicitly references within-group activations for controls and provides supplementary within-group results, meeting I5 and I6. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion as an fMRI investigation of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study used task-based fMRI during a social decision-making task (charitable donations) and reports group-level univariate whole-brain activation results. Participants were healthy adults (N=22 females, age 19–38). The paper provides whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., VMPFC correlation with donation value, p < 0.05 corrected) and reports results in the main text with supplemental tables/figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, healthy adult sample, univariate whole-brain task activations reported).

This peer-reviewed fMRI study investigates perception and understanding of others’ actions (social perception) using task-based fMRI (weight-judgement and action-observation tasks). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., ActionOBS–CtrlOBS) for healthy adult participants across multiple experiments (Experiments 1–4), with thresholded statistical maps and cerebellar and whole-brain results described in the text and figures. The sample includes healthy adult groups (N across experiments; healthy-group results are reported separately from the patient SCA6 group). The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from healthy group), and I6 (maps/results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, not developmental/geriatric-only, and includes univariate task contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (modified Cyberball inducing social exclusion and evaluative stress). Sample: 40 healthy adult participants (mean age 27.8), with exclusions for neurological/psychiatric illness; healthy-group results are reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses with voxelwise FWE-corrected thresholds and extensive tables of MNI coordinates for multiple univariate contrasts (e.g., EX>IN, PG EX>FG EX, conjunctions). Whole-brain results are clearly labeled as coming from the healthy sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results (behavioral and whole-brain fMRI), Discussion, and supplementary materials referenced. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, non-adult sample, or MVPA-only) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social processing using an interactive social task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) contrasted with a non-social gamble task, satisfying the review scope. Participants are healthy adults (Experiment 1: n=20 females, mean age ~20.8; Experiment 2: n=30 adults, mean age ~21.2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked contrasts (PD vs. Gamble; in-group vs. out-group contrasts) with thresholded statistical maps and tables of activations and coordinates. Whole-brain analyses for the healthy/control sample are clearly described. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social inference (Why/How) (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (trauma-exposed veterans without PTSD) with results reported separately in ROI and post hoc tests (I4). However, the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The whole-brain results presented are interaction and between-group effects (Group × Stimulus) and post hoc group-difference tests, not an accompanying univariate, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criterion met: E4.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social-related processing: participants regulated emotional reactivity to idiographic negative self-beliefs embedded in autobiographical social situations (perception/understanding of self in social context). Sample consists of healthy adults (n=35; ages 21–55), satisfying adult healthy-group requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (react vs neutral; reappraise vs react; acceptance vs react; reappraise vs acceptance) with cluster-correction and presents tables/figures of whole-brain results; amygdala ROI analyses are additionally reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-adult sample, not multivariate-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study uses a social task (Cyberball) in adults (I3 met). However, the sample includes 9 participants meeting criteria for social anxiety disorder as well as 37 without Axis I disorders. The paper reports group-level whole-brain activation maps for the entire combined sample and regression analyses across the continuous BFNE score, but it does not present a separate, clearly-identified whole-brain group-level task activation map for a healthy/control-only group. Because the study includes a clinical subgroup but does not report healthy-group results separately, it fails to meet I4. Similarly, although whole-brain maps are reported, they are not clearly identified as coming from a healthy/control group, so I5 is not satisfied. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. No formal exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are directly triggered, so exclusion is based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age ~25.9) that manipulates social-related constructs (self-involvement, social interaction) using virtual characters and reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (SPM2 random-effects analyses) with stereotactic coordinates and figures/tables of activations. The methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample).

This is an fMRI study using a social-cognition (Theory of Mind) task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes) in a sample of healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age 26.4). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise univariate task contrasts for the placebo (healthy) condition (ToM > gender) and reports exploratory whole-brain analyses (P < 0.001 uncorrected) with tables and coordinates; it therefore provides whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked activation maps. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text, and no exclusion criteria apply. Thus it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This study reports task-based fMRI of a social cognitive task (False-Belief Localizer) relevant to theory-of-mind (social perception/understanding), satisfying I3. It includes healthy adult samples: a large MIT reference group (n=462, ages 18–69) and a Caltech reference group (n=18), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked contrasts (Belief > Photo) for the healthy/control groups (including an unthresholded MIT group map and whole-brain analyses/tables/figures), satisfying I5 and the acceptable reporting formats in I6. The full-text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain univariate results are present; not limited to ROI/ connectivity/ multivariate-only or non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (Cyberball) in healthy adults (n=21; ages 20–37), using a randomized placebo-controlled within-subject design. The paper reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain univariate contrasts (e.g., not receiving ESE > receiving INCL) for the placebo condition and Pla vs Psi comparisons, with whole-brain tables (Tables S3/S4) and figures describing healthy-group effects. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI during a social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps from the healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs, are not only connectivity/resting-state analyses, include within-healthy-group whole-brain effects, and are empirical. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self-reference and social attribution tasks). Sample comprises healthy adults (n=17 analyzed; mean age 21.5), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and peak coordinates for multiple contrasts (Self vs Letter, Mother vs Letter, Self vs Mother, Friends vs Bumper Cars), with statistical thresholds and tables of Talairach coordinates. Whole-brain results are presented in figures and tables (satisfies acceptable reporting formats). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not developmental-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This task-fMRI study examines social cognition and includes a healthy (typically developing) adult control group (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper reports ROI-to-ROI and seed-to-voxel (seed-based) functional connectivity results and does not present any univariate, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (e.g., main-effect or within-group activation contrast) for the healthy/control group. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only seed-based connectivity reported without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy group). Full text appears complete. Excluded on that basis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a dynamic social gestures task (social vs nonsocial intent) that probes social communication/interaction. The sample comprises healthy young adults (N=20; mean age 21.4, range 16.9–25.7) reported separately and analyzed as a healthy group; a slight inclusion of an age <18 does not exclude the adult sample per review rules. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FLAME, cluster correction, and coordinates in Table 1) and presents whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates for contrasts involving social processing and personality covariates. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of facial emotion processing (social communication/perception of others) in healthy adult participants (N=29, ages 20–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation results (FWE-corrected maps and direct contrasts) for explicit and implicit emotion tasks, with tables/figures and SPM random-effects analyses. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI tasks in healthy adults and provides univariate whole-brain group activation maps (reported in text, tables, and figures). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study using a social cognition (Frith–Happé animation; ToM) task (I3). The sample includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group (NT adults aged 19–56) with group-level results reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain one-sample t-tests and whole-brain analyses (including NT group effects and contrasts), with whole-brain results described in the text and supplementary materials (I5, I6). The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper does not report only ROI or connectivity or multivariate-only results, nor is it non-empirical or outside adulthood. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study using a deception task (socially relevant: deception/manipulation) in healthy adult participants (male, ages 19–60). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (lie > truth and truth > lie) analyzed with SPM and thresholded maps (P<0.001 uncorrected with small-volume corrections and tables/figures of activated coordinates). Results are presented for the healthy sample (no separate patient-only reporting), and whole-brain univariate activation contrasts are provided in text/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full article is available. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the review.

Full text incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Abstract describes simultaneous fMRI during a social interaction (a deception game), so I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task) appears to be met. However, the sample characteristics (ages, whether participants are healthy adults) are not specified in the abstract, so I4 cannot be confirmed. The paper as provided does not report or show that a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for a healthy/control group is available, so I5 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E7) can be positively identified from the abstract alone. Because the full article (methods, results, group-level maps) is not available, inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not verifiable; therefore I exclude pending retrieval of the full text for re-screening.

This is an original fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults: includes social-cognition tasks (false belief, animacy/intentional triangles, eyes intention, trustworthiness, vocalizations) and reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and maps. Sample: 78 healthy adults (age 18–40), satisfying adult-sample requirement. Whole-brain voxelwise RFX results (p<0.05 FWE corrected), peak tables, figures, and supplementary maps are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (ages 18–29) involving social interaction and joint attention tasks, satisfying the review topic. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Live > Recorded; Joint Attention > Solo Attention) are reported and corrected for multiple comparisons, with coordinates and figures/tables provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (results presented as tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, nor non-empirical; includes univariate whole-brain activation maps). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this fMRI study uses a social-related threat-reactivity task (faces) and includes a healthy control group reported separately, the paper only reports region-of-interest (amygdala) analyses rather than any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation maps for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence inclusion requirement.

This is an fMRI study using a social judgment task (social acceptance/rejection), includes a healthy adult control group (20 females, mean age ~28), and reports within-group, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for the control group (acceptance>control, rejection>control) with cluster-corrected voxelwise analyses. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results (within-group activations for controls), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This study uses task-based fMRI probing social/attachment processes (baby-cry task) and includes a healthy adult control group, so it meets I3 and I4. However, all reported activation results are presented after small-volume correction within a priori ROIs (extended amygdala, NAc, dmPFC) rather than as unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps for the healthy/control group. The paper reports group comparisons and ROI-corrected clusters; it does not provide an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group activation map or whole-brain voxelwise results. Therefore it violates the review requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group voxelwise map), I6 (not applicable because no whole-brain result to be presented in any format). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (final N=13, ages 19–25) using a social task probing interpersonal synchrony and affiliation (a social/affective construct). The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (factorial ANOVA and synchrony vs. asynchrony contrasts) with cluster correction and reports specific brain regions (e.g., IPL, parahippocampal gyrus/amygdala, vmPFC/ACC). Voxelwise BOLD:behavior correlations and clusterwise results are described. Thus the study uses fMRI during a social-related task (I3), includes a healthy adult sample (I4), and reports whole-brain group-level task activation maps/contrasts (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study used task-based fMRI to investigate animacy perception from visual motion cues, which maps onto social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). Participants were healthy adults (ages reported 19–36) and group-level analyses were performed. The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise results (e.g., FWE-corrected maps and MNI coordinates; figures and tables of coordinates are described), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-emotional face processing (emotion discrimination), satisfying the review objective. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (two nonclinical groups: high and low social anhedonia) with screening to exclude Axis I disorders. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level activation analyses (one-sample t-tests across participants for EE vs baseline and EE vs EI, and group×condition flexible factorial analyses), with results presented in tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This paper reports a task-based fMRI study using Theory-of-Mind (social) animated stimuli (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=20, ages 22–56) with results reported separately (meets I4). The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked contrasts (within-group ToM > random-motion) for the healthy control group with corrected activations described in text, tables, and figures (meets I5 and I6). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or multivariate-only maps) are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This empirical fMRI study used a well-established social (Theory of Mind) task (moving-triangles animations) and acquired task-evoked BOLD data (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants with reported ages 24–64 (mean 45.6), meeting the adult 18–65 criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (ToM > R, ToM > Baseline, R > Baseline) with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds and tables/figures (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not an age-limited non-adult sample, and it is primary empirical work. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using the Cyberball social exclusion task (a social-processing paradigm) in a sample of healthy adult university students (final N=42, l/l and s/s groups). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (exclusion vs inclusion) across all participants and genotype groups with FWE-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of activation peaks (e.g., Tables 3–4, Figures 1–3). Whole-brain analyses and coordinate tables are clearly described in the text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (face encoding/ social cognition) and includes a separate typically-developing control group of (mostly) adult participants whose within-group whole-brain, voxelwise task activation (Dm effect for remembered vs. forgotten faces) is reported (tables/figures and text). Whole-brain group-level contrasts for the healthy/control group are provided (Table 2, figures), satisfying the requirement for unmasked, group-level healthy-task effects. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps/coordinates for the control group), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI experiment that directly examines social interaction and mentalizing (social-related processing), meeting the review objective. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=29, ages 18–27) are reported and analyzed separately. Whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts are reported (e.g., Live Story > Social Story; thresholded at p<.001 and cluster-corrected; figures and Supplementary Table 2 show group maps), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results. Results are presented for the healthy/control group (not limited to a subgroup). The paper includes complete core sections (methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social-emotional processing (schadenfreude and fremdscham) using a task where participants observed social-integrity threats and rated their affect. Sample: N=34 healthy adults (ages 19–31 and 22–29), reported separately by group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (SIT > NEUT) with FWE-corrected results and coordinates/tables/figures, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results for the healthy/control groups are clearly described. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI, only-connectivity, only-between-group without healthy-group map, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

The provided content appears to be an abstract rather than a complete full text. While the study clearly uses task-based fMRI of social-cognitive processes in "normal subjects" and reports group-level brain activations (left IFG, caudate, cingulate, etc.), key details are missing: participant ages/sample characteristics (cannot confirm adults 18–65), full methods, and explicit presentation of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables in the body of the paper. Therefore I cannot verify inclusion criterion I4 (sample ages) and fully confirm I5/I6 from a complete methods/results section. Because the full text is incomplete, inclusion cannot be confirmed.

This is an empirical fMRI study of prosocial/social learning in healthy adults (n=31 males, ages 19–32). The task is explicitly social (learning to obtain rewards for self, another person, or no one) and uses fMRI with group-level second-level analyses. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level contrasts and parametric maps (flexible-factorial second-level, reported main effects and contrasts; tables and figures/coordinates provided; SPM whole-brain framework and statements that main effects are reported at P<0.05 FWE across the whole brain or SVC-FWE for ROIs). Sample falls within 18–65. Whole-brain results are clearly described and reported (including coordinate tables and figures). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, SI referenced). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an fMRI study of emotion evaluation from voice and music—an instance of social-related processing (perception/understanding of others’ emotional states), meeting I3. Sample consists of healthy adults (N=16, ages 18–26), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., emotion task vs pitch task; voice vs rest; music vs rest) with cluster-level correction and presents tables/figures of results, satisfying I5 and I6. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, not developmental/geriatric-only, not multivariate-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It used task-based fMRI during a social-related task (a simulated peer-evaluation paradigm) addressing social self-conscious emotion and anticipatory evaluation (I3). The sample includes healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range (ages up to 22.9), satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and cluster-corrected results (e.g., MPFC activation related to age predictors; whole-brain corrected PPI results for MPFC–caudate coupling), clearly described as arising from the healthy participant sample (I5). Whole-brain results are reported in the text and figures and meet acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without task activations, not between-group-only contrasts, sample includes adults, and it is empirical). The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The article reports an event-related BOLD fMRI task probing social perception (affiliation, isolation, nonsocial) with pleasantness judgments, satisfying I3. The sample includes a younger adult group (N=16, mean age ~20.8), meeting the healthy adult sample requirement I4. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses (random-effects t-tests, conjunctions) with tables of peak coordinates, thresholds, and figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures, references) is present and sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria from E2–E7 apply.

The provided "full text" is incomplete: it contains only privacy/cookie text and metadata (title, authors, journal, DOI) but lacks the article’s introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore I cannot verify that the study used an fMRI social task (I3), included a healthy adult sample reported separately (I4), or reported whole-brain, group-level task activation results (I5/I6). Because core content is missing, inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed. Exclusion is based on incomplete full text preventing assessment of all inclusion criteria.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (meets I3) and reports whole-brain task results across the sample. However, it does not include a separately reported healthy adult group: the sample (ages 18–21) contains participants with current Major Depressive Disorder and anxiety, and all reported whole-brain maps and regressions are from the mixed clinical/non-clinical sample rather than an explicitly defined healthy/control group. Therefore it fails I4 (no separately reported healthy adult group results) and I5 (no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map clearly identified as coming from a healthy/control group). Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met; inclusion criterion I3 is met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interactive task (competitive reaction time/Taylor paradigm) that elicits reactive aggression and observation of another’s suffering, addressing social processing. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=16 males, mean age 28.6; two excluded for disbelief) meeting the adult healthy-group requirement. Imaging: reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2), voxelwise thresholds, coordinates, tables and figures (conjunctions, parametric modulation), and ROI/small-volume tests are additional but not exclusive. Whole-brain univariate task-evoked activation contrasts for the healthy group are clearly reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: n=13, mean age ~26.6; Experiment 2: n=18, mean age ~23.1) that tests perception/processing of vocal (socially relevant) versus non-vocal sounds — a social-communication/perception task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation contrasts (vocal > non-vocal and related maps), thresholded and reported with peak coordinates and figures. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only/resting-only, no between-group-only contrasts, sample is adult, and univariate whole-brain task contrasts are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study meets inclusion criteria I3 (task-based fMRI of social cognition) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). However, the provided full text does not clearly present at least one unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map that is explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. While the paper reports main task effects (across participants) and group-by-condition interactions and refers to ‘separately for the groups’ results in supplementary materials, no explicit whole-brain healthy-group activation map or contrast is shown in the available full text. Therefore this paper effectively reports between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task effect, meeting exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E4.

This is an fMRI study of social perception in healthy adults (N=20) that meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task: social-comparative judgments of close vs. non-close others) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately). However, all reported group-level statistical results were analyzed and corrected within a set of a priori ROIs (the manuscript states group SPM{t} maps were FWE-corrected within ROIs and the caudate result was derived from a caudate ROI). The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map or whole-brain-corrected results; therefore it reports only ROI-based group results. This meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked map) is not met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded.

Full text appears incomplete: only title, authors, journal, DOI and web navigation metadata provided; core article content (methods, participants, results) is missing. Cannot confirm key inclusion criteria: I3 (use of fMRI during a social-related task) not verifiable; I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately) not verifiable; I5 (whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map in healthy group) not verifiable; I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/supplement) not verifiable.
