Please provide the complete article text (methods and results) to reassess.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E2 and E4. The paper reports task fMRI in a social cognition (Theory of Mind) paradigm and includes a healthy control group, but the imaging results are presented primarily as ROI-restricted, small-volume-corrected analyses and as between-group contrasts (ALS > HC); no unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group is reported. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — Theory of Mind) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain, group-level healthy/control task-evoked statistical map). Because the study lacks an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group activation map and reports results via ROI-restricted and between-group contrasts only, it fails the meta-analysis requirement and must be excluded.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=14 analysed; ages 18–30) that explicitly probes social cognition (trustworthiness judgments of faces). The paper reports group-level, random-effects SPM analyses and whole-brain contrasts (main effects and parametric contrasts), with tables and figures of activation coordinates and small-volume corrections, clearly identifying healthy-group task-evoked activation maps. Full article text including Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of social cognition (affective theory of mind) in healthy adult participants (22 recruited, 21 analyzed; mean age 23.7), meeting the sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (EFE > no EFE and related whole-brain analyses reported in tables/figures and described in the text), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement; coordinate tables and figures are provided. The task is clearly social-related (affective ToM). It is not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and not a non-empirical paper. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathy/attachment (imagining self, loved-one, stranger in pain), directly addressing social-related processing (affiliation/attachment and perception of others). Sample: 36 healthy adult participants (mean age 23) reported separately. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (Pain>Neutral and perspective contrasts) with voxelwise FDR correction, tables of coordinates, figures, and ROI/PPI secondary analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social stimulus processing that includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met). However, the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The only whole-brain results described in the full text are exploratory between-group contrasts (healthy>manic and manic>healthy) reported uncorrected (Supplementary Table 1). Healthy-group results are reported via ROI analyses rather than a whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task map. Therefore inclusion criteria I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task map) and I6 (acceptable whole-brain reporting for the healthy group) are not satisfied. This falls under exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group whole-brain contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Hence excluded.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (biological motion) but the reported whole-brain fMRI results are for a single patient only. Healthy participants are included behaviorally, but the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for a healthy/control group; comparisons to healthy fMRI data reference prior work rather than presenting new healthy-group maps. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for a healthy adult whole-brain fMRI activation map.

This study reports task-based fMRI during an explicit social judgment (approachability) task (meets I3). A healthy adult control group (age-matched adults) was recruited and reported separately alongside clinical groups (meets I4). The paper describes voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts (social > gender, social > baseline) analyzed in SPM8 with cluster- and voxel-level FWE correction, and reports within-group analyses and contrasts (within-group results and supplementary tables/figures are referenced), indicating whole-brain healthy/control group activation maps are available (meets I5). Results and whole-brain findings are reported in main text and supplementary material (meets I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary material is referenced (acceptable).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (university students aged ~19–24) that investigates perception of others’ emotions (social communication/perception), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA and simple effects contrasts) with thresholding (PFWE<0.05) and tables/figures of activated regions (univariate results). The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, sample is adult, and univariate whole-brain maps are reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (empathy/theory-of-mind) that used a social-related task (viewing emotional vs. neutral social scenes; two vs. one person). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=16 analyzed; mean age 27.8). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM, ANOVA) with statistical maps thresholded (FDR q<0.05), figures and coordinates (Table 1), and ROI follow-ups. Thus it meets the review’s fMRI, healthy-adult, and whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making in healthy adults. Neuroimaging was acquired (simultaneous fMRI hyperscanning) and analyzed with voxelwise GLMs and random-effects group analyses; whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and cluster results are reported (with multiple-comparison correction) and made available on NeuroVault. The neuroimaging cohort consists of healthy adult participants (neuroimaging subset n=62; ages 18–53). The task explicitly manipulates social information and assesses social influence, matching the review’s domain. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition/preprocessing, GLM), Results, and Discussion; supplemental maps/coordinates are referenced. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of impression formation/updating (a social cognition task), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=24, ages 18–45). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and interaction analyses (e.g., L2>F3, interaction of trial number × consistency) with thresholding and cluster information, figures, and supplementary tables/coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study uses task-based fMRI during a social cognition/mentalizing task (participants judged scenarios evoking 60 mental states), includes a healthy adult sample (N=20; ages 18–27), and reports group-level whole-brain results. Although the paper emphasizes multivariate (MVPA/RSA) analyses and searchlight maps, it also reports univariate whole-brain analyses (ANOVA for voxel selection; parallel univariate whole-brain mapping and voxelwise t tests) and provides corrected group-level statistical maps and tables. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, not MVPA-only without univariate maps, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses fMRI with an emotional face (social) go/no-go task and reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps for the neurotypical/control group, but it does not provide a healthy adult (age 18–65) group analyzed and reported separately. The control sample age range is 12–23 (mixed adolescents and young adults) and results are presented for the combined control group rather than an adult-only subgroup. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (fMRI social-related task), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps for control group), I6 (results presented in text/tables/figures). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (healthy adult-only group 18–65 not provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Consequently, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This paper reports an fMRI task probing social-related processing (self- and other-evaluation of personality traits), satisfying I3. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (13 controls) reported separately from the schizophrenia patients, satisfying I4. The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked activation contrasts for the healthy/control group (e.g., SELF vs lexical baseline, OTHER vs baseline, conjunction, SELF vs OTHER) with voxelwise results described in the text, tables of coordinates, figures and Monte Carlo cluster correction, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs, connectivity, between-group contrasts only, multivariate-only maps, nor is this a non-empirical paper. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (evaluation/organization of political beliefs; self/other processing) using a task that engages social cognition. Sample comprises healthy adults (n=26, ages 22–45). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise univariate analyses (second-level random-effects SPM results, thresholding and coordinate tables/figures provided). Reporting includes coordinates and descriptions of whole-brain effects and ROI-corrected results. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self-reference vs other-reference) in healthy adults. It reports task-based whole-brain, group-level GLM results (second-level analyses with FWE-corrected thresholds and reported contrasts such as self>other and other>self; figures and supplementary tables are provided). Sample: 110 healthy adults age 19–31. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using social/interactive stimuli (traffic-campaign videos) that probe socio-cognitive processes (mentalizing/empathy). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (male drivers aged ~19–30) reported separately as groups. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (CV vs NV) and displays whole-brain results (Fig.1) and discusses within-group effects, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=36, ages ~24–25) who viewed social interaction stimuli (affective vs cooperative), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxelwise contrasts, cluster-corrected results, tables and figures are reported) fulfilling I5 and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I6). The manuscript includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and also reports behavioral and imaging results alongside DCM connectivity analyses; no exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-cognition (social attribution/mentalizing) paradigm (DISC) directly addressing social-related processing. Sample: 22 healthy adults age 18–25 (healthy adult group reported separately). Whole-brain, group-level univariate contrasts are reported and described (FRIENDS > WATCH; FRIENDS > SIZE) with thresholding, permutation testing, and family-wise error correction; results are reported in the text and figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The paper is empirical and includes full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

All inclusion criteria are satisfied: (I3) The study used task-based fMRI (dual/dual‑fMRI hyperscanning) during an interactive social task (pattern game) probing cooperation/competition; (I4) Sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=44, mean age 22.37 years); (I5) The paper reports group‑level, whole‑brain, random‑effects voxelwise analyses (FLAME) with nonparametric permutation correction and presents thresholded t‑maps and cluster tables; (I6) Whole‑brain results are provided in figures and tables and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI‑only, not connectivity‑only, not limited to between‑group contrasts, not multivariate‑only, and the study is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). Therefore the study meets the meta‑analysis inclusion standards for whole‑brain task‑evoked fMRI in healthy adults addressing social processing.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based fMRI to probe social perception/animacy (construct fits I3). The sample is healthy adults (28 naturally-cycling women aged ~22–24), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., FRIENDS+SIZE>WATCH, FRIENDS>SIZE) with family-wise error correction and TFCE, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, multivariate-only, pediatric/geriatric-only, or non-empirical study).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants viewed dynamic and static emotional facial expressions (social communication/perception of others). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=13; ages in range) with results reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps for the control group (simple main effect of dynamic vs. static), with corrected voxelwise results and figures/tables showing control-group activations. Full article text (background, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Exclusion rationale: This study uses fMRI during a social joint-attention task in healthy adult dyads (I3 met) and reports healthy adult samples (I4 met). However, the paper’s neuroimaging results are based on group ICA components and cross-brain coupling (multivariate component maps and connectivity analyses) rather than reporting any univariate, voxelwise group-level task activation contrast for the healthy group. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E3 (reports connectivity/ICA without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E6 (the only whole-brain maps are multivariate/ICA component maps without a univariate task-evoked contrast). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no univariate, voxelwise healthy-group task activation map reported). Full text appears complete. Consequently, the study should be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cooperation (Prisoner’s Dilemma), addressing social processing. Sample: healthy adult participants (female, mean age 21), with group-level results reported for the healthy sample. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task contrasts (CC vs. other outcomes; gain vs. loss; context×cooperation interaction) with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates in tables. ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain maps are present. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports an fMRI experiment probing social cognition (empathic concern) using naturalistic empathy-evoking film clips with contextual and musical manipulations (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=26, ages ~30) with results reported for the healthy group (meets I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise univariate contrasts and ANOVA results (Tables and figures with cluster-level FWE correction) clearly identified as healthy-group task effects (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered: whole-brain univariate activation maps/contrasts are provided (not ROI-only or only connectivity/resting-state), and the sample is within adulthood. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during social-related processing (self/other reflection), includes a healthy adult sample (N=22; mean age 37.4), and reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked activation maps (surface-based cortical maps and cluster-wise results for the SR>AL contrast) clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only analyses, and not between-group-only contrasts. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test) in healthy adults (16 women, mean age 20.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (emotion vs control) with cluster-forming thresholds and FWE-corrected results, and provides peak coordinates and tables for these univariate activation maps, as well as PPI connectivity analyses. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without whole-brain task maps, non-adult sample, multivariate-only maps, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=28, ages 30–50) that explicitly manipulates social stimulus processing and self-referential processing during an fMRI task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (main effects, conjunctions, direct contrasts, interaction effects) with cluster thresholds and voxel coordinates, and presents results in text/tables/figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures and described in the text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social perception (cooperation vs noncooperation) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=19) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for the healthy controls (e.g., C+ > C–, FDR-corrected whole-brain results reported and discussed). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation maps for healthy group), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (approachability judgments from faces) that reports whole-brain, group-level univariate activation results for the healthy control group (coordinates, cluster-corrected p-values, and figures). The study includes a healthy adult control sample (n=24) and reports control-group activation maps (approachability > gender). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not MVPA-only, not non-empirical, and includes adults). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

The study reports an fMRI investigation of social processing (trustworthiness judgments), includes a healthy adult control group (n=18, mean age 32.2) with results reported separately, and provides whole-brain, group-level within-group activation analyses for the control group (whole-brain contrasts and tables/figures). Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described (Tables and t-maps). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social cognition (mentalising/theory of mind), meeting the review objective. Participants are healthy adults (Experiment 2: N=17, mean age 22) within the 18–65 range. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked activation contrasts (e.g., mentalising > factual; parametric modulation contrasts) analyzed with SPM2, thresholding and cluster-correction, and provides whole-brain results in tables/figures (Table 1, Figures 4A–C). Thus it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses task fMRI of a social-related process (irony comprehension) and includes a healthy adult control group, but it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group in the full text. The paper primarily reports between-group contrasts (healthy>schizophrenia) and references control-group results as previously published, without presenting a standalone healthy-group whole-brain activation map in the article. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult participants). Inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task map) is not met. Full text appears complete for the purposes of screening.

The article reports an event-related fMRI experiment of moral reasoning (a social-related task) including a clearly reported healthy adult control group (n=28, ages 18–55). The paper presents whole-brain, group-level one-sample activation analyses for the healthy/control group (FWE-corrected results, Table 3 and Figure 2) and describes these results in the text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: incidental fearful face processing) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). However, it does not present any group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group in this paper: the manuscript focuses on region-parcellated multivariate connectivity (3-MDS) and states that activation mapping by mass univariate analysis was ‘previously reported’ elsewhere. Therefore it fails I5 (no whole-brain univariate healthy-group activation map reported) and I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results described here). This triggers exclusion criteria E2 (no whole-brain voxelwise results; ROI/parcellation/connectivity-focused analyses only) and E4 (paper reports between-group connectivity contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social-related processing (recall of self- and other-referential relationship episodes) meeting the review objective. Sample: healthy adult participants (final N=35; psychiatric screening with mini-DIPS; adults recruited from university/community), satisfying the sample inclusion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (self-relevant > control; other > control) with FDR correction and cluster tables/figures clearly from the healthy group. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, not multivariate-only, and is empirical). Therefore include.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social interactive mentalizing paradigm (Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adults (fMRI subsample n=163, ages 19–35). The paper presents whole-brain, group-level univariate activation contrasts (ment > cont) using SPM8 with voxelwise and clusterwise statistics and reports activation maps and coordinates across the healthy sample; results are not limited to ROI-only analyses. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria are met.

Although the study includes healthy adult control participants and uses fMRI during a social-related task (joint attention/social gaze), the fMRI results are reported only via region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with small-volume correction. The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group (no whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group contrast is provided in the main text or supplementary ROI tables). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult group reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group map). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of empathy for pain (a social/other-perception task) using task-based BOLD (pain vs no-pain). Healthy adult participants are included (young group aged 20–30 satisfies the 18–65 requirement). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps/contrasts (e.g., pain>no pain; pain>baseline) with FWE-corrected results and provides statistical maps (figures/tables and NeuroVault link). Analyses are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only approaches. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study of action observation/anticipation (perception and understanding of others), a social-related construct relevant to the review. Participants are healthy adult players (adult competitive levels reported). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise contrasts (e.g., shots–mctrl; FWE-corrected thresholds) and provides coordinates and figures. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I3 (uses task-based fMRI with a social theory-of-mind task – false belief vs false photo), I4 (includes a healthy young adult group, ages 18–33, reported separately), I5 (reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts, including main effect and false belief > false photo whole-brain maps), and I6 (whole-brain results are described and reported in text/tables/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and provides univariate task activation contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis focusing on fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study investigating social processing (minimal group affiliation and emotion perception) in healthy adults. The sample includes healthy adult participants (n=20 analyzed), and the experiment used a social group categorization task (affiliation/social perception). The paper reports group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses (voxelwise thresholds P<0.001 and cluster-level FWE correction P<0.05) with coordinates and reported activations that co-vary with EEG measures (Table 1, whole-brain results described in Methods/Results). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state-only, no patient-only sample, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

The study is an fMRI investigation of face perception (socially relevant processing) in healthy adult participants and reports ROI-based analyses and participant-level ROI localization; however, the provided full text does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or tables/figures of whole-brain univariate activation contrasts for the healthy group. Main reported analyses focus on ROIs (FFA, STS, amygdala) rather than whole-brain results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear group-level whole-brain map). No other exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study uses an interactive Domino fMRI task and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the analyses are based on ICA-derived component spatial maps and component β-weights (temporal sorting) rather than reporting an univariate, voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. The paper reports group comparisons and component maps but does not present an unmasked, voxelwise show>no-show (or equivalent) whole-brain statistical map clearly attributed to the healthy group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group/interaction/component-based results without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (race perception and trustworthiness evaluations), involving a social-related task (perception/evaluation of others). The sample is healthy adults (n=30, ages 18–29). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Black > White) and second-level covariate analyses with reported peak coordinates and cluster tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain univariate results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

While this is an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4), the manuscript does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map. Analyses are described as voxelwise but were explicitly restricted to particular brain regions and combined with ROI analyses; results are primarily ROI-based and masked voxelwise searches. Therefore the study fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5 not met) and falls under exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI/restricted analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (gaze-mediated social stimuli) with healthy adult participants (N=23, ages 21–37). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., main effects and interactions; SPM maps thresholded at cluster-level corrected P<0.05 with cluster-forming threshold Puc<0.001) and provides anatomical localization and tables/figures of activations. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, multivariate-only, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6) and the study should be included in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (hand-holding under threat) conducted in healthy adults (mean age 23.6). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (threat vs safe) identified via cluster-wise, voxelwise analyses and presents ROIs/coordinates (Table 1), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is a within-subject, placebo-controlled fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=20 males, ages 21–37) performing an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma, a social decision-making task. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task-evoked activation contrasts (e.g., main effects and treatment×opponent interactions) with cluster-level FWE correction and lists activations in tables/figures. All required content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI during a social task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task maps reported), and I6 (results described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of pragmatic (socially relevant) language processing that explicitly examines integration of speaker characteristics (voice-inferred age/gender/social background) with sentence content — a social-communication task (meets I3). The sample includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (N=24, ages 18–39) reported separately from the ASD group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and presents within-group whole-brain contrasts for the control group (e.g., speaker-congruent > speaker-incongruent results in vMPFC/ACC; tables and figures provided), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-only (E3), not limited to between-group contrasts without a healthy-group map (E4), sample is adult (E5), not exclusively multivariate maps (E6), and this is original empirical data (E7). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using an interactive social task (iterative Prisoner’s Dilemma) that probes mentalizing/social cognition, satisfying I3. The sample comprises 164 healthy adult participants (age range 19–35), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (game task vs control) analyzed with SPM8, voxelwise thresholding and cluster correction, and provides activation coordinates and cluster descriptions, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the report appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult, multivariate-only, or non-empirical study. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social communication (speech act understanding) in healthy adults. Sample: 18 healthy right-handed native English adults (age 18–41). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., “Request > Naming”) with FDR-corrected results and tables/coordinates and ROI SVC analyses. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This peer-reviewed fMRI study used a task probing conceptualization of actions at different levels of abstraction, explicitly engaging mentalizing/theory-of-mind processes (why questions) and action representation (how questions), i.e., social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). Participants were healthy adults (N=17; mean age 29.5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (cluster-forming threshold P<0.001 with cluster-level FWE correction) and tables/figures of whole-brain results; data/images are also available on NeuroVault. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses fMRI during a social-related task (biological motion perception) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately, but the imaging results are reported primarily as individual- and ROI-based analyses. STSp and MT were functionally localized per subject and event-related analyses were conducted within those ROIs; the paper does not present an unambiguous group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group (only individual localizers, ROI peak values, and a limited whole-brain search described for patients). Therefore it fails the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: the task contrasts personal (improvised) prayer — which the authors interpret and test as social-cognitive/theory-of-mind processing — against controls. The sample is healthy adults (n=20, ages 21–32). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked contrasts (whole-brain analyses, FDR-corrected, with coordinate tables for main effects, interactions, and individual condition contrasts), satisfying reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only results, non-adult sample, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of Theory of Mind (social cognition) in healthy adults (n=19, ages 20–53). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., SocAdj > PhyConf; Soc > Phy; Adj > Conf) analyzed with SPM8 and thresholding with cluster correction, and provides coordinates/tables of significant peaks. The task is explicitly social and probes mentalizing/contextual integration. The full text includes introduction, methods, results (behavioral and whole-brain fMRI), and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social attribution task (People vs Bumper) that probes theory-of-mind/social processing, includes a healthy adult control group (n=17) with results reported separately, and provides whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps/contrasts for the control group (figures and tables of coordinates). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are met.

The paper reports an fMRI study of social perception (passive viewing of biological vs scrambled point-light displays), includes a healthy adult sample (48 adults, ages 20–35) reported separately, and provides group-level, whole-brain univariate task activation results (biological > scrambled) with cluster-corrected maps/tables and further PPI analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI during social/affiliation-related processing (implicit attitudes toward monogamy/adultery and response inhibition to attractive cues), uses a healthy adult sample (27 heterosexual males, ages 20–32), and reports group-level whole-brain univariate task contrasts (IAT incongruent vs. congruent) with cluster-level FWE correction and peak coordinates. Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in the text. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample) apply. Therefore the paper satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

Exclusion E4 applies: the paper reports group comparisons (patients vs. controls) and statistical maps of between-group differences, but does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met: (I3) the task is an fMRI social-related face-processing task; (I4) a healthy adult control group (N=21, age-matched adults 18–65) is included and reported separately. Inclusion I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task map) is NOT met because no healthy-group univariate whole-brain task activation map or within-group contrast for controls is reported in the full text (only between-group contrasts are reported). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

This fMRI study examines perception/understanding of others’ actions (force estimation during action observation), which is a social-related construct. Participants: healthy adults (final N=12, mean age 26) satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM12 GLM, one-sample t-tests, conjunctions) with coordinates/figures and SUIT cerebellar analyses; results for the healthy group are clearly described. Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article is a narrative review/synthesis that summarizes and adapts results from multiple empirical fMRI studies (including the authors' prior work) rather than reporting an original, new fMRI experiment with novel whole-brain group-level results for a healthy adult sample. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for an empirical paper presenting original fMRI data in healthy adults. Exclusion ID met: E7 (non-empirical/review without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria: none of the required inclusion criteria for the present meta-analysis are satisfied by this article itself — I3 (the paper itself does not present a new fMRI task dataset), I4 (does not report an original healthy adult sample group as a primary empirical cohort), and I5 (no original whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps from a healthy/control group are reported as novel data). Full text appears complete and is a review-style article, so exclusion is appropriate.

This study used task-based fMRI with a social-related paradigm (dynamic fearful faces) and reports group-level univariate whole-brain activation contrasts. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=19, mean age 31.8) reported separately and uses second-level one-sample t-tests and group comparisons (face>place) with voxelwise and clusterwise correction (p<0.05 FWE). Whole-brain group maps and coordinate tables (Fig. 1, Table S1; and group comparisons reported in Table 2) are presented for controls and for control vs TLE contrasts. The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked map for controls), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts without healthy-group map, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion provided).

The study meets I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task: cyberball social interaction and face perception probing learned social roles) and I4 (healthy adult sample, N=15, ages ~24). However, it does not report any group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for the healthy group that survive correction or are provided as coordinates/figures; the only significant whole-brain results reported are from a multivariate searchlight (MVPA) correlation analysis. According to the review’s benchmarks, studies whose only whole-brain healthy-group result is multivariate (searchlight/MVPA/classification) must be excluded (E6). The authors explicitly state that univariate SPM group analyses did not reveal significant voxels surviving correction. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain univariate task-evoked map) is not met, triggering exclusion under E6.

This paper reports an fMRI task-based study of emotion regulation in response to angry faces (socially relevant stimuli), with a healthy adult sample (N=60, age range 18–57) and separate resting-state subset (N=48). The manuscript includes multiple group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., Observe-angry > Observe-neutral; Decrease vs Observe-angry; Increase + Decrease vs Observe-angry) with tables/figures and cluster-level FWE correction, clearly reported for the healthy group. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting analyses, not between-group only, not non-adult sample, nor multivariate-only). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/collaborative learning in healthy adults. It uses task-based fMRI during a communicative/collaborative referential task (social cognition/mentalizing), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample: healthy adult participants (ages 18–33) are reported. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation contrasts (cluster-corrected results, tables/figures and coordinates) and also provides ROI analyses; whole-brain univariate maps/contrasts for the healthy group are clearly described. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply.

Although this is an fMRI study of social decision-making in healthy adult participants (I3 and I4 satisfied), the paper does not report a conventional univariate, group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation contrast. The whole-brain results provided derive from multivariate classification (SVM/RVM) weight/discriminating-volume maps and permutation-based significance of classifier weights. According to the review's Exclusion E6, studies whose only whole-brain healthy-group result is a multivariate/classification map (without also reporting a univariate voxelwise task activation map) must be excluded. Therefore the paper fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (a group-level, whole-brain univariate task map) and is excluded on the basis of E6.

This fMRI study examines neural responses while healthy adult participants (age 18–24) listened to musical stimuli and rated beauty, and interprets activations in social-cognition/ToM and empathy-related regions (arMFC, PCC/PC, TPJ/temporal pole, hippocampus) as reflecting cognitive empathy and social cognition. Thus it addresses social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others / social cognition). The sample is a healthy adult group (N=18, ages 18–24) meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain contrasts and ANOVA results, with voxel thresholds and cluster-level FDR correction, coordinates, and ROI follow-ups (i.e., univariate whole-brain task-evoked maps are provided). Reporting in tables/figures/coordinates satisfies acceptable whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI during social cognition paradigms (emotion processing and theory-of-mind), includes a healthy adult control group (N=14, ages 28–30) with results reported separately, and provides group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) univariate contrasts (EMOTION–GENDER) for the healthy group with statistical thresholding and figures/tables describing activations. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not exclusively between-group contrasts, not non-adult, and is empirical).

This study reports an fMRI task probing empathy (a social cognition task; Perception/Understanding of Others), includes a healthy adult control group (n=14; ages 22–47), and presents group-level, whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy/control group (one-sample t-test, thresholding, tables/figures). Whole-brain results are reported in the text/tables/figures (acceptable formats). Full article contains methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-adult sample, and reports univariate whole-brain activations).

This fMRI study measured brain activity while healthy adult participants (age 18–27) listened to literary stories and explicitly modeled Mentalizing (theory-of-mind) and Action content. The task probes social cognition (perception/understanding of others), satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (Mentalizing > Action and Action > Mentalizing) with cluster-level correction and displays activation maps and coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and does not fall under any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, not non-empirical, adult sample). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (observation of social vs. individual actions with gaze manipulation) in healthy adult volunteers (N=17, mean age 26). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (second-level SPM ANOVA) and presents voxelwise results including activation maps and coordinate tables for main effects and interactions (dMPFC, IFG, pSTS, amygdala, etc.). These satisfy the review’s requirements for task-based fMRI in healthy adults and whole-brain univariate results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates facial color processing, a form of social perception/social communication (perception/understanding of others). It tests healthy adult participants (N=25, mean age 25.24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (natural-colored face vs natural-colored scrambled image) to localize face-selective regions and provides coordinates/figures of these whole-brain results. Although ROI analyses are also reported, they are accompanied by univariate, group-level whole-brain results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of real-time social interaction (mutual eye contact), directly addressing social communication/attention (meets I3). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (mean age ~21.8; N analyzed = 30–32 depending on analysis), meeting the adult healthy-sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked contrasts (LIVE > REPLAY) with voxelwise inference and cluster-level FWE correction, tables/figures of activation, and describes whole-brain interbrain synchronization and gPPI results (meets I5). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text and figures/tables (I6). No exclusion criteria apply: the study includes whole-brain univariate activation (not ROI-only), not limited to connectivity-only results, not a between-group-only contrast, not an exclusively non-adult sample, and is empirical. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports only resting-state seed-based functional connectivity without any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps) and E5 (sample comprises only children/adolescents, age range 6.5–18.7, with no healthy adult group). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no task-based fMRI of social-related processing; study uses resting-state fMRI), I4 (no healthy adult participants; sample is male children/adolescents), I5 (no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map for a healthy/control adult group), I6 (not applicable because no whole-brain task results are reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper does not address the review objective of task-evoked social processing in healthy adults and must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study that probes event simulation including social-related processing (explicit situation inference and theory-of-mind–related constructs); ~42.7% of stimuli depicted social situations and analyses tested social vs non-social effects. Sample consists of healthy adults (N=20, mean age 20.65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Imp–Con, Exp–Imp, Ftr–Exp) using SPM8 with cluster correction and provides coordinate tables/activation figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (results presented as coordinates/figures described in text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (joint action with haptic contact) that directly probes social-cognitive processes (leading, following, mutuality, mentalizing, social reward). The sample comprises healthy adults (n=18, mean age 40.4), meeting the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (multiple univariate contrasts, Talairach coordinates, tables and figures) rather than only ROI or connectivity analyses. Results are clearly described for the healthy participant group. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply.

Exclusion E2 met: the reported analyses focus on a priori ROIs with small-volume correction (SVC) and the manuscript does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy adult group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI of social/attachment processing: mothers viewing own vs. unfamiliar child/dog) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 22–45, results reported for that group). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked map) and I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results presented in tables/figures that are unmasked/whole-brain). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI hyperscanning study of live verbal social communication (social communication construct), involving 22 healthy adult participants (11 pairs of adult women, mean age ~27), reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses (second-level voxel-wise t-tests, cluster correction, figures and tables). Whole-brain univariate task-evoked activation maps for talking, listening, and inter-individual coupling are described in the text and supplementary materials. The methods, results, and discussion are present, and the study is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or limited to non-adults. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not trigger any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (17 male students, mean age 23.6) that used a social-related task (viewing affiliation/romantic and power film clips). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (affiliation>control and power>control) with activation clusters and MNI coordinates (table/figures) and describes mixed-effects group analyses. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore the study meets the review criteria for inclusion.

The study meets I3 (uses task-based fMRI with a social perception task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). However, task-related fMRI results are reported via ROI-based analyses (ANOVA on predefined ROIs) rather than a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) univariate task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. Although the paper reports whole-brain resting-state connectivity results, these are not task-evoked maps. Therefore it fails I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task activation map) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI task analyses with no whole-brain task results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criterion met: E2.

The study is EXCLUDED because the sample is wholly adolescent (ages ~12–18) and does not provide a separate healthy adult (age 18–65) group, violating exclusion criterion E5. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I3 (task: fMRI during social-related facial emotion processing), I5 (reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the control group with FWE-corrected results), and I6 (whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no healthy adult participant group reported separately). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=46, ages 18–45) using a task in which participants viewed and rated emotional (including people-containing) IAPS images and performed a person-detection button press. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (HA− > NTR) with cluster-wise inference and a supplementary table/figures identifying activated regions (dmPFC, right amygdala). The task taps emotion perception/processing and involved stimuli containing social content (people) and included dmPFC, a region linked to social cognition. Therefore it meets: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: perception/understanding of self/others via emotional/social images), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrast reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical study reports task-based fMRI during two social-cognitive paradigms (emotional perspective-taking and emotion attribution) in a sample of healthy adult participants (n=129; ages 18–35). The authors performed whole-brain group-level contrasts (emotion perspective-taking > shape matching and emotion attribution > gender matching) using a whole-brain FWE-corrected threshold and then conducted whole-brain regression analyses relating methylation to task-evoked BOLD, reporting voxelwise clusters and coordinates in the text/figures. Thus the paper (i) uses fMRI for social-related processing, (ii) includes a healthy adult sample, and (iii) provides whole-brain, group-level task activation maps/results clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or multivariate-only results) are met.

The study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses fMRI with a social-related mentalizing task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group with results reported). However, the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group; the whole-brain analyses reported are between-group contrasts (Controls > ASC) and ROI analyses. This violates exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded under E4.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social motor response learning paradigm (social inclusion/exclusion) in a sample of healthy adults (N=18, mean age 42±12). The paper provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (one-group t tests, FDR whole-brain correction) and reports significant activations in figures/tables (dorsal anterior cingulate, bilateral frontal operculum, ventral striatum, amygdala, thalamus). All required inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables and described in text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not MVPA-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (causal attribution/mentalizing) using a task-based design (meets I3). Sample comprises 20 healthy adult participants aged 18–41 with no psychiatric diagnoses reported (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., self/other/situation > truth baseline), conjunctions, and whole-brain results with voxelwise thresholds and FWE-corrected clusters (meets I5). Results are reported as whole-brain tables/figures and described in text (meets I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is a dual-fMRI hyperscanning study of social interaction in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper does not report a conventional univariate, group-level whole-brain task activation contrast; instead results are based on group ICA spatial components and inter-subject correlation (multivariate) analyses. Thus the only whole-brain maps presented are multivariate ICA components without accompanying univariate task-evoked activation maps, meeting exclusion criterion E6. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-cognitive task probing self-related processing (general and contextual self-judgments), with healthy adult participants (N=24, ages ~21–24). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise random-effects analyses (main effects, contrasts, interaction), tables of activations, and whole-brain regression results; ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain univariate results are clearly present. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of co-speech gestures during narrative comprehension—a form of social communication—conducted in healthy adults (N=20, ages 22–35). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task contrasts (e.g., low_ID>high_ID; speech>gestures+speech; gestures+speech>speech) using SPM12 with cluster correction and provides activation tables/figures in MNI space. Methods, results, and group-level statistical maps/coordinates are described, satisfying whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not multivariate-only, and is empirical). Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of social-related fMRI processing in healthy adults.

This fMRI study examines self- and other-referential processing (self, mother, president) — constructs clearly within perception/understanding of self and others (I3). The sample includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (n=15, ages 31–58) reported separately from patients (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and statistical contrasts for the healthy/control group (figures and voxelwise ANOVA, cluster-corrected maps and coordinates) and describes thresholds and corrections (I5,I6). Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, multivariate-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of biological motion perception (point-light walkers), a social-related task tapping perception/understanding of others. The sample comprises 13 healthy adult participants (mean age 28.2), meeting the adult healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (canonical vs. scrambled biological motion) with corrected statistics and tables/coordinates and figures describing these results. Thus it provides univariate whole-brain healthy-group activation maps in text/tables/figures. Although the paper also includes seed-based functional connectivity and DCM, these are supplementary to and do not replace the reported whole-brain activation. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social decision-making task (repeated public good game) and explicitly models social tie formation, satisfying construct relevance. The sample includes healthy adult participants (25 scanned; mean age ~22.6), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM results with MNI coordinates and cluster-wise FWE correction (reported maps, tables, and figures), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results and coordinates are presented in text, figures, and supplementary tables. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an fMRI study investigating perception of emotional facial expressions (social communication) with healthy adult human participants (n=23; ages 24–34). It reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (cluster-corrected significance maps shown and described) for the healthy human group separately from monkey data. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (maps/tables clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete and reports an event-related fMRI study of empathy (social cognition) in healthy adult participants (n=23, ages 19–34). The paper uses whole-brain, group-level random-effects univariate analyses (SPM) with reported voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Pain > No Pain; No Pain: Dissimilar > Similar) and tables of cluster coordinates; figures showing thresholded statistical maps are provided. The task is clearly social (perception/understanding of others’ affect) and meets the meta-analysis focus. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adult group whole-brain task effects, not MVPA-only, empirical data present). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This paper reports an fMRI study of a social task (eye contact modulation of spontaneous mimicry), tested in healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age 23). The authors present group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM contrasts (e.g., Congruent > Catch, Incongruent > Catch, Direct > Averted, interaction contrasts) with cluster-level FWE correction, coordinate tables (Table 1), and figures—fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. Results for the healthy sample are reported clearly and separately. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This study reports an fMRI experiment examining how observed eye contact between faces modulates gaze-following, a clearly social-cognitive task. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=21, mean age 24.6). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports contrasts (e.g., EC>AG, Cong>Incong, interaction contrasts) with cluster thresholds and tables/figures of activation loci, consistent with whole-brain univariate results. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not a non-empirical paper, and the sample is adult). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This peer-reviewed fMRI study investigates social gaze processing (mutual vs averted gaze) using a task that clearly probes social perception/communication, meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy young adult participants (fMRI group), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses and displays t-statistic activation maps (group-averaged, voxel-based activation maps shown in Figure 4), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are also described in text and figures, satisfying the allowance for tables/figures. The full text (background, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting/state-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-adult sample only, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of self- and other-reflection — constructs mapping to perception/understanding of self and others (social-related processing). The study includes a healthy adult control group (N=21) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate activation results for the healthy control group (e.g., main effects: self>semantic and other>semantic with voxelwise FWE correction and cluster info; supplementary tables and figures provided). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-cognition task (comic-strip ToM and empathy conditions) in a sample of healthy college students (age range 17–21, mean 19.3). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM activation maps (with RFT correction) for task contrasts (ToM vs control, Emp vs control, and pooled social > physical), with coordinates and cluster information described. Thus it meets I3 (task-based social fMRI), I4 (healthy adult participants reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy group), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables and described). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Although the study uses fMRI during a social-related task (face encoding/recognition) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. The analysis is centred on individually defined fusiform face area (FFA) ROIs and subsequent ROI-based comparisons; no unmasked whole-brain healthy-group activation maps or voxelwise contrasts are provided in the main text. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting) and fails inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task: face perception/recognition) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level task map from healthy group). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Provided full text appears to be limited to title, author information, and abstract only; core article content (detailed methods, whole-brain results, figures/tables) is missing. From the abstract the study uses fMRI during a social-related face perception task (satisfies I3) and reports healthy adult participants (satisfies I4). However I cannot verify whether the paper reports at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map from the healthy group (I5), because the full methods/results and any whole-brain tables/figures are not present. No exclusion criteria E2–E7 are clearly met based on the abstract alone. Because the full text is incomplete and I5 cannot be confirmed, I exclude the study pending the full article.

This paper includes task fMRI data for social cognition (explicitly reports analyses on social cognition tasks) drawn from the healthy Human Connectome Project cohort (n=493), satisfying the sample requirement for healthy adults. The authors report and use group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation patterns (they state task-evoked activation patterns were obtained from the HCP dataset and show group-level GLM-derived maps for working memory; social-task related whole-brain results and sensitivity maps are reported in main/supplementary figures), which meets the requirement for whole-brain, group-level univariate task activation reporting. Whole-brain results are presented in figures and supplementary materials, consistent with the allowed reporting formats. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, multivariate-only maps, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults and is included.

This is an empirical fMRI study administering a social task (face-viewing of real-world group members and person-judgment localizer), with healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 28.7). The paper reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain analyses (parametric whole-brain regression; Fig. S1 and Table S4; FWE-corrected results and coordinates), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy adult whole-brain contrasts, not multivariate-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, SI).

This fMRI study probes social emotional processing (images of group vs individual social interactions) and includes a healthy adult control group with separate within-group results (satisfies I3 and I4). However, the reported control-group results are derived from analyses constrained to an a priori ROI mask and reported as ROI-corrected activations; the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI-based task results for the healthy group). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E2.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly manipulates social processing (trustworthiness judgments) during an n-back task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (mean age 22) and results are reported for the healthy group. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster correction and tables/figures of peak coordinates and activation maps, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not multivariate-only, and not non-empirical). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is provided.

This study meets I3 (uses fMRI during social-related tasks: emotion attribution, age attribution, and social animations) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately).
