However, the paper’s whole-brain results are reported as multivariate (searchlight MVPA) maps and ROI-based MVPA; the manuscript does not present a univariate, group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group in the main text (univariate analyses are only briefly mentioned as reporting no group differences and referred to supplementary material without a clear univariate whole-brain healthy-group map). Therefore it fails I5 (clear univariate whole-brain healthy-group task map) and meets exclusion E6 — the only whole-brain healthy-group results shown are multivariate (searchlight) maps without an accompanying univariate group-level task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E6.

The study uses fMRI of a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes) and includes a healthy adult control group, but the reported neuroimaging results are presented as between-group contrasts (controls vs high-risk) rather than as an unmasked, whole-brain, within-group task activation map for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clear report of a whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map for the healthy/control group). Exclusion criterion met: E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete.

Full text provided appears incomplete (only metadata/abstract present). The abstract indicates an fMRI study of social judgments (empathy, forgiveness) in ten volunteers and reports activated brain regions, so I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is satisfied. However, the full manuscript (methods, participants’ ages, and detailed results) is not available here, so I cannot verify I4 (that at least one healthy adult group, ages 18–65, is reported separately) or I5 (that a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group is reported). Because these essential inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the provided content, the study is excluded pending provision of the complete full text. Recommend retrieving the full article PDF to reassess eligibility.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy young adults using a social-attribution task (perception of human-like interactions among geometric shapes). The paper reports group-level activations in the fusiform gyrus and multiple social-cognitive regions (amygdala, temporal pole, medial PFC, etc.), indicating whole-brain task-evoked results rather than ROI-only analyses. The sample is healthy adults and results for that group are reported. The full text is available. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of a social-related manipulation (social sharing of emotional vs unshared experience) in healthy adult participants (behavioral sample n=58; fMRI sample n=26; ages 20–33). It includes clear group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and reports suprathreshold whole-brain activations (with AFNI AlphaSim cluster correction) in addition to ROI results; contrasts and tables/figures present healthy-group task-evoked activation maps. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses task-based fMRI to probe social-related processing (evaluative judgments of guilt and embarrassment; I3). The sample is healthy adult participants (N=19, ages within adult range) with no psychiatric history (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (G−N, E−N, G−E, E−G) analyzed with random-effects and thresholding, and provides coordinate tables and figures (I5, I6). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, enabling verification of analyses; no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study (EmpaToM) probing social-cognitive processes (empathy and Theory of Mind) in a healthy adult sample (N=178, mean age 40.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., emotional vs neutral videos; ToM vs non-ToM questions) analyzed with random-effects one-sample t-tests and provides activation peaks/coordinates and figures. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures as described). Although the paper also includes connectivity/DCM and resting-state analyses, these are supplementary to and do not replace the univariate whole-brain task results, so no exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, MVPA-only, non-adult-sample, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore, I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study where healthy adult participants (n=13, mean age 27) passively viewed realistic social-interaction movie clips (social-related task). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (relational vs. rest; relational vs. alone) with cluster-level results and whole-brain multiple-comparison correction (P ≤ 0.05), shown in figures and a table of activations. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic multimodal empathy/social cognition stimuli) and includes a healthy adult control group (n=24, mean age 35.25). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (mixed-effects random-effects GLM, whole-brain cluster correction) and describes within-group T-contrasts performed separately for each participant group (controls included) with results in-text and referenced supplementary tables/figures (online Tables DS3–5, Fig. DS2), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group, whole-brain task-evoked map (reported via tables/figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy results, univariate whole-brain activation contrasts reported). Full text provided appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included.

The study is an fMRI investigation of face processing (a social-related task) comparing a single adult patient with ASD+DP to control subjects; therefore I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (includes healthy control group) appear satisfied from the abstract. However, the provided full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata available), so I cannot verify whether the paper reports an unmasked, group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked (univariate) statistical map for the healthy/control group (I5). Without the complete methods/results, I cannot confirm whole-brain evidence and must exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are clearly met, but inability to confirm I5 prevents inclusion. Full text incomplete flag set.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social cognition (face-based trustworthiness judgments and feedback learning), i.e., a social-related task. The sample includes a healthy younger adult group (age 20–33) meeting the 18–65 requirement. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task activation results (ANOVA and whole-brain analyses, cluster/voxel results, tables and figures showing significant clusters, and between-/within-factor effects), clearly identified in the text and tables/figures. Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures (satisfying acceptable reporting formats). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, MVPA-only, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided and appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study of emotional sentence attribution (a social-cognition task concerning perception/understanding of others), includes a healthy adult control group (n=25) with results reported separately, and presents whole-brain, group-level univariate task-evoked contrasts (e.g., healthy-controls EMO>GRAM activation including mPFC) with FWE-corrected maps and figures/tables. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references present).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (self-evaluation and endorsement of others’ evaluation) in healthy adults. The full text reports task-based whole-brain, group-level univariate contrasts and a whole-brain multiple regression with tables/figures of voxelwise results (cluster-level FWE-corrected), satisfying the meta-analysis reporting requirements. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=31, ages 19–24). The article includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and activation coordinate tables; full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside adult range, not multivariate-only, and not non-empirical).

Excluded: this paper reports structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) associations between GM volume and proneness to moral sentiments and behavioral responses on the VMST, but does not report task-evoked fMRI whole-brain activation maps from healthy participants. A secondary analysis uses previously acquired SSC-BOLD values from a subgroup (N=29) but the article does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain fMRI task map for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task reported in this paper) and I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group). No exclusion criteria from E2–E7 directly apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (mentalizing about friends vs kin) in healthy adults (female sample, mean age 23.2), satisfying the review scope. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (friend > kin and parametric linear analyses across network layers) with cluster-thresholded statistical maps and tables of cluster coordinates, clearly identified as healthy-group results. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI experiment of legal decision-making that probes social cognition (inference about others, responsibility, punishment), meeting the social-related task requirement. Sample includes healthy adults (final N=20; age range 18–45), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task activation contrasts (multiple whole-brain contrasts, tables of peak coordinates and corrected results are described), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports an fMRI experiment where participants observed virtual social interactions (a social-related task). Methods indicate healthy adult participants were recruited and group-level results are reported (activation maps based on data from 15 participants). The paper presents whole-brain, voxelwise univariate activation maps/contrasts (social interaction vs. no-interaction) using SPM and shows activations in canonical social cognition regions (STS, mPFC, amygdala). Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult group reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I6 (results presented as figures/activation maps). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears to include core methods, results, and figures; fulltext_incomplete set to false.

The article reports an fMRI study using a social/emotion-related task (facial affect matching), includes a healthy adult control group (n=12, ages ~32), and presents group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked contrasts for the healthy group (Emotion Match > Shape Match) in tables and figures (thresholded at p<.005, cluster extent=10). The full text contains introduction, methods, results (within-group healthy maps in Table 1 and figures), and discussion, so core content is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study uses task-based fMRI to investigate social-cognitive processes (affective Theory of Mind, emotion recognition, face processing) in adults, meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample includes a clearly reported healthy control group of adult participants (n=18) with results reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation results for the healthy/control group (within-group contrasts and coordinates for STS, inferior prefrontal gyrus, fusiform, etc.), and provides coordinates/figures and ROI analyses; whole-brain thresholds and coordinates are described (supplementary tables referenced), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not MVPA-only, not non-empirical, and includes adult healthy group).

Full text appears incomplete (only metadata/cookie banner and citation info provided). Cannot verify key inclusion criteria: I3 (use of fMRI during a social-related task) cannot be confirmed from the provided content; I4 (at least one healthy adult group reported separately) cannot be confirmed; I5/I6 (reporting of a whole-brain, group-level task-evoked healthy/control map, reported as maps or coordinates) cannot be confirmed. Title suggests an affective theory-of-mind fMRI study in schizophrenia out-patients that likely includes controls, but the provided full text lacks methods, results, and figures/tables to confirm whole-brain healthy-group results. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) can be positively identified from the incomplete content. Therefore excluded due to incomplete full text and inability to verify inclusion criteria I3–I6.

E4 met: The paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related face-processing task) and I4 (contains a healthy adult control group reported separately in ROI/behavioral analyses). Inclusion not met: I5 (no whole-brain, group-level healthy/control task-evoked statistical map was provided — only whole-group maps and between-group contrasts, plus ROI results). fulltext_incomplete is false.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The abstract indicates use of dyadic fMRI during an eye-contact social interaction task, so inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is met. However, critical information is missing: no participant/sample details are reported (so I4 is not met), and no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or results are provided in the provided content (so I5 and I6 are not met). Because the provided content lacks methods, participant demographics, and whole-brain results, I cannot verify other inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) can be confidently applied based on the truncated content. Recommend obtaining the complete paper (full methods and results) before reconsidering inclusion.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (participants thought about interpersonal social interaction verbs), meeting I3. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (17 age- and IQ-matched controls) with results reported separately, meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked contrasts for the within-group (all social interactions – fixation) analyses and shows SPM contrasts for both groups (uncorrected p=0.001, extent threshold 5 voxels), satisfying I5 and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/text). The study also includes multivariate/classification analyses but importantly provides univariate whole-brain healthy-group activation maps, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=19, mean age 27.7) investigating mirror neuron responses and the modulation by emotional (IAPS) primes — a social-cognitive/emotion processing paradigm. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (full article content present). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., untrained>trained) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and stereotactic coordinates, and provides ROI and whole-brain analyses and figures. Thus it meets the meta-analysis benchmarks: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps), and I6 (results presented as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply.

This is an fMRI study of implicit facial emotion recognition (a social-perception task), and it reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps for the healthy control group using SPM (one-sample t-tests with cluster-level correction). The sample includes age-matched healthy controls (matched to GHR aged 16–35); the review allows age ranges that slightly extend below 18. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, non-adult-only sample, or MVPA-only) are met.

This article is a systematic review / multilevel-kernel-density meta-analysis of previously published fMRI studies and does not report original, unmasked group-level whole-brain task activation maps from a healthy adult sample. Exclusion criteria met: E7 (non-empirical paper/meta-analysis without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none of I3–I6 are directly satisfied by this paper as an empirical report (it does address social-related constructs such as love/affiliation in the reviewed studies, but it does not itself present original fMRI task data from a healthy group). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not itself use fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (does not report an original healthy adult participant group), I5 (does not report at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from a healthy group), I6 (not applicable—no qualifying whole-brain results reported as original coordinates/tables for an empirical healthy group). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study of verbal irony that explicitly probes Theory of Mind/social-communication processing (a social-related task). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=20, mean age 22). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task contrasts (Ironic > Literal) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level corrections, and provides coordinates/tables and ROI analyses; thus whole-brain healthy-group results are clearly reported. Reporting in text/tables meets acceptable formats. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-adult-only, not multivariate-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a third-party punishment task that clearly probes social cognition/understanding of others (mentalizing/attribution of intent). The sample consists of healthy adult volunteers (n=26; mean age 26) meeting the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (ANOVA on beta parameters; whole-brain FDR q<0.05) with Talairach coordinates for significant clusters (R TPJ, R anterior insula) and displays figures and statistical maps described in the text. Results for the healthy/control group are reported directly (not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses). Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses fMRI during a social-related task (adaptive emotion recognition) and includes a healthy adult control group, but the full text does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Results focus on between-group contrasts (patients vs controls), interactions, and ROI analyses of the amygdala; I cannot find a healthy-group whole-brain task effect (healthy>baseline or emotion>baseline within controls) reported as a whole-brain map or table of coordinates. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Full text appears complete.

The study reports task-based fMRI during reading of a literary narrative that evokes social-cognitive processes (mentalizing/theory-of-mind). Sample: healthy adults (n=23, age 19–32). The authors present whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses (GLM; SPM results reported with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/figures of coordinates) showing activity in medial frontal cortex and TPJ linked to perspective-taking/understanding others. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related processing: perception/understanding of others), I4 (healthy adult participants), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked map), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (imagined triadic interactions, self- and other-referential tasks) in healthy adults. Sample: 19 healthy adult participants (mean age 26.5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise univariate contrasts (triad>iron, self>iron, other>iron; conjunction and direct contrasts) with family-wise error corrected thresholds (p<.05) and provides tables of coordinates and figures. Thus it addresses social-related processing with functional MRI (I3), includes a healthy adult sample (I4), reports whole-brain group-level task activation maps (I5), and provides coordinate/figure reporting acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only (although PPI is included, univariate whole-brain results are present), not between-group-only, age is adult, and univariate activation contrasts are reported (so not multivariate-only). Full text appears complete. Therefore INCLUDE in the review.

This study must be excluded. Exclusion IDs met: E3 (study reports resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses without any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps) and E5 (sample is wholly adolescent; participants are aged 11–18, not healthy adults 18–65). Inclusion IDs met: none ([]). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (does not use task-based fMRI of social-related processing; it uses resting-state fcMRI), I4 (does not include a healthy adult sample; control group are adolescents), I5 (does not report a group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for a healthy adult group). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the paper does not satisfy the review’s inclusion criteria and meets multiple exclusion criteria (E3, E5).

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Task is an emotion discrimination of faces — a social-related task (perception/understanding of others); (I4) Sample includes 38 healthy adults (mean age 27.5) with clearly reported healthy-group results; (I5) Reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked SPM contrast (FACES>OBJECTS) with thresholds, cluster sizes, peak coordinates; (I6) Whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, not MVPA-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore include for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=19) using a social-related task (charitable donation decisions tied to moral/social causes). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate GLM contrasts and random-effects analyses, with activation tables/figures and coordinate reporting (P < 0.005 uncorrected), clearly from the healthy participant group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (coordinates/figures reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related facial emotion task (meets I3) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (meets I4). However, the full text only reports between-group (VCFS vs control) voxelwise differences (Table 1) and does not present or describe an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (I5 not met). Therefore exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) is met. Other exclusion criteria (E2, E3, E5, E6, E7) do not apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This article reports an fMRI experiment of social-related processing (self and reflected evaluations; attribute framing), with a healthy adult sample (n=21, ages 19–41). The paper includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation contrasts (e.g., positive vs negative frame, task vs control, frame-consistent vs inconsistent) with thresholding and reported coordinates and cluster sizes. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-adult sample, and includes univariate whole-brain task-evoked maps). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (30 right-handed adults, ages 18–35) using a social task (empathy for pain with minimal ingroup/outgroup manipulation), satisfying social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate SPM analyses (main effect of pain with FWE-corrected results and pain×condition interactions) with cluster tables and coordinates (Tables 5–7), fulfilling whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, not multivariate-only, and the sample is within the adult range. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore the study should be included.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on abstract, the study used fMRI of face–voice integration in 20 participants (meets I3: social-related fMRI task, and I4: healthy adult sample). However I cannot verify I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain univariate task-evoked voxelwise map) from the provided content. The abstract mentions regions and PPI connectivity, but the full methods/results (whole-brain group contrasts, tables/coordinates, or figures) are not available to confirm compliance with I5/I6. Because not all inclusion criteria can be confirmed and core article content is missing, I exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are demonstrably met from the available text, but inability to confirm whole-brain univariate results prevents inclusion. fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a social cognitive task (false belief/theory of mind) in healthy adults (N=34, ages 20–28) reporting group-level whole-brain task activation contrasts (ROMS vs CTRL) with statistical maps and coordinate tables. The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures describing voxelwise analyses and thresholds. Therefore it meets I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map from healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results reported via figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not exclusively between-group contrasts, adult sample, univariate activation reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using a social interaction task (a modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm presenting opponents’ facial expressions) in healthy adult participants (32 included in analyses; mean age 23.3). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (angry > neutral) with cluster-wise FWE correction and tables/figures of activation results, clearly identified as coming from the healthy sample. Whole-brain results are described in text, tables, and figures (satisfying reporting flexibility). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the report appears complete. Although ROI analyses are also reported, they do not preclude the presence of whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met.

(a) Exclusion criterion met: E6 — the paper’s whole-brain results are based on multivariate encoding/PCA maps and voxelwise model projections, not on a univariate, group-level task-evoked activation contrast. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 — fMRI was acquired while subjects passively viewed natural movies that include social-communication content and the analyses quantify responses to social-communication categories; I4 — the sample consists of healthy adult participants (6 subjects, ages in range). (c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 — the paper does not report a conventional univariate, group-level, whole-brain task activation map (main effect or within-group contrast) for the healthy/control group; instead results are multivariate encoding and PC projection maps. Because E6 applies, the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study directly investigates social-related processing (empathy/perception of others’ pain) in healthy adult participants (n≈36, ages ~21). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task contrasts (painful vs. non-painful) with FDR-corrected voxelwise results and tabulated activation coordinates (pre- and post-priming whole-brain analyses are described). The task and analyses map onto the review constructs (Perception and Understanding of Others). All required elements are present in the full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion), and healthy-group results are reported separately and as whole-brain contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (face perception with emotional and neutral expressions) and reports task-evoked contrasts (task vs. rest). A healthy adult control group (n=7, mean age 30) is included and analyzed separately; within-group analyses showed DMN deactivations in both groups. The methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise group-level GLM analyses (task vs. rest) with Monte-Carlo cluster correction and report significant clusters for within-group effects and group comparisons, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group results. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not multivariate-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This study reports an fMRI task explicitly probing social processing (observing social interactions vs non-social motion), tested in a healthy adult sample (N=14, mean age 29.4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise contrasts (SI > NSI) with FDR-corrected results and cluster coordinates reported (Table 1, whole-brain maps discussed and displayed). It is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, multivariate-only, nor non-empirical. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly investigates social (interpersonal resource conflict) processing using an event-related fMRI task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (final N=17, mean age 23.5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts and presents voxelwise statistical maps and tables (e.g., Conflict > No Conflict; Human vs Computer interaction), clearly derived from the healthy participant group. Behavioral and covariate whole-brain analyses are also reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all applicable inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (Narrative Experiment n=41, localizers n=14; ages 18–37 and 19–33) that investigates social cognition (empathy, Theory of Mind) using task-based fMRI narratives and functional localizers. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (SnPM) with corrected thresholds and peak coordinates for contrasts (e.g., Pain vs No Pain, PP vs PPC, EP vs EPC), and also presents ROI analyses; whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and tables. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Exclusion: E2 met. This study used task-based fMRI of social interaction in healthy adults (I3 and I4 satisfied: interactive joint-attention task; healthy adult sample n=24, ages 20–34). However, all reported voxelwise fMRI inferences were performed using small-volume correction (SVC) within a priori ROIs; the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map or whole-brain voxelwise results for the healthy group. Therefore it reports only ROI/SVC results and lacks the required whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (I5 not met). Because the qualifying whole-brain result is absent, the allowed reporting formats (I6) are also not satisfied. Decision: EXCLUDED due to E2. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met: I5, I6.

This paper reports an event-related BOLD fMRI study of self-face recognition—a social-cognitive task tapping ‘Perception and Understanding of Self’—in healthy adult participants (right-handed males, mean age 19.36). Group-level whole-brain random-effects contrasts are reported (e.g., self vs. familiar, familiar vs. unknown) with thresholding and cluster reporting; results are presented in figures and tables with coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to emotional facial expressions (affiliation-relevant stimuli: happy and disgust) — a social-related task. Sample consists of healthy adults (n=40, mean age ~29). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses (family-wise error cluster-corrected thresholds) and provides ROI and voxel coordinates for significant clusters (i.e., whole-brain maps reported as coordinates), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a face identity discrimination task (social perception of others), includes a healthy adult control group (CA; N=17, mean age 31), and presents voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses and maps (voxel-wise ANOVA, mean z-score images for control groups; Supplementary Table 1). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of the healthy-group activation maps. Thus it meets social-related task requirement (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and whole-brain group-level reporting (I5,I6). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of social perception (eye-gaze/intentionality processing — perception and understanding of others/theory-of-mind) that includes a healthy adult comparison group (n=9; mean age 23.4 years). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses for the neurologically normal (healthy) group (figures of activation maps and Table 1 with stereotaxic coordinates of clusters) and within-group incongruent>congruent contrasts. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level statistical maps for the healthy group), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing (explicit mental simulation of another's actions/feelings), includes a healthy adult sample (N=20, ages 21–47), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (GLM SPM-t maps, cluster-level FDR-corrected contrasts) and ISPS/SBPS connectivity results. Whole-brain univariate activation contrasts (simulate > watch; simulate losing > simulate winning etc.) are reported and visualized, satisfying the requirement that healthy-group whole-brain task effects be available (figures/tables and text). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the record appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, multivariate-only, non-empirical, non-adult sample) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the review.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social/affective touch (a social-related task), testing CT-targeted pleasant touch versus baseline and arm versus palm. Sample: 22 healthy adults aged 19–35 (meets adult healthy sample). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses (arm > baseline, palm > baseline, arm > palm) with FDR and cluster correction, tables of results, coordinate lists, and figures—satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

The study reports task-based fMRI of empathy/social cognition (observation of human and animal suffering), meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample is healthy adults (n=60, ages 18–60) with group-level analyses reported separately for omnivores, vegetarians, and vegans. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results are reported (SPM2 random-effects analyses; FWE-corrected maps and MNI coordinates are provided in text/figures/tables). Results are univariate activation contrasts (human>neutral, animal>neutral) with coordinate tables; not ROI-only, not connectivity- or multivariate-only. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (manipulated social touch by perceived toucher sex) with a within-subject pharmaco-fMRI design in healthy adult participants (N=40, mean age 25.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., touch>close; Female TouchOXT>Female TouchPLC) with coordinates and family-wise error-corrected results across multiple regions (OFC, pACC, insula, precuneus, SI, caudate), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, sample is adult, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, references).

This full-text reports an event-related fMRI task that manipulates social reputation (positive, negative, neutral) while participants (healthy adult volunteers, N=28, ages 20–24) rated pleasantness—meeting the social-related task requirement. The paper presents whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (e.g., positive vs. neutral; negative vs. neutral) with cluster-level FWE correction and reports activation tables and coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Healthy adult sample is reported separately. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not MVPA-only, and is an empirical fMRI study). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore, the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social decision-making task (iterative modified prisoner’s dilemma) fulfilling social-related processing (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=20, ages 23–45) with results reported separately (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation contrasts and coordinates for the healthy controls (e.g., HC Task>CONT, conjunction and within-group maps, Table 1 and figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (perception/understanding of others via laughter types), using tasks explicitly probing social communication (I3). The sample comprises 18 healthy adult participants (mean age 26, right-handed, no neurological/psychiatric history), satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation contrasts (conjunctions, whole-brain analyses, tables of coordinates and figures) clearly from the healthy group (I5,I6). Results include both ROI-based small-volume corrections and whole-brain analyses; it is not ROI-only and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria met.

The study reports an fMRI task involving observation of others’ actions (risk-taking vs safe), which maps onto social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). The sample consists of healthy late-adult participants (ages 18.1–22.8), meeting the adult age criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation contrasts (risk-taking vs safe) with coordinates and figures, and conducts whole-brain regression and conjunction analyses; results are reported for the healthy group. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study using a social interactive task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) that probes responses to unreciprocated cooperation. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (ages 18–22) with group-level analyses reported. The paper explicitly reports whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation contrasts (e.g., CD>CC) and refers to whole-brain results and figures/tables (main effect and drug effects), satisfying the requirement for group-level, whole-brain healthy-group maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts without healthy-group maps, non-adult sample only, multivariate-only maps, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the review objective and is eligible for inclusion.

This study uses task-based fMRI to probe social-related processing (positive social interaction, faces, erotic scenes) meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=14) with results reported and compared separately (I4). Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise (stimulus group × participant group × scan ANOVAs with Monte Carlo cluster correction) and report group-level clusters and simple-effects for the control group (I5). Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in text (I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=55, mean age ~25) using an explicit social task (viewing attachment-related erotic scenes and fearful social scenes). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate activation contrasts (e.g., erotic > neutral; fearful > neutral; erotic > fearful) with FWE-corrected results and cluster/ROI analyses described in the text and supplementary material. Healthy-group whole-brain task effects are clearly reported (not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only results). The sample is within the adult age range and results for the healthy group are presented. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants (N=34 healthy adults, mean age 22.2) viewed a movie and the authors used fMRI to characterize responses to social interactions. The paper reports both ROI analyses and a whole-brain voxelwise reverse-correlation analysis (with χ2 tests and thresholded statistical maps; Fig. 3), providing group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy sample. Reporting includes figures and tables describing voxelwise findings. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related tasks in healthy adults and provides whole-brain results suitable for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (impression formation/person evaluation) in healthy adults. The sample comprises 20 healthy male adults (ages 19–31). The paper reports both ROI analyses and an exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analysis (ANOVA and contrast images versus fixation) with activations reported in a table and figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not MVPA-only, empirical fMRI data in adults). Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI during a social-cognition (Theory of Mind) task and included a healthy adult control group (n=25) with results reported separately. The manuscript describes whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (with tables/figures of activated regions and whole-brain images) and reports activation in ToM-related regions for the groups, satisfying the requirement for a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map for the healthy/control group. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic happy and fearful facial expressions) in adults, and it reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps for the study groups including the healthy control group (figures and thresholding details given: Z>2.3, cluster-corrected). The sample includes healthy adult controls (N=52) and results for groups are reported separately. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social processing (gaze-following toward political in-group/out-group faces), meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy adults (N=28, ages 18–29) reported as the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (incongruent > congruent) with cluster-level correction and tables/coordinates, clearly identified as coming from the healthy participants. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=41; mean age 22.6) that used a social-affective mimicry task probing affiliation-relevant processing (emotion and group membership). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., Incongruent>Congruent, and masked contrasts for Happy vs Angry and Out-group vs In-group) with cluster-level correction and tabulated coordinate results, clearly identified as healthy-group results. Full methods, results, and discussion are present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and none of the exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (N=50, ages 18–29) that used a social-related task (explicit labeling of others’ emotional facial expressions), meeting the review’s definition of social processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked contrasts (HA>NE, AN>NE, FE>NE) analyzed with SPM8 and cluster-level FWE-corrected results presented in tables and figures. Whole-brain regression analyses using alexithymia measures are also reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, references). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports event-related fMRI during an explicit social task (empathy for others' pain; participants asked to imagine how the person feels), includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group (n=13) with separate analyses, and provides group-level whole-brain univariate SPM results (figures and tables of coordinates for the control group). Whole-brain contrasts and within-group effects for healthy controls are described and tabulated, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria are met and the full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of impression formation (perception/understanding of others), using healthy adult participants (N=18, ages 19–30). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent) with cluster thresholds and FDR correction and provides coordinate tables and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the review.

This fMRI study investigates dynamic happy facial expression processing within social interaction cues and includes a healthy adult comparison group (non-SPD). However, the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The results focus on combined-group maps and between-group contrasts and ROI extractions, but no separate whole-brain healthy-group (non-SPD) task-evoked map is provided. Therefore it fails the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain activation result.

This fMRI study used a social-related task (explicit facial emotion recognition) meeting I3. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (ages ~25–27), meeting I4. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task-evoked contrasts (Emo_Emo > Neu_Age and related contrasts) with tables of significant clusters and coordinates (Table 2, Fig. 3), satisfying I5 and I6. The full-text contains Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (empathy/threat to self, friend, stranger) in healthy adults (N=22, mean age 23.6). The task is social/affiliation-related (threat-to-other, hand-holding). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task contrasts (threat minus safe) and conjunction analyses using non-masked whole-brain data, with higher-level whole-brain analyses and tables/figures of results. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not multivariate-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of causal attributions (a social-cognitive task involving perception/understanding of self and others). It used task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (12 right-handed male volunteers, ages 20–51), satisfying the sample criterion for healthy adults. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99 fixed-effects and follow-up random-effects ROI tests) with tables of peak coordinates and figures for contrasts such as internal vs external attributions and self-serving vs non-self-serving attributions. Results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not developmental/geriatric-only, not MVPA-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related visual perspective-taking task (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (I4). However, it does not report an univariate, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. Second-level activation analyses were restricted to predefined prefrontal ROIs (ROI-based inference) and group comparisons are emphasized (patient vs. control). The only whole-brain voxelwise results reported are exploratory seed-based functional connectivity analyses. Therefore the paper violates exclusion criteria: E2 (reports ROI-restricted activation results with no whole-brain task activation map), E3 (the only whole-brain voxelwise maps presented are connectivity results), and E4 (results focus on between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a randomized longitudinal fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n≈51, ages ~31), using the Ultimatum Game — a social decision-making task probing cooperation/affiliation. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked analyses (conjunction and interaction contrasts) with voxelwise statistical maps and coordinates (FDR-corrected results and tables/figures), and also provides ROI and PPI results. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during a social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activations reported for healthy groups), and I6 (coordinates/figures describing whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not MVPA-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group healthy results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary summaries present).

The study reports an fMRI experiment of social communication (viewing, imitating, and producing facial expressions and social hand gestures), meeting the review’s social-process requirement (I3). Participants are described as study participants (healthy adults), with no clinical groups reported separately, satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The paper describes group-level task-evoked activations in the mirror neuron system (inferior parietal lobule and frontal operculum) and contrasts between conditions, indicating whole-brain, voxelwise task effects reported for the healthy group (I5). The reported activations are described in text (and likely figures/tables), which fits acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Note: the provided full text appears to be abstract/summary-level rather than the complete article (methods and full results not present), so fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is moderate.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (20 male adults, ages 20–28) who viewed social/traffic-awareness videos designed to elicit empathy (a social cognitive/emotional task). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (CV>NV) with FWE correction, includes tables of peak coordinates and whole-brain images, and links brain activation (STS) to behavioral empathic indices. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating perception of different laughter types (social vs. tickling) using task manipulations that probe social information processing (laughter-type categorization vs. bout counting). The sample comprises 18 healthy adult participants (mean age 26), and group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (e.g., CSL>TIC, CAT>COU) are reported with coordinates, cluster thresholds, and figures/tables. Although the paper also reports PPI connectivity analyses, these are supplemental to and accompany univariate whole-brain activation contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related processing in healthy adults and provides whole-brain task-evoked activation maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 18–25) who performed a social interaction task (competitive matching-pennies game) — satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise univariate task-evoked analyses (parametric modulation and game-related contrasts; voxel-wise p<.001 with cluster FWE correction) and lists peak coordinates/tables — satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core data and whole-brain results are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, contains univariate whole-brain task maps, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interaction simulation task probing friendship (affiliation/attachment, social cognition). Sample: healthy adult participants (N=28, mean age 22.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and contrasts (SPM5, p<0.05 FWE-corrected, cluster thresholds) with tables/figures of activations (main effects and interaction), clearly from the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are triggered.

The available full-text content appears to be an abstract-level summary. Positives: the study used task-based fMRI during a social perception task (gender judgments of faces with gaze manipulation), satisfying I3, and the sample consists of healthy adult men (satisfying I4). Critical missing information: the provided text does not allow verification that the paper reports at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) univariate task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from a healthy/control group (I5). The abstract describes between-group differences (LFS vs NFS) and regional activations (amygdala, fusiform, STS) but does not state whether whole-brain, unmasked, within-healthy-group maps or coordinate tables are reported (I6 cannot be confirmed). Because I5 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete text, the study cannot be included at this stage. Full text is incomplete, so inclusion cannot be verified without the full article.

This article is an fMRI study of social-related processing (observation of socio-affective touch) using task-based fMRI and multivoxel/univariate analyses, meeting inclusion I3. The sample includes a separate healthy adult (neurotypical) group (n=21) reported separately from the ASD group, meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked univariate results for the healthy/control group (see main text and Additional file 1: Figure S2 and Table S2 with MNI coordinates), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, MVPA-only without univariate maps, non-adult sample) apply, so the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study reanalyzed using a finite impulse response model to identify neural correlates of facial mimicry during perception of socially relevant facial expressions. It uses a task manipulating social interaction/self-involvement (social vs. arbitrary facial gestures), acquired fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=17, mean age 25.9), and reports whole-brain, group-level univariate activation maps and stereotactic coordinates (SPM analyses, thresholded, with tables/figures). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Provided content appears to be only an abstract (fulltext_incomplete=true). Inclusion criterion I3 is met: the task involves self-regulation/personal goal processing (a social-related construct: Perception and Understanding of Self). However, I4 cannot be confirmed because participant ages and confirmation that the sample are healthy adults (18–65) are not reported in the provided text. I5 cannot be confirmed because the abstract does not explicitly report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E7) are clearly met based on the provided content. Recommend obtaining the complete full text (methods and results) to reassess eligibility.

Full text is complete and reports an fMRI social task (multi-round trust game) with healthy adult controls (20; ages 18–50). Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately). However, the paper does not report any univariate, group-level whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group alone; the only whole-brain voxel-wise results described are between-group contrasts (control > patients) from an exploratory analysis (coordinates reported). This means Inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task map) is not met. Because the only whole-brain results are between-group contrasts, Exclusion criterion E4 applies. Therefore the study must be excluded. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met: I5. Exclusion IDs met: E4.

The study reports an fMRI task probing perception/understanding of others (goal-directed biological motion vs non-goal-directed motion) — a social-related process. The sample is healthy adults (n=12, mean age 29.4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrast (BR motion minus BU motion) with reported coordinates and statistical thresholds, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, multivariate-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants viewing dynamic facial expressions (a social perception task). fMRI methods describe group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (one-sample t-test, dynamic > static contrast) with FDR-corrected whole-brain results, reported figures and tables of regions/coordinates. Sample: 40 healthy right-handed adults (mean age 30.5) with results clearly from the healthy group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and tables/figures, allowing verification of voxelwise whole-brain activation maps and coordinates. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-adult sample, and reports univariate whole-brain activation). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This fMRI study examines decoding of emotional prosody (social communication / perception of others) in healthy adult participants using task-based fMRI and thus addresses the review objective. Sample: 22 healthy right-handed adults (age mean 26.3 ± 7.7) — meets adult healthy sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked results from the voice localizer contrast (human voices vs animals/environment) and describes conventional univariate GLM analyses, satisfying the requirement for at least one whole-brain healthy-group map. Results are reported in the main text and supplemental figures/tables referenced, consistent with acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not an MVPA-only whole-brain report, and is empirical. Therefore include.

The study reports an fMRI task that explicitly evaluates social processing (face approachability judgments), meeting I3. The sample appears to be healthy adult participants (trait anxiety measured and no clinical group reported), meeting I4. The abstract and results describe task-related activations (interaction contrasts) indicating group-level activation in amygdala and frontal regions, and BOLD correlations with trait anxiety, which supports the presence of whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (I5). Reporting of activations in text and references to SPM/whole-brain methods indicate acceptable reporting in tables/figures (I6). However, the full article text is not accessible here (page indicates "You do not currently have access to this content"), so I cannot inspect methods/results sections directly to fully verify specifics (e.g., explicit statement of whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and coordinate tables). Given the clear abstract-level evidence and typical reporting, I include the study but flag the full text as incomplete for verification.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (adult male sample; age range includes 17 but acceptable per criteria). The task is social-related (in-group/out-group action perception and judgment). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task activation contrasts (e.g., action videos vs fixation; own vs other; decision vs baseline) with cluster-level FWE correction for the whole-brain search volume and provides coordinates/tables and figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, MVPA-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical limitations).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of audiovisual social-signal perception (faces and voices) using a gender-classification task under implicit conditions, satisfying I3. The sample comprises 24 healthy adult volunteers (mean age 26.6), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (conjunction AV>A and AV>V), random-effects inference, voxelwise correlation analyses, and thresholded activation maps/figures/tables, satisfying I5 and I6. Analyses are univariate task-evoked activations (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or MVPA-only), and healthy-group whole-brain results are clearly presented. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and complete.

Excluded per E2: the fMRI analyses are conducted as an a priori amygdala ROI (results corrected within the amygdala). While the paper reports group-level amygdala activations for the TD (healthy) group (e.g., right amygdala response to fearful faces), it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked group map for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task using emotional faces) and I4 (a healthy adult TD group is included and reported separately). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level healthy-control activation map reported). Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, the study uses rt-fMRI combined with EEG targeting social communication (I3 satisfied). However, no participant/sample details for a healthy adult group are reported in the available text (I4 not confirmed), and there is no evidence of a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked map; the analysis focuses on a predefined ROI (right pSTS) and EEG–fMRI correlations, consistent with ROI-only reporting (E2). Unable to verify whole-brain results due to incomplete full text. Therefore excluded pending full-text confirmation. Inclusion met: I3. Inclusion not met/ not verifiable: I4, I5, I6. Exclusion met: E2.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social processing (empathy and Theory of Mind) in healthy adult samples (Experiments: N=25, N=65, N=178; ages within 18–65). It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., ‘Empathy contrast’, ‘ToM contrast’), reports activation peak tables, and uses appropriate statistical thresholds (including FWE-corrected results). Behavioral and neuroimaging results for the healthy/control groups are reported separately. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social perception using a task that manipulates approach behavior and emotional facial expressions (affiliation/dominance), meeting the review’s social-related construct requirement. The sample consists of healthy young adults (n=10), satisfying the adult healthy sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (Angry>Happy, Happy>Angry) with MNI coordinates, cluster sizes, and thresholding details, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement; coordinate tables and figures are described. No exclusion criteria are met. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (ten right-handed males, ages 22–32) using a social-related task (perception/understanding of others’ dyadic biological motion). The authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., atypical vs typical displays) with cluster-level correction and tables/coordinates of activated regions. The healthy-control group results are reported directly (not limited to an ROI-only, connectivity-only, or multivariate-only analysis). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=35, mean age 29) that uses a social-related task (memory for faces displaying emotional expressions—perception/understanding of others). The authors report whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected results, emotion and load contrasts) with Talairach coordinates and statistical maps described in the text and tables, and correlate behavior with regional beta values. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported for the healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates and described in text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside adult age range, not MVPA-only, and is empirical).

The article is a non-empirical review (Japanese) discussing fMRI approaches and examples; no original fMRI data, methods, or group-level results in healthy adults are reported in the provided content. Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata present). Exclusion applies per E7 (Non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). No inclusion criteria are met: I3 (no original fMRI task data reported), I4 (no healthy adult sample reported), I5 (no whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results). fulltext_incomplete flagged true because core article content (methods/results) is not present in the provided full text.

This is an fMRI study that used a virtual-reality social cognition task (face-to-face inference of avatars' emotions) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise univariate activation maps. The paper includes a healthy adult control group (n=14, ages 18–45) with within-group (control) contrasts reported (Emotion vs Control; Table 2, Fig. 2) and between-group contrasts; results for the healthy group are presented separately with coordinates. Methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and voxelwise GLM (threshold p<0.001, cluster>12 voxels). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusions. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not restricted to non-adults, and not non-empirical).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (joint attention/theory-of-mind paradigm) in healthy adult participants (analyzed N=12; ages 20–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (body>place and place>body) with statistical maps and a table of activation regions (p<.01, cluster size threshold), and includes figures and group analyses derived from whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study does not rely solely on ROI-only analyses, connectivity-only analyses, or multivariate-only maps, nor is it a non-empirical or non-adult sample. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (interns and producers) that used task-based fMRI during a social-communication paradigm (encoding and recommending show ideas). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate analyses (random-effects) with voxelwise coordinates, tables, and figures (thresholds and MNI coordinates provided). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (pseudo-interactive joke task probing action-outcome contingency and self/other processing) in healthy adults (N=38, ages 19–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked contrasts (e.g., SELF vs OTHER, listener response contrasts, interaction effects) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction, and provides coordinates/tables and figures. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are triggered: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, not exclusively non-adult, and not purely multivariate. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables).

Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: subjects watched a socially awkward TV episode), I4 (healthy adult control group present). Inclusion not met: I5 (the paper does NOT report a whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group). The manuscript reports whole-brain maps collapsed across both groups and reports a between-group contrast (NT > ASD), but no unmasked NT-only whole-brain activation map. Per exclusion criterion E4 (studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect), this study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-cognitive processing (perspective taking/empathy for others), satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample comprises 18 healthy adult participants (ages 21–31), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports univariate, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Self vs Other; View-Pain vs View-No-Pain), second-level SPM analyses, cluster- and peak-level FWE corrections, conjunction analysis, and tables/figures of activation coordinates—providing whole-brain healthy-group results.
