Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, not outside the adult age range, and not non-empirical or MVPA-only. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore, include this study in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathic (social) decision-making (buying DVDs for others), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=32, mean age 22.8). The task probes perception/understanding of others and social processing (empathy/mentalizing), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate GLM analyses with cluster-level correction and tables/figures of activations (vmPFC, IPL, etc.), conjunctions and contrasts—i.e., whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group. Results are not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only (PPI is included but alongside univariate whole-brain results). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) Uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing (self- and mother-reflection vs celebrity; social cognition constructs); (2) Sample consists of healthy adult participants (Chinese college students; n=34 analyzed); (3) Reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (self- vs celebrity and mother- vs celebrity) with SPM analyses and tables of activations; (4) Whole-brain results are reported in text/tables and used for further analyses. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, genotyping, stimuli, imaging parameters, analysis), Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given the clear univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation contrasts from the healthy-group, this study should be included in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (political attitudes IAT) in healthy adult participants (final N=24, ages 21–40). The paper reports group-level, random-effects, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts and tables/figures of activation (including FDR-corrected whole-brain results and coordinate tables), and describes univariate subtraction and correlational analyses for the healthy group. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (joint attention) using gaze-contingent virtual characters. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=21) and results report group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activations (GLM analyses; activations in MPFC, PCC, anterior temporal poles are described, with voxel-level correction noted and figures of neural correlates provided). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition/analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the full-text appears complete. Therefore the paper satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and no exclusion criteria are met.

This paper uses fMRI during a social-perception task and includes a matched healthy adult control group (meets I3 and I4). However, the full text reports seed-based "background/intrinsic" connectivity (seed-based functional interaction) analyses and between-group connectivity contrasts and does not present any univariate, whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails to meet I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task activation) and I6. It matches exclusion criterion E3 (seed-based/resting/background connectivity only without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6. Exclusion criteria met: E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of face perception (a social cognition task: Perception and Understanding of Others). It includes a healthy adult sample (ages 18–37) and reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked analyses (faces > objects) with whole-brain maps and tables of coordinates (Table 3, figures). Whole-brain results are clearly described and reported for the healthy participant sample; figures/tables provide coordinate-based results. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study uses event-related fMRI during evaluative judgments linked to social cognition/theory-of-mind (satisfies I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (mean age ~26.4, n=7) reported separately (satisfies I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for the control group (one-sample t-test maps, thresholded maps, figures, and coordinate tables for evaluative judgment vs. semantic retrieval), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement (satisfies I5 and I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, figures, and tables, so the provided content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, only between-group contrasts without healthy-group maps, non-adult sample-only, multivariate-only maps, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This study reports an fMRI investigation of communicative speech (a social-communication task) in healthy adult participants (n=29, ages 18–24). The methods describe whole-brain, group-level random-effects SPM2 analyses and report voxelwise contrasts (communication vs description, familiar vs unfamiliar) with thresholding, figures of activation maps, and tables of activated cortical areas. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objectives (fMRI of social-related processing) and satisfies inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses task-based fMRI examining perception of dynamic head turns (a social-perception task), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (final analyzed sample: 17; ages 22–38), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain (gray matter–masked) univariate task-evoked statistical maps and peak coordinates (with SnPM nonparametric group analyses) and describes whole-brain results in text/tables/figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., results are not limited to ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not MVPA-only; univariate whole-brain contrasts are present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a social-related task (Dynamic Social Gesture) directly comparing social vs. nonsocial gestures, satisfying the social-processing requirement. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=20; mean age 21.4; range 16.9–25.7) and reports results for the healthy group separately; the minor inclusion of an age slightly below 18 is acceptable per protocol. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (TFCE with permutation testing) with figures and tables of activations for main effects and interactions, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Whole-brain results are presented in text/figures/tables. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of self-recognition (perception/understanding of self), a social-related process. Sample: healthy adults (n=35, ages 18–24) with analyses reported for the healthy group. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts are reported (tables, figures, cluster- and voxel-level inference described). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and imaging/statistical details.

This study uses an fMRI social-related task (PANSIT-MC) probing maternal response to child affect, so I3 is met. However, the sample includes only clinically depressed mothers (no healthy adult/control group reported or analyzed separately), therefore I4 is not met. Although whole-brain task maps are reported, they are for the clinical group rather than a healthy/control group, so I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) directly apply. Full text appears complete. Because the review requires at least one healthy adult group with whole-brain task-evoked maps, this study must be excluded.

The paper is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (dynamic virtual characters with direct vs averted gaze), reports results for a healthy adult control group separately, and presents whole-brain group-level task activation analyses for controls (full-factorial and within-group whole-brain results described in text, tables and figures). The full text includes introduction, methods, results (behavioral and whole-brain and ROI analyses), and discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, multivariate-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (facial emotion recognition and related non-emotional face judgments), includes a healthy adult control group (n=27), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation results for controls and within-group contrasts (whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using FSL Randomise; figures/tables and text describe control group activations). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

Full text incomplete: only abstract/metadata available (PDF not accessible). From abstract, I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample) appear satisfied. However I5 (reporting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task-evoked map) cannot be confirmed because core methods/results and whole-brain maps/tables are not available in the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are clearly met based on available info. Inclusion cannot be confirmed without full text, so exclude pending retrieval of full article. Recommend obtaining the PDF to verify I5/I6 before inclusion.

The paper examines fMRI during a social-related task (direct vs averted gaze) and includes a healthy adult control group; however, the current article reports seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity results (whole-brain PPI maps) and does not present an univariate, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group (main-effect or within-group task activation contrast) in the present manuscript. Thus it violates exclusion criterion E3 (reports only seed-based connectivity without also reporting a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I6 (acceptable reporting in supplement). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy group in this paper). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (action observation, mirror neuron and mentalizing systems), conducted in a healthy adult sample (N=19, ages 18–32). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task contrasts and corrected statistical maps; while main ROI-restricted results are emphasized, the manuscript states that whole-brain results and details about the mask are provided in the Supplemental Material (acceptable per I6). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, and sample is adult). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an fMRI study of social communication in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, the reported analyses are based on an ROI approach: parameter estimates extracted from predefined measuring points along the STS and one-sample t-tests across subjects. The paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or unmasked whole-brain contrast (no whole-brain coordinate table or voxelwise maps for the healthy group are presented). Therefore it fails to meet I5 (and by extension I6 is not satisfied). This violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses without whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (comparative judgments of physical attractiveness/beauty of other people), conducted in a healthy adult sample (25 right-handed British women, mean age 23.46). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation analyses (random-effects ANOVA, whole-brain thresholding, conjunctions, figures and tables of coordinates) and ROI analyses; whole-brain univariate contrasts are clearly reported for the healthy group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only without healthy-group task effects, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI task that explicitly probes social cognition (agency attribution/intentionality) using animated shapes (meets I3). The sample includes healthy adult participants (12 in fMRI; ages ~25; meets I4). The authors conducted second-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and report group-level contrasts (High>Low, Low>High) with reported activation loci and figures/tables (meets I5). Results are described in text and figures and thus satisfy the allowance for coordinate/figure reporting (meets I6). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are univariate whole-brain task activation contrasts (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not MVPA-only), sample is adult, and the paper is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (face emotion perception) in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper does not report a whole-brain, univariate task-evoked activation map for the healthy group (no group-level voxelwise activation contrast is presented); instead results focus on ROI-based FFA/amygdala signal changes and seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity maps. Because it reports only seed-based connectivity analyses without an accompanying whole-brain univariate healthy-group task activation map, it violates exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded for meta-analysis purposes due to E3.

This empirical fMRI study used a social-relevant task (viewing humorous cartoons; humor relates to social communication) in healthy adult participants (10 right-handed male subjects). Data were acquired and analyzed at the whole-brain level and the paper reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked results (coordinates and clusters for correlations between trait cheerfulness and BOLD response), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Results are reported as univariate group-level contrasts and tables/figures of coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social task probing affiliative/attachment-related scenarios (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (mean age ~27; N=27 final), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., affiliative vs nonaffiliative; whole-brain FWE-corrected results and tables/figures), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective and should be included.

This fMRI study examines prosocial decisions toward family, which is a social-related task involving mentalizing and self-control (affiliation/attachment and perception/understanding of others). Sample comprises 25 healthy adults (mean age 20.2), satisfying adult sample requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (Costly-Donation vs Noncostly-Reward) with tables of coordinates and whole-brain results, and reports PPI connectivity analyses additionally. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (viewing familiar vs. unfamiliar faces; partner/attachment and perception/understanding of others) with both a patient and an age-matched healthy control group. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate contrasts for the control group (coordinates and FWE cluster-corrected results are provided), satisfying the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked maps. The healthy sample (n=13, mean age 64.5) constitutes a healthy adult group reported separately. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/coordinates) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, MVPA-only, non-empirical, or wholly non-adult sample) are met. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, mean age 22) that explicitly investigates processing of communicative vs noncommunicative vocal signals—a social-communication task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (vocal > nonvocal; communicative > noncommunicative) thresholded with FDR and provides peak coordinates and whole-brain maps/figures. Methods, participants, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults. Full text appears complete (methods, results, figures/tables described). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a biological motion point-light paradigm, a social-perception task addressing ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’ (social-related processing). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (N=15; age range in adults) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and coordinates for the healthy/control group (see Table 2 and related figures) for the biological-motion versus scrambled-motion contrast. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, contains within-group healthy whole-brain maps).

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social perception (observation of touch on another's hand), satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (mean age 26, range 23–39; right-handed; N after exclusions = 20), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (random-effects analysis, p<0.05 FWE corrected), with coordinates, figures, and tabulated results, fulfilling whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting standards. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, not multivariate-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult college participants that used a social-related task (observation of others' goal-directed hand actions probing the mirror neuron system), addressing perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (one-sample within-group maps for alexithymia and non-alexithymia groups, conjunction analyses, and tables of coordinates), with corrected voxel/cluster thresholds and ROI follow-up. Healthy adult groups are reported separately (ALEX n=16, non-ALEX n=13). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not multivariate-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception of others’ eye gaze and identity), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=9, mean age 24). The study used whole-brain voxelwise analyses to identify face-responsive regions (clusters with z>4, cluster-size thresholding) and reports activation coordinates (Talairach/SPM) and task-evoked percent signal changes with group-level statistical comparisons across subjects (repeated-measures ANOVA; reported p-values). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Figures/Tables, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation reported), and I6 (coordinates/figures/tables reported). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses fMRI during a social-related task (voice perception, a form of social perception/understanding of others); (I4) reports a healthy adult control group (8 age-matched healthy male adults, reported separately from the autism group); (I5) provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results for the control group (voice > non-voice, random-effects analysis, P < 0.001 corrected); (I6) results are reported in text/figures and supplementary materials. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-group healthy whole-brain maps). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material is referenced but not required for inclusion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study where participants performed social evaluation/impression-formation tasks in the scanner. The sample includes a healthy young adult group (ages 20–29) satisfying the 18–65 requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects contrasts (social vs. non-social; social-meaningful vs. social-irrelevant), corrected maps, tables/figures, and conjunction analyses for the healthy groups. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (viewing social vs non-social scenes) (I3); sample consists of healthy adult participants (undergraduates aged 18–21) with results reported for the healthy group (I4); the paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts (social > non-social) with FDR-corrected maps and a table of results (I5,I6). The full text provided contains introduction, methods (fMRI and experience sampling), results (whole-brain contrast, ROIs, correlations), and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, multivariate-only, non-empirical, or non-adult-only issues).

This paper reports an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception/understanding of others’ emotional body gestures), meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (12 adult controls) reported separately alongside an ASD group, meeting I4. The manuscript provides group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation analyses for the control group (e.g., contrasts Fearful vs. Neutral, Dynamic vs. Static), thresholded statistical maps and tables of coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. The study also includes connectivity (DCM) analyses, but these are supplemental to and do not replace the univariate whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group maps, adult sample). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures description, references) is provided and appears complete.

This study should be excluded because it does not provide task-evoked fMRI results in a healthy adult group. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (the paper reports resting-state functional connectivity and seed/ROI connectivity analyses and effects of intranasal OT, not task-evoked whole-brain activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task—resting-state only), I4 (no healthy adult group reported separately—sample is adults with ASD only), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from a healthy/control group). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirements.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (recognition of others’ ‘vitality forms’), using task-based fMRI during social-action observation and explicit what/how tasks, satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample is healthy adults (n=19, ages 21–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked activation contrasts (e.g., what vs implicit baseline, how vs implicit baseline, how vs what) with voxelwise and cluster-level PFWE-corrected results; coordinates and figures/tables of activations are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not outside adult age range, not multivariate-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusions.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, mean age 26) investigating responses to empathic vs. unempathic verbal comments. The task is social in nature (processing empathic social responses; social cognition/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts with FWE-corrected clusters and tables/figures (univariate activation contrasts: e.g., EE>EN, CE>base, negative>positive feedback), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (intergroup competition, self-referential moral processing) in healthy adults (N=21, Mage=23.1), satisfying the review topic and sample criterion. The full text reports both ROI and whole-brain, group-level random-effects univariate analyses (cluster-corrected thresholds), with whole-brain results presented in tables/figures (Table 2 and Supplementary Fig. 1) and described in the text; therefore it provides qualifying whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. The article includes complete methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample) are met. Consequently, the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social impression formation in healthy adults. The task is social (impression formation of confederates; meets I3). Sample: N=19, mean age 19.1 (healthy adult participants reported), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts with coordinates and cluster-corrected thresholds (functional localizer contrast form-impression > sequencing with Talairach coordinates and cluster-correction; main task coordinates in Table 2), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, not non-adult sample only, not multivariate-only, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interaction task (live bidirectional conversation human–human vs human–robot), with healthy adult participants (n=21; mean age 25.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM full ANOVA; cluster-level FDR-corrected results are presented and neuroimaging maps deposited on NeuroVault/OpenNeuro). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets the review objective and inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly manipulates social interaction (cooperation vs. competition) during task performance. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (SPM analyses; cooperation vs. independent, competition vs. independent, and direct comparisons; results presented in tables and figures), and provides methods, results, and discussion for the healthy adult sample (N=12, ages 21–28). Full article content (introduction, methods, behavioral results, imaging acquisition/analysis, and discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult participants), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps/contrasts), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not multivariate-only, not non-empirical).

The study meets I3 (uses fMRI of social-related processing: face-matching fearful faces) and I4 (healthy adult sample: 15 males, mean age ~26.7). However, the paper reports group-level results using an amygdala ROI (statistical significance assessed with correction confined to the amygdala ROI) and reports connectivity analyses constrained to a brainstem ROI. The manuscript does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked activation map for the healthy group (or coordinates/figures that constitute whole-brain results beyond the ROI). Therefore it fails I5 and falls under exclusion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social interaction recognition that includes a healthy adult group (n=16; ages 20–41). The paper reports within-group whole-brain univariate contrasts (SI > NM) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster/FWE corrections and describes adult-group activations in text, figures, and tables. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for task-based fMRI on social processes, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, and discussion).

This study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses task-based fMRI of social perception) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). However, it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group; the primary whole-brain results are between-group contrasts (HC vs schizophrenia) and subsequent analyses are ROI-based follow-ups derived from those between-group clusters. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text incomplete: only abstract/metadata/PDF notice provided. The abstract indicates two fMRI experiments on understanding intentions in social interaction, so I3 (use of fMRI during a social-related task) is met. However, participant/sample details (to confirm a healthy adult group; I4) are not presented, and no methods or results are available to verify that at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group is reported (I5) or that reporting format criteria are met (I6). Because all inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the available content, the study must be excluded at this stage. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) can be confidently applied based on the truncated content.

The study uses task-based fMRI of a social-related paradigm (interpersonal pleasant touch) and reports behavioral and neural responses to social reward (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (age 18-35) with results reported separately from the cannabis-dependent group (I4). The manuscript provides whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation results for the control group (e.g., TOUCH > CLOSE and FEMALE > MALE contrasts), with cluster coordinates and corrected statistics reported in the text and supplementary materials (Figure S1, Table S1), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5, I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material is referenced but not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not restricted to non-adult sample, not multivariate-only, and is empirical). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This paper reports task-based fMRI during a social-related imitate/observe task (imitating/observing emotional faces). The sample includes a healthy adult group (discovery: 70 healthy controls, ages 18–55; replication: 39 healthy controls). The authors performed whole-brain, second-level general linear model analyses (imitate > observe) with family-wise error correction and threshold-free cluster enhancement, and state that group-level analyses were run separately for each site and group; group activation maps are described in the main text and supplementary figures/tables. Whole-brain univariate task-evoked results are therefore available and clearly attributable to the healthy/control participants. Thus the study satisfies the review’s requirements for an fMRI social task in healthy adults with whole-brain within-group results.

This study reports task-based fMRI of facial emotion processing (a social cognition task: perception/understanding of others), includes a healthy control group reported separately (31 controls, age range 16–40, which is acceptable under the review age policy), and presents whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation results for the healthy/control group (paired and one-sample t-tests; control-group activations reported in Table 3 and supplemental materials; maps thresholded at p<0.05 FWE). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and therefore appears complete. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (Theory of Mind and empathy cartoon task), tested in a healthy adult sample (N=13; ages 19–36). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using SPM2 (random-effects one-sample t tests), thresholded and presented as statistical maps and tables of activation coordinates and figures. Results for the healthy group are reported separately and include within-group contrasts and conjunction/interaction analyses. Reporting includes tables of foci and figures, satisfying acceptable reporting formats. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and does not involve only non-adult or clinical-only samples. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is present in the provided text.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (implicit interpersonal/affiliation task comparing social vs. non-social stimuli) in healthy adult participants (male, age 19–30). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task analyses (main effects and interaction: right medial frontal gyrus, left ACC/culmen, right dorsal striatum) and describes thresholds/methods and ROI follow-ups; results are reported for the healthy/control group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The paper uses task fMRI of social simulation/empathy (meets I3) and reports a healthy adult control group (meets I4). Whole-brain task activation is reported in tables/figures for the sample (so reporting format is acceptable per I6). However, the manuscript does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone; whole-brain results are reported for the full sample (HC+SZ) and between-group contrasts showed no significant differences. Thus it does not meet I5. Exclusion criterion E4 applies (no accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it lacks a clearly-identified healthy-group whole-brain activation map.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a social cognition task (an fMRI adaptation of the Movie for the Assessment of Social Cognition; Theory of Mind task), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adults (n=18 included in analyses; ages 20–45), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked GLM contrasts for the healthy group (e.g., ToM vs. PI; Table 1, cluster thresholds, and coordinate reporting), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. Although the study also includes model-free T-PICA analyses, univariate whole-brain GLM maps are present. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates an fMRI study of social inference, so I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) appears satisfied. However, critical details required for inclusion cannot be verified: the sample characteristics/ages for a healthy adult group (I4) are not clearly reported in the abstract, and it is unclear whether the paper reports at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (I5). Because these inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the provided content, the study is excluded pending access to the complete full text. fulltext_incomplete=true.

Exclusion E2 applies: the fMRI results reported are ROI-based (bilateral amygdala) correlations within a patient subsample (N=25). While the study includes an fMRI task using social-phobia related words (I3) and includes healthy adult participants in the overall sample (I4), it does not report any group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain voxelwise result) is not met. No whole-brain healthy-group activation maps (tables/figures/coords) are provided; reported imaging results are patient-only and ROI-focused. Full text appears complete (not truncated).

This is an original fMRI study of social processing: participants (N=23, ages 21–43) performed a social judgment (dominance) task during fMRI (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adults reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrast (Social Judgment > Perceptual Judgment) with thresholding and a table of peak coordinates and cluster sizes (meets I5 and I6). Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, tables/figures) is present and sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or multivariate-only restrictions).

This study reports task-based fMRI during social-related tasks (approachability and intelligence judgements from faces), includes a healthy adult sample (47 healthy controls; results for controls reported separately from the ASD group), and presents group-level, whole-brain univariate activation contrasts for the healthy/control groups (within-group ‘social vs gender’ contrasts with SPM thresholds and cluster-level correction; figures and coordinates are reported). Reporting of whole-brain maps is clear in text/figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not restricted to non-adults, not multivariate-only, and is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study meets all inclusion criteria. I3: It uses task-based fMRI probing social-related processing (perception/discrimination of affective vocalisations — social communication/perception of others). I4: The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=19, mean age 25.9). I5: The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (the species contrast human>chimpanzee>macaque) with mixed-effects group analysis (FLAME). I6: Whole-brain results are reported as figures and MNI coordinates in tables. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical limitations). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study used event-related fMRI during an implicit facial emotion processing task (social perception), includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (n=9, ages within 18–65), and reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise and clusterwise) activation maps and tables/figures for the control group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of communicative speech (social communication) in healthy adults, reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., COM vs DES; L2 vs L1) analyzed with SPM5 and reported with cluster- and voxel-wise thresholds and coordinates. Sample: 27–30 healthy native Japanese adults (mean age 23.35), within 18–65. The paper provides full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task: social communication), I4 (healthy adult participants), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (results described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of third-party punishment, a social-cognitive/legal decision task (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 26) with results reported for this healthy group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (Experimental > Control) using whole-brain FDR correction and parametric modulation, with coordinates and figures/tables described (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply: the study includes univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside adulthood, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-related task (guilt memories vs hypothetical social scenarios). The sample comprises healthy adult students (mean age 25.7; 20 scanned). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., guilt memories > neutral memories; thresholded at p<0.001, extent 23 voxels) and describes coordinates, figures, and ROI SVCs. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making (Ultimatum Game) that includes a healthy adult group (ages 19–28) and reports group-level whole-brain univariate task activation contrasts. The paper presents one-sample t-tests for each group and full-factorial ANOVAs and post-hoc t-tests on the unfair–fair contrast, with thresholded voxelwise maps and regions reported (tables/figures). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study of self- and other-referential processing in healthy adults meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI for social-related constructs (self/other perception), includes a healthy adult sample (20 women aged 18–52), and reports group-level whole-brain univariate task activation results (tables/figures and voxelwise contrasts described). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-adult sample, and reports univariate whole-brain contrasts).

This study uses simultaneous PET-fMRI to examine maternal bonding in healthy adult mothers and reports PET task-evoked dopamine contrasts (own vs unfamiliar infant) and seed-based intrinsic (resting-state) connectivity of the medial amygdala network. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (functional MRI used during a social/affiliation task context) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 21–42). However, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked fMRI activation map for the healthy group; the fMRI analyses focus on intrinsic/seed-based connectivity (resting-state) rather than task-evoked whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. Therefore exclusion criterion E3 applies (only seed-based/resting-state connectivity reported without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Full text appears complete.

The study meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: audiovisual speech/speech perception/social communication) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group with results reported). However, it does NOT provide an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. The paper reports a whole-brain main effect of audiovisual congruency across both groups and reports group-by-congruency interaction maps (with beta-weights by group extracted), but it does not present a standalone whole-brain healthy-group task map or within-group whole-brain contrast for controls. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=17, ages 18–27) that investigates social processing (responses to an emergency/bystander effect). The methods describe task-evoked BOLD acquisition and preprocessing, and group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric and contrast maps) with results reported in tables/figures. These meet inclusion I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not a between-group-only contrast, not developmental/geriatric-only, not MVPA-only, and not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study used action observation/execution paradigms probing mirror-system responses—directly relevant to social cognition (perception/understanding of others). It tested healthy adult participants (n=21, mean age 24) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses. In addition to ROI analyses, the authors explicitly conducted and reported whole-brain analyses (threshold p<0.001 uncorrected) with peak coordinates and tables, satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group, whole-brain task-evoked map. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study satisfies I3 and I4: it uses task-based fMRI of a social-related process (direct vs. averted gaze) and reports data from a healthy adult sample (N=55 males). However, the neuroimaging results are reported as ROI analyses (amygdala and inferior occipital gyrus masks) with FWE correction within those ROIs and no unmasked, voxelwise whole-brain group-level task activation map or whole-brain coordinate results for the healthy group are presented. Thus it does not meet I5 (whole-brain evidence) and falls under exclusion criterion E2 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses task-based fMRI during theory-of-mind narratives and MVPA to probe social cognition (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (ages and sample sizes reported; meets I4). The paper reports task-evoked contrasts used for a theory-of-mind localizer (Belief > Photo) and references group/whole-brain localizer results (Fig. S1 / supplementary materials) used to define ROIs, indicating availability of whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group (meets I5). Reporting of whole-brain results in figures/supplementary is acceptable per I6. The full text provided includes methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (emotion identification and attribution) in healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task — Why/How emotion comprehension task), I4 (healthy adult sample: N=22, ages 19–32; results reported for healthy group), I5 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts such as How>Why and Why>How with statistical thresholds and Tables of coordinates), I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables and figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or MVPA-only reporting). Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study examines social touch (self- vs other-touch) using a task that manipulates social touch (social-related processing). It includes a healthy adult control group (neurotypical controls; ages in adult range) with results reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps for the control group (e.g., 'Other-touch in NC' and 'self-touch in NC') with family-wise-error correction at the whole-brain level and describes whole-brain analyses in the methods and results. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not pediatric/geriatric-only, and not non-empirical).

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It uses task-based functional MRI during a social-related perception task (biological motion; I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=26 analyzed; ages 18–39), meeting the adult healthy-sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses: whole-brain analyses of biological-motion selectivity and correlations with social-network diversity yielded a significant cluster in right pSTS/TPJ with correction for multiple comparisons (reported in the supplemental figure/tables), satisfying the requirement for a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (I5). Reporting of whole-brain results in supplemental material is acceptable (I6). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., this is not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age 20) performing social cognition tasks (inferring vegetable preferences and age judgments about social group members), satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. The paper presents group-level, random-effects, whole-brain univariate contrasts (task main effect and social-group-member main effect) with reported voxelwise statistics, cluster sizes, and Talairach coordinates in text/tables/figures, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-adult sample, not multivariate-only, and is empirical). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study examines social cognition (linking person perception and person knowledge) using an event-related task pairing bodies/names with trait/neutral statements—clearly a social-related task. Sample: 21 healthy adult participants (mean age 24.6) with exclusions reported; meets healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (main effects and interaction) and PPI connectivity results, with tables of coordinates and figures; whole-brain voxelwise results are clearly described. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not merely abstract/metadata). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without whole-brain activation, between-group-only, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=78 analyzed; mean ages ~24–26) using a social/moral narrative task (reading personal narratives assessing perceived protected values), meeting the review objective of social-related processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., reading stories vs baseline; protected-values vs non-protected stories) with cluster correction and ROI analyses derived from resting-state but the main task effects are whole-brain voxelwise GLM results described in the text and figures/tables. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This record is a non-empirical review article (Article in Japanese) and does not report original fMRI data from healthy adult participants. Exclusion E7 applies. None of the inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during a social task) not met; I4 (healthy adult sample reported) not met; I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked map) not met; I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results) not met. Full text appears incomplete here (only abstract/metadata), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (emotion perception/integration), using whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses and reporting voxelwise contrasts and conjunctions (FDR-corrected) from a healthy adult sample (N=24, ages 18–34). The paper provides full methods, results, figures, and tables with whole-brain activation maps and coordinates for group-level task contrasts (congruent vs incongruent AV, AV > A/V, etc.). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps from healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study that includes a social decision-making task (altruism task varying self vs other payoffs), satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adults (N=55 for altruism, subset N=37 for food) within the adult age range, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses: whole-brain searchlight MVPA decoding maps (FWE cluster-corrected) and also references conventional univariate analyses (Appendix) and specific whole-brain univariate contrasts (e.g., decision-value results reported with FWE cluster correction); derived univariate and multivariate statistical maps are available on the OSF, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state only, only between-group contrasts, MVPA-only without univariate maps, non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI experiment of social communication where healthy adult participants (n=37, mean age 25) made social judgments (feeling addressed). The study reports group-level whole-brain univariate task contrasts (main effects and interactions) with voxel coordinates, cluster correction and figures/tables, clearly from the healthy sample. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social perception (animacy, action observation, mentalizing) using a task where participants observed agents and rated the stimuli—fits social-related processing. Sample: 23 healthy adult participants (age mean 26.4) reported separately—meets the healthy adult sample requirement. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task contrasts are reported (voxel-wise threshold p<0.005, cluster reports, coordinate tables and figures), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are described in text and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, MRI acquisition, analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) are met.

Full text is incomplete: provided content contains only an empty body tag and lacks Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore I cannot verify that the study used task-based fMRI for a social-related task (I3), that it reports a healthy adult group (I4), or that it provides whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the healthy group (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria from the list can be confirmed from the available information. Because core article content is missing, the study must be excluded pending a complete full text. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4, I5, I6. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is an fMRI study of self/other social-referential processing in healthy adults (N=18, ages 19–29). It reports group-level task-evoked whole-brain analyses (conjunctions and whole-brain FWE-corrected activations) and provides coordinate tables and detailed methods/results for the healthy control group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported via coordinates/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, MVPA-only, non-empirical, or non-adult-only issues).

This article reports task-based fMRI including a social cognition contrast (TOM vs Random) appropriate to social-related processing (I3). The sample comprises a large healthy adult cohort (n=787; ages 22–>35) meeting the healthy adult sample requirement (I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and descriptions (Cohen's d and z maps, cluster tables, figures), clearly identified as healthy-group results (I5/I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, figures, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are univariate task activations (not only ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only, MVPA-only), and the study is empirical. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=41, ages 18–24) that uses task-based fMRI during decisions to select and share news articles—a social-related task engaging self- and other-processing (sharing with a friend vs. broadcasting). The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate contrasts (select > content, share > content, share > select) with family-wise error correction and tables/figures of activations, and also reports ROI and whole-brain results and parametric modulation by preference ratings. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not multivariate-only, and the sample is adult). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates perception of social interactions using task-based fMRI. It reports scans of healthy adult participants (n=14, ages 20–32) and provides group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (e.g., interaction > independent point-light contrast) with reported MNI coordinates and figures, as well as univariate contrasts and MVPA—all clearly described for the healthy/control group. The full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not a between-group-only contrast, not outside the adult age range, and not non-empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (take-advice and trust games) in healthy adults (N=31, mean age 24.3). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task-evoked activation contrasts (e.g., honesty vs. dishonesty; value contrasts; whole-brain FWE-corrected results and Supplementary Tables) and also provides coordinate tables and GLM details. The methods and results sections are present and complete. Therefore it satisfies I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not multivariate-only, not non-empirical, not outside adult range).

This fMRI study investigates social processing (perception of fearful facial expressions with gaze direction) using a task that probes social attention/understanding of others. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=22) reported separately, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses for the control group (within-group contrasts such as AVERTED>DIRECT and DIRECT>FIXATION) with corrected statistics and figures. Full methods, results, and discussion are provided in the full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Full text incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion met: I3 (study uses fMRI in a social-related task—gaze/face processing). Inclusion not met / cannot be confirmed from provided content: I4 (participant sample explicitly identified as healthy adults 18–65 and reported separately) and I5 (presence of at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map clearly reported for the healthy/control group). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) can be confirmed from the available material. Cannot verify whole-brain univariate results or participant details without full text; therefore excluded pending retrieval of the complete article.

Although the study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI activation maps in healthy adult participants (meets I5) and includes a healthy adult sample (meets I4) with whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables (meets I6), the task is a word/pseudoword repetition paradigm focused on speech production and RT-correlated activity rather than social processing per se. The experiment does not investigate social-related constructs (e.g., affiliation, social communication in an interpersonal context, perception/understanding of others or self) and thus does not satisfy I3. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are triggered by the manuscript. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I3 (social-related task).

The full text reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=12, ages 22–37) using a social auditory task (listening to footsteps of one vs. two people) that probes social perception/mentalizing. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results with voxelwise statistical maps and Talairach coordinates (figures and tables of coordinates are reported) for contrasts of interest (e.g., STEP1+STEP2 – REST; STEP2 – NOISE2; STEP1 – NOISE1). The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections, so the full text appears complete. This satisfies I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinates/figures acceptable). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not pediatric/geriatric-only, not MVPA-only, and is empirical).

This paper reports an fMRI study of communicative (social) speech production in healthy adults. It uses task-based, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM) with reported group-level contrasts, coordinates, tables, and figures, and describes thresholds and preprocessing. Sample: healthy native Japanese adults (n=27 included in imaging analyses; ages 19–31) satisfying adult age range. The task is explicitly social communication (communicative vs. descriptive speech). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported as tables/figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI task study of social-related processing (attentional orienting to social gaze vs arrow cues with social voice vs tone targets), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=22, mean age ~23). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts (main effects and interactions) with whole-brain and small-volume-corrected results, and provides coordinate tables and ROI analyses. Full article (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using the Reading the Mind in the Eyes task, a social-perception/theory-of-mind paradigm (social understanding of others). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (native Japanese and white American, ages 18–27) with group-level analyses reported. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., RME − GD; same- vs. other-culture contrasts) with tables of activations, thresholds, and ROI/conjunction analyses, clearly identified as coming from the healthy groups. Full article contains methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-affective video task (SoVT) depicting people in distress, directly probing social-related processing (affiliation/response to others’ suffering). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=15, ages 45–62). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Compassion > Watch-Negative; Reappraisal > Watch-Negative) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides tables/figures of results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, sample is adult, and univariate whole-brain activation contrasts are reported. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans (45 men, 45 women; ages 18–22) using a social interaction paradigm (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) that probes affiliation/ social processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (e.g., whole-brain contrasts showing VTA attenuation in women, amygdala effects in men) and applies appropriate voxelwise and FWE cluster thresholds; results are reported in text and figures. The full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the cyberball social interaction task (social exclusion/inclusion/control) with whole-brain univariate analyses. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (20 adults) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain task-evoked effects and within-group post hoc comparisons for the healthy control group, and indicates t-contrasts are reported in the Supplementary Data. Results are reported as whole-brain clusters and peak voxels in main text/tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult group), I5 (whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results identified for healthy group), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social attribution (why/how task) in healthy adults (N=19, ages 21–46). The task probes perception/understanding of others (theory of mind/folk explanations), satisfying relevance to social-related processing. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (one-sample t tests, conjunctions, cluster-level correction FWE p<.05) and presents whole-brain results/tables and figures (e.g., Table 2, whole-brain conjunction maps). Healthy adult group results are reported separately. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are met.

This is an fMRI study that implements a social working memory task (social cognition: ranking friends on trait dimensions) and reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps with coordinates and cluster thresholds. The sample consists of healthy adults (n=16; mean age 20), satisfying the adult healthy sample requirement. Whole-brain, random-effects group analyses are described (parametric modulators, coordinates for DMPFC, TPJ, DLPFC, etc.; tables/figures referenced), meeting the requirement for univariate whole-brain healthy-group task effects. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete.

The study reports fMRI data collected during a social-related task (animated human face producing non-verbal vocalizations) addressing social perception/communication, satisfying I3. The fMRI group sample comprises healthy adults within the 18–65 range (fMRI: ages 24–37; ERP: 19–43), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxel-by-voxel two-tailed t tests, percent signal change maps versus rest, AV versus ApV contrasts, cluster correction via AlphaSim) and presents group activation maps and contrasts, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, and not MVPA-only).

The study is excluded because it reports only seed-based effective connectivity analyses (gPPI) and group comparisons without presenting any univariate, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group. This meets exclusion criterion E3. The paper does use fMRI with social-relevant stimuli (faces/emotional valence) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 are satisfied), but it does not provide the required whole-brain healthy-group task activation map (I5 is not met). Full text is complete and supplementary material is not required for this decision.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI experiment probing social cognition (acquired moral status via cooperative/defective behavior) during a task (gender judgments of previously learned cooperator/defector faces). Participants were healthy adults (scanned N=11, ages 21–36). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (random-effects one-sample t tests across the 11 subjects) with tables of coordinates and ROI/whole-brain thresholding described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, paradigm, MRI acquisition/analysis), Results (behavioral and neuroimaging effects with coordinate tables), and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a longitudinal fMRI trial in patients with early-course schizophrenia (CET vs EST). It does not include a healthy adult group, and the task used (Preparing to Overcome Prepotency) probes cognitive control, not social-related processing. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), and I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task map) are not met. Exclusion criterion E4 applies because the paper reports only between-patient-group contrasts/interactions (CET vs EST) without any unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. Full text appears complete.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment using a standard Theory of Mind (social cognition) paradigm (FB vs FP), meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=25; ages 18–59) reported separately and matched to patients. The paper describes and uses whole-brain group-level contrasts (e.g., FB > FP) and explicitly states that control-group functional localisations (FB > FP) were generated and used to create masks, indicating availability of whole-brain univariate task activation maps from the healthy group. Results are reported in the main text with figures/tables (and supplementary data), satisfying acceptable reporting formats. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (own vs other child; appropriate vs inappropriate child behavior), satisfying I3. Participants are adult mothers (scanned 16 years after initial child assessment), meeting the adult sample requirement (I4). The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (voxel-by-voxel multiple regression, random-effects group analyses) and presents significant activations in whole-brain contrasts (figures/ROI coordinates), meeting I5 and the acceptable reporting formats in I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) are met. Note: sample is small and somewhat heterogeneous, but this does not violate inclusion criteria. Given these points, the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants imagined encountering neutral faces in goal-relevant versus goal-irrelevant social situations while undergoing fMRI. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=17 analyzed; ages 20–36). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts (encoding and recognition), with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinates reported in tables/figures and small-volume corrections described. Behavioural and neuroimaging methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, multivariate-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating visual sensitivity to social spatial relations (face-to-face vs back-to-back body dyads), which falls squarely under social perception/Perception and Understanding of Others. The fMRI sample consists of healthy adults (n=20, mean age 24.1) meeting the adult age criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (e.g., dyads > single bodies; facing > nonfacing dyads) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction, plus tables/figures of activations and peak coordinates. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). None of the exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply: the study includes whole-brain univariate analyses (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or MVPA-only), reports within-group healthy subject effects (not only between-group contrasts), involves adults, and is an empirical report. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI probing social-related processing (perception of emotional crowds and interactions); (I4) healthy adult sample reported separately (16 right-handed participants aged 19–27); (I5) reports group-level whole-brain univariate analyses (random-effects ANOVAs) with cluster-corrected results and tables of coordinates; (I6) whole-brain results are presented in tables and figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not MVPA-only, and the sample is adult. The provided full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and acknowledgments). Therefore include.
