This paper reports a task-based fMRI study of theory-of-mind/social cognition (social communication/understanding of others), includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group (12 right-handed healthy subjects, mean age 24.75), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation results for the control group (ANOVA contrasts, tables of coordinates, figures). Whole-brain contrasts for controls versus the physical causality baseline and condition-specific within-group activations are reported and tabulated. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only analyses, no connectivity-only or resting-state-only analyses, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are reported).

This fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses functional MRI during a social-related mentalizing task (I3), tested a healthy adult sample (final N=28 imaging participants, ages 18–22) (I4), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results. Specifically, the paper presents a whole-brain searchlight representational similarity map (medial PFC) with TFCE-corrected thresholds and a voxelwise repetition-suppression (univariate parametric modulation) group-level t-test showing effects in posterior precuneus (both corrected p < 0.05), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps (I5, I6). Although multivariate (RSA/searchlight) analyses are reported, the study additionally provides an univariate, group-level repetition-suppression map, so it does not fall under exclusion E6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore, include this study in the review.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-related task (emotional face recognition). The sample is healthy adult males (n=116, mean age 24.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (e.g., FWE-corrected voxelwise contrasts for fearful>neutral, whole-brain regression with AQ predicting amygdala response), clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, not non-empirical, and sample is adult). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is an event-related fMRI study of processing anger prosody (a social-communication cue) using a dichotic-listening task—clearly a social-related task. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 24.4). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses (contrasts, MNI coordinates, cluster-level correction for OFC) and presents brain maps/coordinates in text and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not developmental or non-empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social processing (empathy/valuation of others’ emotional facial expressions) in healthy adults. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with described contrasts (e.g., PERCEPTION OF EMOTION vs CONTROL, SHARED EMOTION) and statistical thresholds, and describes activation loci and conversion of MNI to Talairach coordinates, indicating whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy sample. Sample consists of 14 healthy adult participants (mean age ~29), meeting the age range. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults that reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts. The task involves learning about other people’s generosity (social condition) and a matched non-social control; participants are healthy adults (ages 19–37). The paper presents whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and tables/figures of activation (e.g., contrasts Gifter > Lottery, conjunctions, parametric effects), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present.

This is an fMRI study of social perception (voice-based identity and emotion recognition), meeting the social-related task requirement (I3). The sample includes healthy adult participants (sighted controls; and congenitally blind participants) with results reported for the healthy adult group (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise univariate task-evoked statistical maps and cluster tables (e.g., main effects, interaction maps; figures and Tables 2–4), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I5) and allows maps reported in figures/tables (I6). Although multivariate analyses are also reported, the paper includes univariate, group-level activation contrasts, so no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study tests social tasks (theory-of-mind and social attribution) with fMRI in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper’s task-evoked results are derived from localized group-level ICA applied to a TPJ-region-of-interest mask and subsequent IC maps; no univariate, whole-brain group-level task activation contrast/map for the healthy group is reported. The paper primarily presents ROI-limited activation maps and seed-to-voxel connectivity maps (connectivity does not satisfy the required whole-brain task-evoked activation criterion). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only task analyses with no whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level task-evoked map). Exclusion criteria applied: E2.

This fMRI study directly investigates social-related processing (self- and other-reflection), meeting the review’s construct domain (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=33) reported separately from the schizophrenia group (I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation results for the control group (e.g., Self>Facts, Other>Facts, Other>Self contrasts) with figures and supplementary tables of activation (I5,I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, non-adult samples, or multivariate-only maps) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This item is a non-empirical, theoretical/review paper (title and abstract only) discussing explanatory accounts of mirror-touch synesthesia; no original fMRI data or participant methods/results are reported in the provided full text. Exclusion criteria met: E7 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task reported), I4 (no healthy adult sample reported or separable healthy-group results), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), I6 (no whole-brain results in tables/figures/supplementary). Additionally, the provided content is incomplete (only abstract/metadata), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (N=16, ages 25–49) that used whole-brain, voxelwise analyses to examine synchronization of brain activity across participants while they viewed affect-laden movie clips. The task probes social-related processing (perception and understanding of others’ emotions; includes empathy measures). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain ISC maps and GLM analyses linking valence/arousal to voxelwise ISC (permutation testing and FDR correction) presented in figures and supplemental tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps from healthy group), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not multivariate-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=31, ages 18–35) using a social perception task (gender judgment of faces with/without disfigurement), directly addressing social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). It presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (pre- vs post-surgery faces) analyzed with SnPM and familywise-error correction and reports cluster results and figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants that examines observation and interpretation of another person’s actions (Imagine/Evaluate tasks), addressing social-cognitive processes (perception/understanding of others, intention attribution). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8 random-effects second-level contrasts, FDR-corrected maps, and coordinate tables/figures) clearly attributable to the healthy adult groups. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (humor processing, which involves social cognition/theory-of-mind and emotion) (I3); reports a healthy adult sample (29 right-handed adults, mean age 27, sexes reported) (I4); presents group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation results (Cartoons vs. Neutral and parametric modulation contrasts) with second-level analyses and correction procedures, and provides coordinate tables/figures (I5,I6). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Tables/figures descriptions, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effects). Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study reports an event-related fMRI task probing understanding of others' actions (auditory mirror system)—a social-related construct (Perception and Understanding of Others). It uses healthy adult participants (n=11 in fMRI subgroup, ages 21–29). Whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses are reported (voxelwise contrasts, cluster correction, tables/figures of activations and coordinates). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not developmental/geriatric, not MVPA-only, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a clearly social task (Social Context Decision Task; participants imagine decisions accompanied by a peer), meeting I3. The sample includes a separate healthy adult group (21–22 years) reported separately from adolescents, meeting I4. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Regret>Disappointment, Disappointment>Elation) with cluster results and coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. The provided full text contains methods, results, and discussion (not just abstract), so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply.

The provided full text appears to be an abstract only and lacks key methodological details. Inclusion: I3 is met—the study used fMRI during a task involving perception/understanding of others’ actions (social-related processing). Not met / cannot verify: I4 (sample details: healthy adult participants not specified in the provided text) and I5 (no clear report in the excerpt of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map; results mention region effects but full methods/results and statistical maps are not provided). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are explicitly triggered based on the available content. Because core information necessary to confirm eligibility (participant sample and whole-brain group results) is missing and the full text is incomplete, I exclude this record pending access to the complete article.

This fMRI study tests collective/social memory representations in healthy adults (N=24, ages 22–39) and explicitly links dmPFC activity to social/collective frameworks. It reports ROI RSA results and a whole-brain searchlight (group-level TFCE-corrected) mapping of model-related effects. However, the paper does not report a conventional univariate, task-evoked group activation contrast (e.g., recall > baseline or other univariate task maps). The only whole-brain maps are multivariate (searchlight/RSA-derived beta maps). Per the review’s exclusion rule E6, studies whose only whole-brain healthy-group results are multivariate maps without an accompanying univariate group-level task-evoked activation contrast must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study addresses social-related constructs/collective memory), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps via searchlight RSA), I6 (results reported in figures/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: None (all applicable inclusion criteria were satisfied). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only multivariate/maps without a univariate activation map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (learning to simulate others' decisions) in healthy participants. It uses task-based fMRI during a social ‘Other’ task that probes perception/understanding of others (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult subjects (n=36 analyzed; 39 recruited), reported as healthy/normal participants (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with corrected results and tables of activated clusters (Tables 1 and 2) and whole-brain regression analyses (I5, I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, pediatric/geriatric-only, multivariate-only, or non-empirical. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=22, mean age 24) using social-cognitive tasks (mind perception and gaze-cueing), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Whole-brain, group-level univariate voxelwise analyses are reported (parametric regressors, cluster-based correction at whole-brain level) with tables/figures describing significant clusters (e.g., vmPFC, TPJ, fusiform), fulfilling the whole-brain results requirement. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, multivariate-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable to include in the meta-analysis of task-evoked fMRI of social processing in healthy adults.

This fMRI study investigates social-related processing using dynamic first-person video stimuli (reactive-aggressive, social-positive, neutral), satisfying the social-task requirement. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=20; mean age 24.6), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., reactive–aggressive vs. neutral; p<.05 FDR-corrected) with tables of coordinates and figures, meeting whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample-only, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) are triggered. Recommended for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It uses task-based fMRI during prosodic speech perception (social communication/prosody — a social-related construct) in adults (I3). The sample includes a separate healthy adult control group (n=8) with results reported independently (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses for each group (one-sample t-tests for controls and HFA, conjunctions, and between-group contrasts) with voxelwise thresholds and anatomical localization (i.e., whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps clearly identified as coming from the control group) (I5). Whole-brain results are described in the text/tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-state-only, or missing healthy-group whole-brain maps) apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an fMRI task explicitly probing social-related processing (empathy for pain/pleasure toward human vs robot), uses a healthy adult sample (N=26, ages 18–27), and presents group-level whole-brain random-effects task analyses (cluster-corrected results; whole-brain maps available via NeuroVault/OSF). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of observation and motor imagery of buccofacial and upper-limb movements (social gestures), addressing social communication/perception constructs. Sample: healthy adult participants (14 right-handed males, mean age ~25), reported separately and analyzed. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task-evoked analyses (ANOVA, conjunctions, main effects) with FWE-corrected thresholds and MNI coordinates in tables and figures, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not developmental/geriatric-only, and is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study should be excluded because it does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked univariate activation map for the healthy adult task contrast. The paper reports ROI-based MVPA and percent signal (ROI) univariate analyses and uses a separate group localiser to define ROIs, but I find no clear whole-brain group-level task activation map or voxelwise univariate contrast from the healthy adult experimental task. Exclusion criteria met: E2 (only ROI analyses / no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: perception of others/facial expression), I4 (healthy adult sample, n=24, ages within 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=23, mean age ~24) that investigates social communication/intent understanding (communicative vs private intentions). It reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task contrasts (e.g., CInt > PInt, interaction effects) with voxelwise thresholding and tables/figures of activation coordinates, as well as PPI connectivity analyses. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social communication between healthy adult participants (N=54, ages 18–27). The task is explicitly social/communicative and uses task-evoked BOLD fMRI recorded simultaneously in pairs. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (cluster-level corrected) identifying right superior temporal gyrus and other whole-brain contrasts tied to the task and behavioral dynamics. Whole-brain results are reported in the text and methods. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, nonadult sample only, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) apply.

Meets all inclusion requirements: (I3) Uses fMRI during a social-related task (delegated inter-temporal choice; learning about and evaluating others’ preferences, i.e., perception/understanding of others/social influence). (I4) Sample comprises healthy adult participants (fMRI sample n=29, ages within adult range; exclusions reported separately). (I5) Reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked univariate contrasts (whole-brain random-effects analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and peak coordinates in mPFC, visual cortex, STS, etc.). (I6) Whole-brain results are reported with coordinates and statistical maps described in the text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and not MVPA-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of maternal neural responses to infant cry—a social/attachment-related task—conducted in adult participants (mothers mean age 24.1). The paper reports univariate, group-level, whole-brain analyses (own cry > control; own cry > other) using FLAME with whole-brain FDR correction and provides cluster coordinates and thresholding details (i.e., whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported for the sample). Although the sample included participants with prior perinatal depression and a few on SSRI medication, none met criteria for current major depressive episode at assessment, and analyses examined/controlled for depressive symptoms; the healthy adult group results are reported for the cohort. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This empirical paper reports fMRI during social-related tasks (charitable giving and an independent EmpaToM task addressing empathy and perspective taking), includes a healthy adult sample (n=33, ages 20–34), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses/contrasts (GLM3 group t-tests for EmpaToM contrasts; GLM5/GLM6 univariate analyses are described, and whole-brain searchlight decoding and tables of clusters/coordinates are reported). Results for the healthy/control group are reported and described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E2–E7).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes), includes a healthy adult control group (n=25; ages within 18–59), and presents whole-brain, group-level task activation results for the healthy/control group (described in text and Supplementary Table S2) with appropriate whole-brain correction. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that uses a social-related task (reading passages varying in social content) during task-evoked fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain random-effects contrasts (Social > Non-social; Vivid > Abstract) with cluster-corrected maps and peak coordinates/tables. Sample: 26 healthy adults (age 19–26). Behavioral ToM measures also reported and related to neural activity. The paper includes whole-brain voxelwise results (figures and tables), satisfying the requirement for univariate group-level activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical, and sample is adult). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Meets all inclusion criteria: fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about others) using task-based functional MRI with healthy adult participants (N=64, ages 18–26). Reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects univariate analyses (parametric modulation of BOLD by self–other discrepancy) with peak coordinates, tables and figures. Not confined to ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria met.

This article reports an fMRI experiment that explicitly manipulates social attitudes (control-of-trust and control-of-distrust) and measures neural responses during those social tasks, so the task is social-related (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=60, mean age ~20), satisfying the adult healthy-sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked contrasts (e.g., trust>age, distrust>age, combined contrasts) with family-wise-error correction and provides tables/figures of whole-brain results and coordinates, meeting whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses, are not only connectivity/resting-state, are not only between-group contrasts, and the study is empirical with original fMRI data in healthy adults. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=14, mean age 35.9) that explicitly manipulates social interaction (human vs. machine competitor) to probe Theory of Mind/social processing during a task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with contrasts and tables of coordinates for healthy subjects. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used task-based fMRI with a social cognition paradigm (HCP Animated Triangles) (I3); includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (n=25) matched to patients (I4); reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and statistics for the healthy group (one-sample t-tests, FWE-corrected, with MNI coordinates) (I5); whole-brain results are clearly described in text and figures (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only analyses, and healthy-group univariate maps are reported rather than only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete. Therefore, INCLUDE.

This is an fMRI hyperscanning study of social interaction (mutual gaze and joint attention) in healthy adult participants (mean ages ~21–23), fulfilling the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses: inter-individual neural synchronization maps (voxelwise correlations with cluster-level FWE correction) with tables of coordinates and contrasts (e.g., MG2–MG1) and task-evoked GLM contrasts for IJA/RJA described at the group level. Results are presented as whole-brain statistical maps/tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections (full text appears complete). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study that used whole-brain, voxelwise analyses during a social-related task (explicit and implicit processing of facial expressions), meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=9, mean age 27±7), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical results and contrasts that include control-group effects (described in the text, figures, and Table 2; e.g., regions activated in controls such as left cerebellum and left amygdalohippocampal region), satisfying I5. Results are reported in standard formats (coordinates, figures, and tables), so I6 is met. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are violated. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study includes a social-related task (social distance trials comparing friends vs acquaintances) and thus addresses social processing (I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=15, ages 20–28), satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise univariate analyses (paired t tests across conditions) even though these yielded null results, fulfilling the requirement to report whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (I5). Whole-brain results (both univariate tests and multivariate searchlight/RSA maps) are reported in the main text and figures, consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., results are not ROI-only or connectivity-only, and the study is empirical). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This fMRI study tests social cognition by having healthy adult participants view images of social groups and make affective (social) judgments, with BOLD responses recorded. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (random-effects), provides coordinates, voxel counts, and t-values for contrasts (e.g., mPFC, insula, amygdala), meeting whole-brain reporting standards. Sample consists of healthy adult undergraduates (mean age 19.5). Results are reported in text/tables with Talairach coordinates. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion: none of the exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample: 10 subjects aged 20–29), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain contrast 'footstep minus rest' with maps), I6 (whole-brain results presented in supplementary material). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (the experiment is an auditory attention/perceptual motion detection task using human footsteps but does not target social-related processing constructs such as affiliation, social communication, or explicit perception/understanding of others). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study does not meet the review’s core criterion of investigating social-related processing and should be excluded.

The article reports original fMRI data collected from healthy adult participants (N=113 imaging sample; ages 18–31) who performed social cognition tasks (mental-state judgment tasks), satisfying I3 and I4. The authors computed GLMs and contrasts for each mental state (whole-brain patterns of regression coefficients and t-statistics per state) and performed a mega-analysis and a whole-brain parcel-based analysis to map effects across cortex, indicating group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps are reported (I5, I6). Analyses include univariate GLM contrasts (not only ROI or connectivity or exclusively multivariate searchlights), and results are presented at whole-brain/parcellated levels, so none of the exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion) and open data/materials are provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This paper is a narrative review (non-empirical) of ecstatic, orgasmic, and musicogenic seizures, Stendhal syndrome, and autoscopic phenomena. It does not report original fMRI task data in healthy adult participants, nor any group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps from a healthy/control group. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task map), and I6 (reporting of whole-brain results). It meets exclusion criterion E7 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods of review, development, and conclusions) but absence of original fMRI data is decisive.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly uses a social-related task: participants imagined self-relevant anger-eliciting interpersonal situations (behavior of another person) and generated cognitive reappraisals, engaging processes of social cognition, perspective-taking, and understanding others. The sample consists of healthy adults (N=45, age 18–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise activation analyses (conjunctions, task contrasts) with voxelwise FWE correction and cluster reporting. Therefore it meets criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults and provides univariate whole-brain task-evoked maps. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (mean age 22.7) using a social cognitive task (implicit/explicit theory-of-mind ‘Sally–Anne’ movies) assessing perception/understanding of others’ beliefs. Group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM results are reported (belief > photo/map contrast) with SPM figures and peak Talairach coordinates and cluster thresholds; additional whole-brain contrasts for implicit false- vs true-belief are described and depicted. Thus the paper meets: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported for the healthy group), and I6 (results presented via coordinates and figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, and includes univariate whole-brain activation maps). Full text appears complete. Hence INCLUDE.

This fMRI study uses a social cognitive (Theory of Mind) visual-joke task (meets I3). It includes a separately reported healthy control group of adults (controls n=13) with group-level within-group analyses (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects SPM2 results (thresholded maps and coordinate tables) for group-level contrasts (e.g., ToM vs Physical) including the healthy/control group (meets I5 and I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of analyses and healthy-group whole-brain maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts without healthy-group maps, non-adult sample, multivariate-only maps, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This empirical fMRI study (Pfeifer et al., 2009) reports task-evoked neural activity during social-related tasks (direct and reflected self-appraisals — perception/understanding of self and others). It includes a healthy adult group (N=12; ages 22.6–30.4) with results reported separately. The paper presents whole-brain, unmasked group-level analyses and contrasts (e.g., adult conjunction analyses and within-group contrasts versus rest), with cluster-level correction and coordinates/figures. Thus it satisfies the review’s requirements for an fMRI social task in healthy adults and reports whole-brain univariate activation maps for the healthy adult group. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and limitations). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (person knowledge) using a person-fact encoding task contrasted with non-social categories and a nonconceptual control. Participants were healthy adults (N=12; ages 20–32). The authors report group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked analyses (random-effects ANOVA, conjunctions, cluster-size corrections) and present whole-brain activation and functional connectivity results for the healthy sample. Whole-brain results are described in the text and figures, meeting reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, and sample is within adulthood). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (face emotion/age judgments) in healthy adults (final N=25, ages 21–33). The study reports whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses (random-effects contrast faces > objects used to define ROIs) and whole-brain searchlight results (Tables/figures reported), clearly coming from the healthy/control group. The task is social-related (perception/understanding of others via facial emotion), and the full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses fMRI during a social-related task (compassion/reappraisal while viewing images of human suffering vs. neutral images), addressing perception/understanding of others and prosocial behavior (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (aged 18–45) with results reported for these healthy groups (I4). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., Group × Redistribution Rank interaction; whole-brain corrected results identifying right IPC and DLPFC at p < .01), and univariate suffering>neutral contrasts were estimated for each scan, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy sample (I5). Whole-brain results are described in-text and supplemental tables/figures are referenced, so reporting meets I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, non-adult sample, or multivariate-only maps) are met. Full text appears complete for core content (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants investigating social processing (pupil mimicry and trust) using an explicit social task (trust game with eye-region stimuli and ToM localizer). The sample includes healthy adults (N=40 behavioral, N=34 fMRI). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., pupil-mimicry > no-mimicry; partner pupil change > static) with thresholding and peak coordinates (reported in text and SI tables). Reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates and figures satisfies reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

Although this is an fMRI study of a social task in healthy adults (meets I3, I4) and reports whole-brain coordinate tables/figures (meets I6), the manuscript reports only between-group contrasts (high-Mach vs low-Mach) at the second level and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task-evoked activation map for a healthy/control group (e.g., a one-sample/group main effect). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clearly reported univariate whole‑brain healthy-group task map). Full text appears complete.

Although this paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 21–46) and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (male vs female erotic stimuli) in text, figures, and tables, the experimental paradigm is an erotic/sexual arousal task rather than a social-related task as defined by the review (e.g., affiliation, social communication, perception/understanding of self or others in a social-cognitive sense). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I3. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) were triggered. Because the primary construct investigated is sexual arousal/sexual orientation rather than social processing per se, I exclude this study from the social-related processing meta-analysis.

The paper clearly meets all inclusion criteria: I3 - uses task-based fMRI probing social cognition (cooperation/competition, self/other processing); I4 - healthy adult sample reported (final N=24, ages 19–31); I5 - reports group-level whole-brain univariate task-evoked activation contrasts (family-wise error cluster corrected whole-brain effects, Table 1, whole-brain contrasts described); I6 - whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criteria apply. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and fMRI analyses, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This manuscript is a non-empirical review/overview (a perspective) of social neuroscience and does not present original fMRI data from an experiment in healthy adults. It therefore does not meet the empirical inclusion criteria: I3 (no original fMRI task data reported), I4 (no original healthy adult participant group reported/analyzed), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps provided), and I6 (not applicable because no original whole-brain results are reported). It meets exclusion criterion E7 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (review article content present).

This article is a non-empirical review chapter summarizing neuroanatomical and fMRI findings across disorders, not an original fMRI experiment in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E7 (review/meta-analysis/non-empirical paper without original fMRI data in healthy adults). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not report an original fMRI social-task in the study), I4 (no reported healthy adult participant group results), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise map from a healthy/control group), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=18, mean age mid-20s) that investigates social communication constructs (vitality forms in speech and action). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task activation contrasts (e.g., Vitality vs. Control) with random-effects analyses, whole-brain results (cluster- and voxel-level FWE-corrected), MNI coordinates, tables/figures, and conjunction analyses — satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Multifaceted Empathy Test) probing perception/understanding of others (empathy/social cognition). The fMRI sample includes a healthy adult control group (29 female controls) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps/main effects for the control group (e.g., Table 5 and text descriptions of main effects in controls) with coordinates and figures. Results are presented in whole-brain analyses (with a priori ROI focus but reporting whole-brain contrasts and peak coordinates) and the healthy-group effects are clearly identifiable. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (n=19, ages 18–35) where participants performed a self-assessment task (rating whether they would like to smell like presented odors). The task probes perception/understanding of self, a social-related construct. Group-level task contrasts are reported with MNI coordinates and statistical thresholds; the authors state that whole-brain analysis and ROI analyses were performed and provide voxelwise activation coordinates for the ‘self’-peptide versus solvent/non-self contrasts. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, resting-state/connectivity-only analyses, or non-adult sample) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This fMRI study uses a social interaction task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) probing reactive aggression, clearly within social-related processing (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adults (final N=15, mean age 22.9) (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts and provides coordinates and figures/tables of activations for decision and outcome phases (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are univariate whole-brain contrasts (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, MVPA-only), and the sample is adult and healthy. Full-text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task that explicitly probes social cognition (audio-visual social-norm inference) during scanning. It includes a healthy adult control group (TD; ages 18–35) with results reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts for the TD group (e.g., neutral GLM all-stimuli > fixation, visual GLM negative > positive, congruency GLM showing right parietal activation in TD), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps described for the healthy group. Results are presented in the main text with univariate voxelwise contrasts (and supplementary materials available), so the whole-brain reporting formats are acceptable. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates person knowledge retrieval (social-related processing) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (two cohorts: n=24, n=26; mean ages ~23 and ~20), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate GLM contrasts (e.g., “all memory > baseline”, status memory > baseline, face vs name contrasts) with voxelwise inference (FWE-corrected P < 0.05) and provides figures/tables of results; these satisfy the whole-brain evidence requirement. The task assesses perception/understanding of others (biographical/person knowledge), matching the social-related task inclusion. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-cognition-related processing (construal-level/mentalizing: Why-How paradigm and category/exemplar tasks that tap understanding of actions/intentions and object construal). Sample: 24 healthy adults (ages 18–27) satisfying the adult healthy sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., How>Why, Why>How, Exemplars>Categories) with cluster correction and tables/figures of activations (Table 2, Figure 1), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are described for the healthy group and contrasts are univariate task-evoked activation maps. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not MVPA-only, not non-empirical, and sample is adult). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an fMRI study of social exclusion (Cyberball), a social-related task (affiliation/belonging). Sample comprises healthy adults (n=20 analyzed; ages ~25). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (social exclusion > fair play; same- vs other-gender contrasts), with tables of coordinates and figures, and describes whole-brain preprocessing/analyses. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not developmental or geriatric only, not multivariate-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study uses task-based fMRI of personally familiar faces and places (a social-related construct—personal familiarity/affiliation), reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the healthy/control group, and presents results in text/figures. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I5, and I6 are satisfied. However, the sample consists of older adults (aMCI patients and healthy elderly controls); no healthy adult group in the 18–65 range is reported. Thus the study does not meet I4 and falls under exclusion criterion E5 (sample wholly outside adulthood/geriatric cohort). No ROI-only or connectivity-only limitations apply. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: E5. Consequently the paper is excluded from the review focused on healthy adults (18–65).

Full text appears to be incomplete (only abstract/metadata/references provided). The study uses fMRI during a social task (Trust Game), so it meets I3. However, the sample is described as adolescents across developmental phases (adolescence, young adolescents), not adults; therefore it fails I4 (healthy adult group 18–65). This places the study into exclusion E5 (sample wholly outside adulthood). I5 cannot be confirmed due to incomplete full text, but exclusion is already met by E5. Hence the study is excluded.

This study investigates emotion/aggression using fMRI and includes a healthy adult control group, but it does not report any univariate, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group. The paper focuses on whole-brain connectivity analyses and between-group connectivity differences (BPD vs healthy) rather than presenting an unmasked, group-level healthy-task activation map. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E3 (connectivity-focused analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports mainly between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — imagined interpersonal rejection/aggression) and I4 (healthy adult group reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map for the healthy group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of facial emotion discrimination (a social perception/understanding of others task) in adults aged 19–35. The paper reports task-evoked whole-brain, group-level activation results (FWE-corrected clusters and tables) and also reports within-group contrasts for the healthy control (NC) group (e.g., NC showed stronger activation in left SPG, SMA, LG, SOG during AH vs HH), so healthy-group whole-brain task effects are available. Participants were screened for psychiatric disorders and both SP and NC groups are adults; results for the NC (healthy) group are reported separately in the text and tables. The study is empirical, univariate, and not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening.

The study meets I3 (uses task-based fMRI during an explicit emotion-recognition/social processing task) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 21–33). However, it does NOT meet I5: the paper used a restricted "whole-slab" acquisition optimized for the amygdala with limited brain coverage and reports voxelwise results only within that slab and ROI analyses; it does not provide a true whole-brain group-level univariate task activation map/coverage. No exclusion criteria E2–E7 are directly triggered, but failing inclusion criterion I5 requires exclusion. Full text appears complete.

The study uses fMRI during a social-cognitive visual perspective-taking task and includes a separate healthy adult control group (meets I3 and I4). However, all task activation analyses were conducted within a predefined combined region-of-interest mask (ROI-restricted), not as an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation map. Therefore it fails I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Task), includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group (age-matched controls) with results described separately, and presents whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts (e.g., mental state > age judgment) and group Z statistic images corrected for multiple comparisons. Healthy-group contrasts and age-related control subgroup contrasts are described in the text and reported in tables/figures. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-state-only, multivariate-only, non-empirical) are met.

This fMRI study examines social-related processing via a peer-presence manipulation during two tasks (Stoplight risky-driving and Go/No-Go response inhibition), addressing social influence on decision making. Sample consists of healthy adults ages 21–24 (n=49) with exclusions for alcohol use disorder, so healthy adult criteria are met. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task activation contrasts (e.g., No-Go>Go; Risk>Safe) and functional connectivity analyses, with thresholded and unthresholded maps available on NeuroVault; thus whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group are provided. The study therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not a non-empirical paper, adult sample). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of action observation relevant to social processing (representation of others’ actions/interactions). Sample: healthy adults (n=29, ages 18–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., Observation > Neutral; Squeeze > No Squeeze; 2H DIFF > 2H SAME) with FWE-corrected thresholds, figures, and tables of peak coordinates. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E2–E7). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception/understanding of others, mentalizing) using a motion-classification task. Participants were healthy adults (n=12, mean age 27.3±4.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects univariate analyses (SPM2) including main effect of stimulus presentation and covariate analyses with FDR-corrected thresholds and tables/coordinates of activated regions. Whole-brain results are presented in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly probes social attribution (attributing awareness to others) using a task involving judgments about a cartoon face, satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (fMRI N=50; ages 18–49), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task activation contrasts (H trials − E trials) with thresholded surface maps (Fig. 3) and coordinate tables (Table 1), meeting I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not exclusively non-adult, not multivariate-only, and not non-empirical).

The study uses fMRI with a social task (cyberball) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map or within-group contrast clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group; the reported results focus on between-group contrasts (BPD>HC, NSSI>HC) and conjunctions. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task map) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion).

This study uses task-based fMRI of emotional prosody comprehension, a social-communication task (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=19 after exclusion), ages 18–51, meeting the adult healthy-sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate voxelwise contrasts (emotional vs neutral; complex vs simple), with SPM analyses, cluster-correction and tables/figures of coordinates (I5,I6). Analyses are univariate activation contrasts (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or MVPA), and results for the healthy group are clearly presented. Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study investigates perception of others by examining neural encoding of face gender (a social-perception construct). It tested healthy adult participants (n=16 recruited; analyses on 15 after exclusion) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects voxel-wise contrasts (gender-different > gender-same) with statistical thresholds and cluster correction, clearly from the healthy group. The methods, results, and discussion are present, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task contrast reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not multivariate-only, and not non-empirical).

Full text incomplete: only abstract/metadata available and PDF behind paywall, so I cannot verify whether the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) univariate task activation map (inclusion criterion I5). From the abstract, the study uses fMRI with emotional face processing (social-related task) and reports results in 12 healthy subjects, so I3 and I4 appear satisfied. However I5 (whole-brain evidence clearly identified as from the healthy group) cannot be confirmed from the provided content; thus the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria based on available information. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are clearly met from the abstract. Exclude pending access to the full text to confirm whole-brain results.

The study used fMRI with a social/attachment-related listening paradigm (I3 met) and involved healthy adult participants in the fMRI sample (I4 met). However, all reported neuroimaging results are seed-based resting-state functional connectivity (FC) analyses (caudate nucleus seed) comparing baseline and post-narrative resting scans; the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked activation maps or within-group task contrasts for the healthy sample. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain task-evoked map from healthy group) is not met. Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on E3.

The paper reports an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=26, mean age 24.4) investigating perception of others' pain and perceived agency—a clear social-related task (empathy, perception/understanding of others). The manuscript provides full methods, results, and discussion, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., pain > no-pain; social context contrasts) with tables of coordinates and FDR-corrected maps. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-adult sample, not MVPA-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI of emotional prosody (a social-communication / perception-of-others task) in adults, includes a healthy control group with results reported separately, and provides whole-brain group-level univariate activation contrasts (e.g., emotional vs. neutral prosody) and conjunction maps for controls. The methods and results describe voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (FSL, cluster-corrected maps) for the control group, and behavioral–brain relationships are reported for controls. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI of gesture-speech integration, a form of social communication, meeting the social-related task requirement. The paper includes healthy adult participants (H-group, n=19; separate C-group n=17) with results reported for healthy groups separately. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (contrasts GG>GR, GG>SG, conjunction GG>GR ∩ GG>SG) and report activation clusters (including left pSTS) for the healthy/control groups; Supplementary tables of clusters are referenced. Whole-brain results are presented in text/tables/coordinates rather than ROI-only or solely connectivity analyses. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social processing (dynamic facial-expression perception and imagery) in healthy adults (n=20, mean age ~25). The paper reports group-level univariate whole-brain analyses (RFX-GLM, FDR-corrected results; whole-brain contrasts and between-group comparisons are described), and results are reported in text and appendices. Thus it meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria.

This study does not meet the key content requirement I3: the task is a continuous performance test with monetary reward (reward-feedback/cognitive task), not a social-related task probing social communication, affiliation/attachment, or perception/understanding of self/others in healthy adults. It does include a healthy adult control group (I4), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for the control group (I5) with results described in text/tables (I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore exclude because I3 is not satisfied (while I4, I5, I6 are met).

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports whole-brain group analyses and multiple between-group contrasts (e.g., VSZ+CD/ASPD vs H) but does NOT clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain, within-group task-evoked activation map/statistical map for the healthy control group (I5 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used task-based fMRI during a social-related Theory-of-Mind task, RMET) and I4 (a healthy adult control group [n=18] is included and reported). Inclusion criterion I5 (a clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude under E4. Note: although whole-brain univariate analyses were performed and results are reported in figures/tables for group effects and pairwise contrasts, the manuscript does not present or describe an unmasked, whole-brain, within-group activation map for the healthy/control group that would meet I5.

This study used resting-state fMRI and connectome/seed-based analyses rather than an fMRI social-task paradigm. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports only resting-state connectivity analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes a healthy adult group, N=45, ages 18–45). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (does not use functional MRI during a social-related task; it used resting-state fMRI to assess intrinsic connectivity linked to emotional intelligence) and I5 (does not report any whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map for the healthy group). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the paper should be excluded from this task-based fMRI meta-analysis focused on social-task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes social-related tasks (theory-of-mind/mental state reasoning) and contrasts social vs. mechanical cognition. Participants are healthy adults (N=45, ages 19–23). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (including corrected statistical maps and peak coordinates in Appendix A) and random-effects analyses. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for social fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI task study of social-related processing (observation/understanding of others’ mouth actions and communicative behaviours) in healthy adults (N=60; ages 18–60). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts (within-group and between-group analyses) with FWE-corrected results, tables of activations/coordinates, and figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full, and the study also includes but is not limited to connectivity analyses. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not employ an fMRI social-related task (inclusion criterion I3 not met). The tasks used are verbal fluency and Hayling sentence completion (executive/response-inhibition tasks), not social-processing paradigms. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the healthy/control group are reported), I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (E2–E7 not met). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports fMRI data including a social cognition (social interaction vs. random movement) task in healthy adult samples (HCP and UCLA datasets). Voxel-wise GLM activation analyses and group-level task contrasts are described and figures of task activations are presented, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps. The sample consists of healthy adults (ages within 22–50). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age 24.2; N=13 analyzed) that uses task-based functional MRI during social-related tasks involving self- and other-referential trait judgments (social cognition: perception/understanding of self and others). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., self>syllables, old/same>new) with coordinates and SPM results presented in tables and figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical study).

This is an fMRI study using a social decision-making task (Trust Game) probing reciprocity and perspective-taking—clearly within social-related processing. Participants are healthy adults (final N=18, ages 18–22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., defect > reciprocate) with MNI coordinates and ROI follow-ups; whole-brain voxelwise results are described in text/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E2–E7).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (emotion alignment in interactive dyads) that meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI during an interactive social task (second-rater/first-rater conditions); (I4) reports a healthy adult sample (n=20, mean age ~23.95, right-handed university students); (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked results (random-effects analyses with clusterwise FWE correction across the whole brain) and presents activation tables/figures; (I6) whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-adult sample, not MVPA-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study that explicitly uses a social-related task (meaning relatedness judgments of social concepts vs. animal-function concepts), satisfying I3. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 29.4), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked contrasts (categorical contrasts, conjunction analyses) with coordinates/tables and whole-brain/ROI analyses clearly identified as healthy-group results, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods (subjects, fMRI paradigm, acquisition, analysis), results, and discussion; it is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, MVPA-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=30, females aged 19–39) who viewed a social/moral movie stimulus about siblings and completed a moral-decision task. It provides whole-brain, group-level univariate results: voxelwise ISC maps comparing conditions (FDR correction, cluster tables) and a GLM analysis of the moral-decision task with corrected group-level activations; cluster coordinates and statistical maps (NeuroVault link) are reported. The study therefore satisfies the review’s criteria for an fMRI social-related task in healthy adults and reports whole-brain task-evoked group maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, multivariate-only, non-empirical, or non-adult sample) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study that directly contrasts social versus non-social semantic judgments and reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (e.g., contrasts ‘social > non-social’ and ‘non-social > social’, P<0.05 corrected) with tables/figures of peak coordinates. The sample consists of healthy adults (N=19, age 19–28). The task probes social-related processing (stereotypes/social-category knowledge). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the reported whole-brain healthy-group task activations satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=27, mean age 27) that used a social-related task (viewing and implicitly evaluating others' facial expressions of disgust vs neutral), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (canonical disgust vs neutral; distaste vs neutral; canonical disgust vs distaste) with random-effects analysis, thresholded maps, figures and tables of coordinates, meeting I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment of social cognition (spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception), using a social-related task (one-back face recognition with learned trait associations). Sample: healthy adult participants (n=11, ages 18–32) with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (random-effects group analysis) with Talairach coordinates, cluster thresholds, and tables/figures of activation—fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (mentalizing, empathy, prosocial decisions) in healthy adult participants (n=32; adults mean age 22.7). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts (e.g., Mentalizing>baseline; Dissimilar>Similar) with thresholding and cluster-level correction and provides MNI coordinates/tables of activation clusters. ROI analyses are also reported but whole-brain univariate results are clearly present. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) apply.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E2 — the reported neuroimaging results are presented using a small-volume ROI (vACC) with small-volume correction; no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain voxelwise results are reported in the provided full text. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 — the study used task-based fMRI of social evaluation (trait attributions about politicians); I4 — sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=36, ages within adult range). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — the paper does not report at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (results are ROI-restricted/SVC). I6: N/A (whole-brain results are not provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study must be excluded because it reports only ROI-restricted analyses without an accompanying whole-brain, unmasked healthy-group activation map.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (empathy for pain) in healthy adult participants (male adults 18–40). The paper reports task-based whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (whole-brain FWE-corrected results are reported for contrasts such as INJECTION>QTIP and BIOPSY>QTIP, as well as conjunctions), and these results are clearly described in the main text and figures/tables. Behavioral and neuroimaging results for the healthy control and stress groups are reported separately. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 for the review objective.

This is an fMRI study of action observation/execution (mirror system) that addresses social-cognitive processes (perception/understanding of others), satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 20–34), satisfying the sample criterion. Whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses are reported (SPM2 second-level random-effects ANOVA, conjunctions and contrasts thresholded P<0.05 whole-brain corrected) with activations reported in tables and figures, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, non-adult sample, or multivariate-only results) are met.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social evaluation in healthy adults (N=20, ages 18–29) using a task that elicits social judgments (affiliation/understanding of others). It reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation results (multilevel whole-brain MLM, cluster coordinates, tables/figures; ROI analyses supplement but whole-brain contrasts are primary). Whole-brain results are described in text and thresholded maps/coordinate tables are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation reported), and I6 (results given as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The article reports an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=32, ages 18–39) performing a social task manipulating collaboration and competition, satisfying the review objective. The methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise univariate GLM analyses at the group level (random-effects SPM analyses), with reported statistical parametric maps and tables of activations surviving clusterwise FWE correction. Behavioral and neuroimaging results, including figures and tables of activations (e.g., basal ganglia, TPJ, mPFC), are presented. The full text includes Introduction, detailed Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening (not limited to abstract/metadata).

This paper meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (facial emotion recognition from eyes/mouth), (I4) includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group (age ~23.6) with results reported separately, (I5) reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (exploratory whole-brain analyses and within-group oxytocin>placebo contrasts with clusters reported for NT controls), and (I6) provides whole-brain results in tables/coordinates (Table 2) and described in text. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, sample includes adults, and univariate whole-brain activation contrasts are reported. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/references).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (real-world speed-dating) that probes social-affiliation and perception of others. Sample includes a healthy adult group (scanned participants N=38, ages 19–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked contrasts (e.g., main effects, Match>Unrequited, violations of expectations) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-correction, and tables of activation coordinates. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.
