This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related (naturalistic theory-of-mind/mentalising) task (I3); includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group (n=22, ages 19–46) analyzed separately from the ASD group (I4); reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task-evoked activation contrasts (ToM vs physical inference) for the control group with cluster-corrected results and figures/tables showing activations (I5,I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, allowing assessment of methods and outputs. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., results are not limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, multivariate maps, nor is this a non-empirical paper). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

Full text unavailable (paywalled); only metadata/title provided. Title indicates focus on first-episode schizophrenia (clinical sample), but no access to methods/results to verify fMRI social-task use or reporting of healthy adult group whole-brain results. Therefore I cannot confirm any inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: [] (no exclusion criterion can be determined from available info). Inclusion IDs met: [] (none can be confirmed). Inclusion IDs not met (unable to verify): I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked map reported), I6 (acceptable reporting format for whole-brain results). fulltext_incomplete=true — inability to assess core content (methods/results) prevents inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of emotional prosody (social communication) in healthy adults (N=22, mean age 24.8). It reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain univariate activation results (emotional > neutral prosody) with cluster-corrected maps and tables/figures described in text, clearly from the healthy sample. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for social-related fMRI in healthy adults and provides whole-brain task activation maps/contrasts suitable for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of action sentence processing that probes social/mentalizing aspects (why/how contrast) and thus targets social cognition. Participants were healthy adults (mean age ~25, range 21–33), meeting the adult healthy sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise univariate activation contrasts and conjunction analyses (thresholds, cluster-extent correction, MNI coordinates; Table 2 and figures), providing the necessary whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, multivariate-only, or non-empirical; not a between-group-only report; sample is adult). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of dynamic facial expressions (social communication) in healthy adults (participants mean age ~22), so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met. However, the reported neuroimaging results are presented via region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and small-volume-corrected contrasts (SVC) for a priori ROIs; the manuscript does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map or whole-brain voxelwise results independent of ROI/SVC. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses reported with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not satisfied; I6 (acceptable reporting formats for whole-brain results) is moot because no whole-brain results are provided. Full text appears complete. Because E2 is met, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about groups and individuals) conducted in healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: N=25, ages 19–27; Experiment 2: N=14, ages 18–23), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., group mental > group physical; member mental > member physical; individual mental > individual physical) with voxelwise thresholds and tables/figures, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are reported for the healthy/control groups and univariate maps are presented in tables/figures; MVPA results are supplemental but univariate contrasts are primary. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (Trust Game) addressing reciprocity, satisfying I3. The sample includes healthy adult participants (reported ages 18–30; 19 subjects included in imaging analyses), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked contrasts (GLM contrasts, cluster-corrected maps) and lists activated brain regions (Table 3) and figures (Fig. 2), satisfying I5 and I6. Results are reported for the healthy/control group (not limited to an excluded subgroup). The manuscript contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections, and is not ROI-only or connectivity-only. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (gaze shifts) in healthy adults reporting group-level whole-brain univariate task activation contrasts. The sample includes healthy adult participants (behavioural N=10, fMRI N=12; ages within 18–65). The paper describes whole-brain SPM2 analyses and reports voxelwise contrasts (e.g., gaze-shift − no movement; incorrect − correct; social − unsocial) with tables of activated loci (Table 1, Table 2) and figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain group-level maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult samples, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion requirements: it uses task-based fMRI to probe social cognition (mental state attribution/intentional stance induced by believing music was composed vs computer-generated), reports results from a healthy adult sample (12 participants analyzed, ages 21–31), and provides group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked contrasts (Composer > Computer) with second-level random-effects analysis, voxel coordinates, cluster correction, and tables/figures describing the whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult, MVPA-only, or non-empirical paper). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of dynamic audiovisual emotion perception—a social cognition task (perception/understanding of others). The sample includes healthy adults (Study 1: n=10, ages 18–33; Study 2: n=5, ages 18–23). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses and presents whole-brain results (tables of coordinates, figures, and conjunction analyses) for the healthy participants. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (competition vs. no-competition) in healthy adult participants (female, ages 18–35). The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate analyses and contrasts (e.g., competition > no competition) with cluster thresholds and peak coordinates described in text and figures, and includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=21 males, ages 23–33) using a social perception task (rating naturalness of dyadic nonverbal interactions), i.e., a social-related construct (Perception and Understanding of Others). The manuscript provides full methods, behavioral and neural results, and discussion. Group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts are reported and described (contrasts such as CS+CR>MS+MR, CR+MR>CS+MS, etc.) with cluster-corrected inference and coordinate tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study acquired task-evoked whole-brain activation while healthy adult participants read 240 sentences, many describing social interactions. The task elicits processing of social content (people/social interactions) and the authors identify brain clusters associated with social-related semantic factors (Figure 4A, SI Table S3). The sample is healthy adults (mean age 25). Group-level, voxelwise results (factor-related voxel clusters and associated maps) are reported and discussed. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, MVPA-only whole-brain maps, or non-empirical) apply.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social stimuli (emotional face matching) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met). However, the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5 not met). The manuscript mainly presents overall task activation collapsed across group/drug and group×drug interaction effects, and extracts parameter estimates from regions of interest. Therefore it fits exclusion criterion E4 (reports interactions/between-group effects without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related interpersonal distance task (affiliation/social processing), with a healthy adult sample (n=19 analyzed, ages 18–30). The paper presents whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (2x2 factorial; treatment x protagonist) with results thresholded (FDR q<0.05) and describes significant whole-brain activations and interaction maps (dmPFC, ACC, PCC, putamen, etc.), satisfying the requirement for univariate whole-brain task-evoked maps. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no resting-state-only, not non-empirical, adult healthy group reported).

This study is an event-related fMRI investigation of self-face recognition (a social-cognitive task involving perception/understanding of self), conducted in a sample of healthy adult participants (n=10, mean age ~26.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (Self vs Other and Other vs Self) with thresholding and MNI coordinates in tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of whole-brain univariate activation maps for the healthy group. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The full text describes an fMRI study using a social provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) in healthy adult males (ages 18–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., high > low provocation) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides coordinates and figures of these effects. Thus the study satisfies the review’s requirements for (1) a social-related fMRI task, (2) a healthy adult sample, and (3) whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported in the text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

All inclusion criteria are met: (I3) The study used task-based fMRI contrasting social vs. non-social image appraisal; (I4) healthy adult sample reported separately (N=14 after data loss; ages 23–50); (I5) group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps are reported (social–nonsocial contrast, whole-brain thresholds and conjunction analyses); (I6) results are reported in maps/tables and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, multivariate-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical study). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used a social communication task (charades) involving healthy adult participants (n=18 analyzed; mean age 27.5), meeting the population and task requirements. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain differential Granger-causality maps (bbGCM) thresholded at P<0.05 (cluster-corrected) and describes GLM-based analyses and seed definition from whole-brain contrasts on the same data. These satisfy the requirement for at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI/connectivity results without whole-brain maps, non-empirical paper, or non-adult sample) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of impression updating (social cognition/perception of others) with healthy adult participants (ages 18–31). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (e.g., L2>F3 main effect of updating; updating-by-condition ANOVA) with cluster-corrected results and tables/figures of activations, clearly coming from the healthy sample. Thus it meets I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (expectancy violations along warmth and competence) in healthy adult participants (mean age 20.4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM), lists Talairach coordinates, cluster statistics, and describes whole-brain contrasts and ROIs; results are reported for the healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study used fMRI in healthy adult participants to probe perception of own vs others' body parts (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper’s analyses focus on ROI-based fMR-adaptation effects (EBA ROI and extracted time courses) and statistical tests on ROI percent signal change. It does not present a clear group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked univariate statistical map for the main experimental contrasts; localization and cluster coordinates appear used to define subject ROIs rather than to report an unmasked healthy-group whole-brain activation map for the task. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used a natural-viewing intersubject-correlation paradigm comparing supporters of rival football teams. It meets I3 (social-related processing: group bias, perception/interpretation of others) and I4 (healthy adult sample, n=18, ages ~21). However, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise univariate task activation map from the healthy group. Results are reported as ROI/region-wise intersubject correlations averaged within 55 Harvard–Oxford atlas regions and post hoc t-tests per region (i.e., region-based analyses), and the principal contrasts are within-group vs between-group ISC (group differences) rather than an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E2 (only ROI/region-based analyses without whole-brain voxelwise results) and E4 (reports group-difference ISC without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task manipulating beneficiary (self, friend, antagonist) (I3); the sample is healthy adults aged 18–26 with results reported for the healthy group (I4); the paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (one-way and Person×Outcome ANOVAs) with tables/coordinates and figures clearly identified as from the healthy sample (I5,I6). Whole-brain results and coordinates are reported, and core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, not outside adult range, not MVPA-only, and is empirical).

This study is an fMRI investigation of pain empathy (a social-related task) including a healthy adult control group (n=21) alongside a clinical group. The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) within-group contrasts for the control group (e.g., Self>Other and Effective>Not Effective contrasts with reported activations in posterior cingulate/precuneus, right frontal lobe, ACC/paracingulate, AI, etc.), with thresholding and cluster extent described. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps for healthy group), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines social-cognitive processing (mentalizing/attribution of mind) while participants viewed sexualized and clothed male and female targets, meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (heterosexual men, n=21, ages within adult range), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (deviant-cell contrasts, Williams' t tests) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction (AlphaSim) and provides tables/figures of whole-brain results. Reporting of whole-brain results in text, tables, and figures is clear. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (impression formation about people vs objects) in healthy adults. The sample is healthy adults (n=14; ages 18.3–23.7), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., person-impression > other trial types) with voxelwise thresholding (P<0.001), cluster extents, and MNI coordinates; tables and figures report coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, nonadult sample, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing using a social-cognitive task (neutral face processing, emotion recognition, affective theory of mind) (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=74; adults with no history of mental/neurological disorders) (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked analyses (one-sample t-tests and ANOVA across participants; whole-brain results reported at p<0.05 FWE with supplementary tables/figures) and provides coordinates/figures for main effects and contrasts (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task maps, adult sample, univariate maps reported).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (masked fearful/happy eye cues) using a task tapping perception of others’ emotional signals (I3). Sample comprises healthy adult males (n=43 analyzed, ages ~24) meeting the healthy adult sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exploratory whole-brain results with coordinates and clusters reported in the Results and Supplementary Tables S1–S3), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5,I6). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion E4 met: The paper primarily reports between-subgroup contrasts (proselfs vs prosocials and interactions with trust) as whole-brain voxelwise maps, but does not present an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect or within-group main effect map for the overall healthy sample. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is social-related: PD games probing cooperation, trust, mentalizing), I4 (sample = healthy adults, age ~24.6, N=35 for analysis), I6 (whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables as acceptable formats). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clear group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map identified as coming from the healthy/control group that is not limited to a subgroup). The provided full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude under E4.

This task-based fMRI study investigates face perception, including changeable aspects of faces (gaze, expression, viewpoint) that are core to social communication, so it addresses a social-related processing construct. The sample consists of eight healthy adult observers (healthy adult group reported). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses/localiser results (FEAT z-statistic images, Talairach coordinates, activation maps and tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation reporting; results are presented in figures and tables. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines perception and production of prosody—a social-communication/emotional processing task—and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts in healthy adult participants (n=19, ages 18–58). Whole-brain contrasts (e.g., “happy–neutral”, “question–neutral”) are reported with voxelwise thresholds and corrections (FDR, cluster sizes) and described in text/tables/figures. Behavioral correlations with empathy measures are also reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (action imitation/observation relevant to perception/understanding of others), includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately (N=16), and reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (one-sample t tests and peak Talairach coordinates reported in Table 2 and figures). Whole-brain results are presented as coordinates and described in the text, satisfying acceptable reporting formats. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not MVPA-only, and not non-empirical).

This study reports task-based fMRI of a social-related task (imitation/observation of emotional faces), includes a healthy adult sample (n=28 initial, N=20 included in imaging analyses; ages 18–55), and provides whole-brain group-level results (GLM whole-brain analysis and multivariate PLS voxelwise maps reported and depicted). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, pediatric/geriatric-only, or multivariate-only without univariate maps) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (racial prejudice influencing disgust face perception) using a passive face-viewing task—clearly a social-related task. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (26 analyzed; mean age ~21). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA, interaction contrasts, cluster-corrected results) and presents activation tables/figures for healthy participants. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social interactive task (virtual handshake provoking social acceptance vs rejection), meeting the social-related task requirement. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=16, mean age ~27) with results reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate contrasts for the control group (refusal vs acceptance) with identified clusters (right pSTS, thalamus) and statistical thresholds, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-adult only, and not multivariate-only). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (persuasion/celebrity influence) using a task probing perception/understanding of others and social influence, performed in healthy adult participants (mean age 21.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (thresholded and cluster-corrected) with tables of significant activation clusters and figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. Full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, allowing assessment. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma (a social interaction task) during scanning (meets I3). The sample is healthy adult participants (n=30, mean age 21.2) with results reported for this group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (one-sample t tests, thresholded maps) and voxel-by-voxel correlation maps, with results presented in tables/figures (meets I5 and I6). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for whole-brain univariate task-evoked activation in healthy adults performing a social task.

This empirical fMRI study uses a social-related task (anticipation of touching an animate vs inanimate target), meeting I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=32, ages 21–33), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (paired-sample t-tests and covariate analyses) with FDR-corrected maps and reported coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and the sample is adult. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary materials are referenced but not required, so fulltext is complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (theory-of-mind: reasoning about intentions, cooperation, deception), in a healthy adult sample (n=13, ages 22–38). The authors performed an exploratory whole-brain, group-level contrast comparing all ToM conditions to non-ToM control (reported with peak coordinates, figures, and cluster extents) and then derived ROIs from those whole-brain results. Whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps from the healthy group are clearly described and reported (coordinates/tables/figures). Although some condition-specific contrasts were subsequently restricted to ROIs, the presence of an unmasked whole-brain ToM > non-ToM group map satisfies the review’s requirement for whole-brain evidence. Therefore I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (perception/understanding of others) using a task where participants judged facing-toward vs away point-light and human-like walkers while undergoing fMRI. The sample comprises healthy adults (N=16, mean age 22.75). Group-level (second-level) voxelwise contrasts were conducted and reported with stereotaxic coordinates and thresholding (FWE-corrected within defined search masks); the manuscript describes whole-brain contrasts and reports task-evoked group activation peaks. Results are reported in tables/figures and described for the healthy/control group. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present.

The study reports an fMRI task of social preference in healthy adults (ages 23-51), with whole-brain group-level activation contrasts (Preference>Gender and task vs baseline) thresholded and reported, and tables/figures of activation peaks; it includes psycho-physiological interaction connectivity analyses but also presents univariate whole-brain results. Inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), and I5/I6 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported) are satisfied. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete is false. However, some uncertainty remains about whether all whole-brain maps are unmasked and clearly identified as healthy-group only; confidence moderate. Inclusion criteria applied: I3,I4,I5,I6. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, ages 23–39) that uses a social-related task (judgments of social coordination vs relationship familiarity), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (ANOVA and post hoc t-tests; contrasts reported at P < 0.05 FDR corrected) and describes results in tables and figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study testing processing of others' decisions (mentalizing/social cognition) in healthy adults. Sample: 12 healthy right-handed adults (mean age 21) — satisfies adult healthy sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses and reports activation coordinates and statistical maps (with small-volume correction within ACC) tied to task contrasts (informative vs. uninformative feedback across agents), meeting whole-brain task-evoked reporting requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it is a resting-state fMRI investigation of ASD vs. typical development rather than a task-based fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only resting-state analyses and no healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria: none are satisfied. Specifically, inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task — the study used resting-state fMRI), I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from a healthy/control group), I4 (does not clearly report a separate healthy adult task group; sample mixes clinical and control participants across a wide age range). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the paper does not meet the review’s requirements for task-evoked whole-brain activation in healthy adults and should be excluded.

This fMRI study used a social attribution task (social cognition) with healthy adult participants (controls aged 18–65) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses. The manuscript reports whole-brain group-by-empathy interactions during the attribution phase and describes the direction of effects within the healthy control group (neural activity scaling negatively with empathy), with clusters surviving whole-brain correction. Thus it provides group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results that are identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The sample includes a healthy adult group analyzed and reported separately from the clinical BPD group. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The paper reports an fMRI study using a validated social-related task (Cyberball social exclusion), includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (HC, n=28) and presents whole-brain, univariate group-level task effects for the healthy group (main effect of condition in HC with voxelwise FWE-corrected results and coordinates). Results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social processing (social closeness task) in healthy participants and includes adult participants, so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the reported fMRI results are ROI-restricted (beta weights extracted from anatomical/functional ROIs derived from VBM peaks) rather than unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation maps for the healthy group. No whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group are reported, so inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Therefore the study meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses reported for fMRI) and must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study uses task-based fMRI of a social cognitive task (trustworthiness judgments) and includes a healthy adult control group, so it meets I3 and I4. However, the reported results focus on region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (mean percent signal change within a priori ROIs) and correlation analyses; there are no unambiguous group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps or tables of whole-brain coordinates reported for the healthy/control group in the full text. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results) and does not satisfy inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study using social-communication tasks (gaze following and finger pointing) to examine neural processing of directional social cues. Sample: 17 healthy right-handed adults aged 20–34 (meets adult sample criterion). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (gaze following vs baseline; finger pointing vs baseline; subtraction contrasts) and visualizes activations on template and subject images; univariate activation maps and ROI analyses are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults. It uses task-based fMRI with social (agent-behavior, agent-mental) and non-social conditions, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample: 24 healthy adult participants (mean age 25.7), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (e.g., contrasts for Background and Outcome segments; Tables 2–3; voxel-wise threshold P<0.001, cluster-wise FWE correction), satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement. Whole-brain results are presented in the main text/tables (acceptable reporting per I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-adult, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of self-face recognition, which falls under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Self), satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=16 analyzed, ages 19–24), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM random-effects contrasts, cluster-corrected results with MNI coordinates for contrasts such as Morph 50% recognized as self vs friend), satisfying I5. Whole-brain results are reported with coordinates and thresholding in the text, satisfying I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (patient vs control) and presents coordinates from those contrasts and extracted % signal changes for each group, but does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related attribution task) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social-related processing (judgments of pride, a self-conscious emotion, vs joy) in healthy adult participants (n=16, mean age ~21). The methods describe whole-brain, random-effects, voxelwise group-level contrasts (P−N, J−N, P−J) with tables of peak coordinates and figures; regression analyses and conjunctions are reported. Results are univariate task-evoked activation maps clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. No ROI-only, connectivity-only, MVPA-only, between-group-only, developmental-only, or non-empirical exclusions apply. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an emotional face recognition task (social-related processing: perception/understanding of others/affiliation) in adult mothers. The paper includes a healthy control group (mothers without early life maltreatment) and reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked activation results (e.g., familiarity effect in medial frontal gyrus for CON; whole-brain FWE-corrected results and reported MNI coordinates/tables). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article is complete for screening. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It used task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (a modified Empathic Accuracy Task probing perception/understanding of others' emotions) satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adults (final N=34; ages 20–30), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., emotional > neutral; parametric modulation by empathic accuracy; time-series correlations) with threshold-free cluster enhancement FWE correction and reports clusters/peak coordinates and figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=30, ages ~24) that uses social-related tasks (gender identification of angry and happy faces; perception/understanding of others). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task activation analyses (FWE-corrected whole-brain contrasts and tables/figures described), and results for the healthy/control group are clearly presented. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text not provided (only abstract/metadata). Based on the abstract, the study meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task of control aversion) and I4 (healthy adult participants are included). However, I cannot verify I5 (reporting of at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group) or I6 from the available information. Because the full article (methods, results with whole-brain univariate activation maps or coordinate tables) is not available here, inclusion criteria cannot be fully confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E2-E7) can be confidently applied from the abstract alone. Therefore I must exclude due to incomplete full text preventing verification of required whole-brain results (I5).

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports group comparisons (ALS > HC and HC > ALS) but does not present an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group (control-only) task activation map or main-effect/within-group contrast clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during social-related tasks: action observation and action-understanding/ToM) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). I5 (required: a clear whole-brain healthy-group task map) is NOT met based on the provided full text. Although whole-brain results and coordinate tables are reported, they are from between-group contrasts rather than an unmasked control group main effect; thus E4 applies. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (emotional face perception during a gender discrimination task), using healthy adult participants (n=30) screened for psychiatric history. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion. Group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts are reported (e.g., main effects of faces vs baseline, fear vs neutral; whole-brain comparisons and supplementary tables of results are provided), satisfying the requirement for at least one unmasked, voxelwise healthy-group activation map. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical, and sample is adult). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=24, mean age 26) that investigates social/emotional processing (integration of facial and vocal emotional expressions), satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (RFX) with voxelwise results and FWE-corrected maps and coordinates (e.g., rpSTS bimodal>unimodal at P<0.05 FWE), and these whole-brain healthy-group task effects are clearly described in the text and figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain univariate task activations are reported alongside ROI and DCM analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI experiment in healthy adults (N=15, mean age 23.6) using a social-related task (observing dyadic violent interactions; attention manipulated to aggressor vs victim), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked contrasts (e.g., all conditions vs baseline; focus on aggressor vs focus on victim) with cluster correction and tables/figures (Supplementary Table S2), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, fMRI acquisition), Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain univariate results are reported; not limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, MVPA-only, or non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

The study is an empirical fMRI experiment in healthy adults investigating social perception (monitoring others' pupil changes), meeting the review objective. It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (main effects of viewing eye stimuli reported at whole-brain corrected thresholds and second-level analyses described), and provides coordinates/cluster results for task-evoked activations. The sample consists of 14 healthy adult participants (mean age 22). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of face memory/recognition (socially relevant: perception and understanding of others). Sample: 18 healthy adults (ages 19–36) meeting the healthy adult criterion. The authors report group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked contrasts using Random Effects analyses and cluster correction (e.g., differential activations for false recognition vs recognition/correct rejection) with Talairach coordinates and figures/tables—i.e., univariate whole-brain results clearly attributed to the healthy group. The task (face recognition/false recognition) fits the social-processing domain. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not multivariate-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task study investigating agency (self-related processing), which falls under ‘Perception and Understanding of Self’ — a social-related construct. The sample includes 31 healthy adult controls reported separately from the schizophrenia group. The authors conducted group-wise, whole-brain (voxelwise) task analyses for the Agency>No-self-agency contrast and explicitly report the results for the healthy/control group (they note no significant clusters were found). Although whole-brain analyses yielded null findings, a group-level whole-brain task-evoked analysis is reported, satisfying the requirement for an unmasked healthy-group whole-brain result. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study employs fMRI during a social-related task (agreement with music experts) and reports a separate healthy control group, satisfying I3 and I4. However, the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group alone. Reported whole-brain results appear to be between-group contrasts (controls > cocaine users) and ROI-based SVC analyses; no standalone healthy-group voxelwise activation map (e.g., agree>disagree within controls) is clearly reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (healthy-group whole-brain map). Exclusion criteria met: E4. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of Theory of Mind (social processing) so I3 is met. However, although the sample includes a healthy adult control group, the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The authors report component maps derived across all participants and report between-group contrasts (ASD vs control) without presenting a standalone healthy-group whole-brain task effect. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not satisfied and exclusion criterion E4 applies (reporting only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (perception/understanding of others via facial emotion; satisfies I3). Samples are healthy adults (ages ~25–26, N reported across experiments), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects task-evoked contrasts (e.g., dynamic > static, contrasts vs baseline) with thresholding and cluster correction, satisfying I5. Whole-brain results and stereotaxic coordinates are reported in tables (and supplemental tables), satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not multivariate-only, and the sample is within adulthood. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses fMRI to examine processing of emotion words (a social/emotion-related construct) and includes a healthy adult control group with reported results; however, it does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The paper’s whole-brain maps are either pooled across all participants or reported as between-group (control > ASC) contrasts, and the control-group within-subject results are presented primarily in ROI analyses rather than as an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group activation map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=30, age 19–41) that used a social task (perception of direct vs. averted gaze) during BOLD fMRI. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task activation contrasts (e.g., congruent vs. incongruent, direct vs. averted gaze) with cluster- and voxel-level inference and provides coordinates and maps; it also reports PPI connectivity but not as the sole evidence. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study using social-cognitive tasks (emotion recognition and theory-of-mind ‘eyes’ tasks), includes a healthy control group reported separately, and presents group-level, whole-brain within-group regression results for the control group (described in the Results with regional correlations and laterality indices, and presumably reported as coordinates/tables). The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Age range is not explicitly listed in the excerpt, but participants are described as adult samples (recruited from hospital/clinic populations) and no evidence suggests a non-adult or exclusively special-age cohort; therefore I am moderately confident this meets the 18–65 healthy adult requirement. Given these points, the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=24 analyzed, ages 19–31) that investigates recognition of personally familiar vs famous vs unfamiliar faces, addressing social-cognitive processing (perception/understanding of others, adaptive social responses). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts and corrected statistical maps (random-effects second-level analyses; contrasts such as P1–Cp1, P1–F1; cluster-level correction reported), with activation tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study examines social impression formation (meets I3) in a healthy adult sample (N=60 males, ages ~23.8; meets I4). However, the paper’s primary neuroimaging results are multivariate PLS maps (behavioral PLS and task PLS) and do not report any univariate, group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation contrasts or coordinate tables/figures from the healthy group within this manuscript. The authors reference a separate univariate analysis of the same dataset but do not provide univariate whole-brain results here. Therefore the study fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only multivariate map reported without an accompanying univariate group activation map). Full text appears complete for the purposes of screening.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults (N=18, ages 18–44) using a task that required predicting others' behavior based on desires vs. rules — clearly social-related processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses with cluster-level correction and tables of coordinates and contrasts (portrait/feedback events, time-bin effects, contrasts such as desires>rules), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Results are reported in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample) apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly investigates social-related processing (trustworthiness and attractiveness judgments) using task-based fMRI. The sample comprises 44 healthy adults (ages 21–60), meeting the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts and conjunctions (thresholded maps with cluster-level FWE correction) with MNI coordinates and tables/figures, clearly describing results from the healthy/control group. Reporting of whole-brain univariate activation maps and coordinate tables satisfies the reporting requirement. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social processing (self/other understanding in romantic relationships), with a task-based fMRI paradigm directly probing social-affiliative and self/other constructs. Sample: 42 healthy adult participants (ages 23–40) meeting the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM results (directional t-contrasts, ANOVA) with FWE voxel-level corrections and tables/figures of activations, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, group-only contrasts, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) are met. Inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; exclusion_criteria_applied is [].

The manuscript reports an fMRI experiment explicitly investigating social/interpersonal touch (a social-related task). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=16; ages 20–34). The paper provides whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level task contrasts (interaction and main effects) and reports cluster coordinates, statistical maps, and conjunction analyses; results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it reports only resting-state fMRI connectivity/graph analyses and behavioral task data collected outside the scanner, not task-evoked whole-brain fMRI activation maps for a healthy adult group. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (resting-state analyses only, no healthy-group whole-brain task activation) and E2 (ROI/network-based connectivity/graph analyses with no whole-brain task results). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI during a social-related task; the Short Story Task was behavioral outside the scanner), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported for the healthy/control group), I4 (while a healthy volunteer group is present, the sample spans adolescents and young adults [ages 12–24] and no separate healthy adult (18–65) whole-group task activation is reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the paper does not meet the meta-analysis requirements.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract and metadata provided). I cannot verify key methodological details required by inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met based on available content: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — prosodic/social-communicative intention categorisation). Inclusion criteria not verifiably met: I4 (no participant ages or explicit statement that a healthy adult group [18–65] was tested and reported separately), I5 (no explicit report in this abstract of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy group), I6 (unable to confirm how whole-brain results, if present, are reported). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are clearly met in the abstract. Because the full text is incomplete and essential inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, I exclude this study pending retrieval of the complete article (methods and results) for re-assessment.

This fMRI study investigates social processing (gaze perception, theory-of-mind network) using a task involving direct vs averted gaze, meeting the review objective. It includes a healthy adult control group (separate group of typical males) with reported within-group contrasts (e.g., controls: direct gaze > averted gaze) and tables/figures with peak coordinates. The paper reports voxelwise contrasts and uses whole-brain FWE-corrected contrasts (faces vs null) to define networks; within-group control contrasts are presented as group-level statistical results (coordinates and figures). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (group-level, voxelwise task-evoked maps/contrasts for the control group reported as coordinates/figures), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level univariate activation contrasts examining perception/understanding of others’ actions (mirror system) via auditory and visual tasks—clearly a social-related processing construct. The sample includes healthy adult participants (14 sighted, 8 blind; ages reported, within 18–65) with results reported separately for the healthy groups. The paper presents voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps and corrected group contrasts (e.g., familiar action vs environmental sounds; motor pantomime vs rest) with cluster-correction and figures/tables of activations. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study uses a social interactive task (pseudo-interactive joke task) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately, satisfying I3 and I4. However, the paper explicitly reports that whole-brain analyses could not be conducted due to signal loss and that the investigation focused on an ROI analysis of the arMPFC rather than reporting any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group activation map reported) and meets exclusion criteria E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E4 (results are limited to group/ROI contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study reports an fMRI task explicitly probing social cognition (joint attention), includes healthy adult control groups (NT matched controls and an independent ROI control group) with results reported separately, and provides group-level whole-brain univariate contrasts and coordinates for the neurotypical groups (e.g., RJA vs. SA, IJA vs. SA) in the main text/tables. Whole-brain random-effects analyses within the healthy groups are described and thresholding/coordinate results are reported, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise healthy-group task-evoked maps. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This fMRI study uses a social-related empathizing task, so I3 is satisfied. However, it does not provide an unambiguous, unmasked whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from a healthy adult control group (no adult-only healthy-group whole-brain contrast is reported). The paper’s reported results focus on between-group age interactions and group-difference covariation with age rather than presenting a whole-brain healthy-group task effect. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task map). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no separately reported healthy adult-only group) and I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain healthy-group task map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study meets inclusion criteria: it used functional MRI during a social-related task (expert advice; social context affecting decision making) (I3), includes a healthy adult group (18–45 years) reported separately (I4), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked group-level analyses with cluster correction and MNI coordinates (satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements; results presented in figures/tables) (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply: the paper is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only or resting-state-only, includes healthy adults rather than an exclusively non-adult sample, and reports univariate task activations. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis focused on fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating emotional/affective speech comprehension and associated social-cognitive processes (theory-of-mind), which fits the review’s social-related tasks (I3). The sample comprises 51 healthy adults (ages 18–53), meeting the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (EMO vs GRAM) with SPM analyses and corrected statistical maps and coordinates (I5, I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore include.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of persuasion, a clearly social-related construct (persuasion/mentalizing). Samples are healthy adult participants (American and Korean groups; ages ~20–22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (persuasive vs unpersuasive) with tables of coordinates and figures (MNI coordinates, SPM analyses), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults. It uses task-based fMRI during social judgments (emotions, beliefs, pain) relevant to perception/understanding of others, reports univariate whole-brain group-level contrasts (multiple whole-brain maps, tables and figures), and includes a healthy adult sample (N=46, ages 18–31). Although the paper also applies MVPA, it additionally reports standard univariate, group-level task-evoked activation contrasts (so it does not fall under exclusion E6). Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided in the supplied text. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (observing cooperative vs. affective interactions) in healthy adult participants (N=27, mean ages ~25), reporting whole-brain, group-level task contrasts with FWE-corrected statistical maps and tables of activations and coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps/contrasts), and I6 (coordinates/tables described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (not truncated).

Although the study uses task-based fMRI of emotion processing (a social-related construct) and includes healthy adult control participants, it does not report a standalone whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The paper reports (a) a main effect of task across all subjects and (b) between-group contrasts (siblings vs controls) showing siblings>controls, but I could not find an unmasked, within-group whole-brain activation map or coordinate table specifically for the healthy control group. This violates inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reporting only between-group contrasts without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting I3 and I4.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (animacy/social cognition) using animated stimuli and participants made social/animacy judgments (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (15 males, mean age ~26.6) (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects univariate analyses with cluster- and voxel-level thresholds and provides tables of peak coordinates and clusters (Tables 2 and 3), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting (I5, I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing complete assessment. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an empathy-for-pain social task (social processing) with both a healthy control group (n=18) and an autism group. The paper reports whole-brain analyses and peak coordinates (Supplementary Table 1) and describes a whole-brain control-group contrast (e.g., control > patient activity in visual cortex) and group/within-group contrasts (High Pain–Low Pain in Other, masked by Self). Thus it provides group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results for healthy adults. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task that probes social-related processing (emotional memory retrieval in rival sports fans; involves self-referential and social-cognitive processes). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (male college students, ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM5 random-effects, whole-brain contrasts, tables/figures, small-volume corrections); results are reported for the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, multivariate-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of empathy (social-related emotional perspective-taking) in healthy adults (N=26, mean age ~24), reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (SELF- and OTHER-task vs baseline) with tables of coordinates and statistical thresholds. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an fMRI task that directly manipulates self-referential processing and perspective taking (social-related constructs) by having participants judge trait adjectives for self vs. a close other and adopt different perspectives. The abstract reports group-level activations in multiple MPFC subregions (ventral/dorsal anterior and posterior dorsal MPFC) and an interaction effect, consistent with whole-brain task-evoked contrasts from a healthy sample. However, the provided full text appears to be an abstract/summary only and lacks detailed methods (participant ages, explicit statement of voxelwise analysis or coordinate tables). Therefore I include the study but mark the full text as incomplete, giving moderate confidence.

This fMRI study investigates attachment-related processing using masked emotional faces (social/affiliation-related stimuli) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts. Sample: 51 healthy adults (mean age 28.5), satisfying the adult healthy sample requirement. The paper reports group-level univariate whole-brain analyses (emotion vs neutral contrasts), provides tables of activation coordinates and describes voxelwise regression analyses relating attachment avoidance to brain responses, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

The study uses task-based fMRI to investigate perception of social actions (meets I3). Participants are healthy adults (Experiment 1 N=20, Experiment 2 N=20 before exclusion; ages within 19–32), meeting the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain analyses: univariate baseline contrasts (actions vs. baseline) are referenced (Supplementary Fig. 11), and whole-brain searchlight RSA maps are reported in the main results; reporting in supplementary figures satisfies the acceptable reporting formats (I5 and I6). None of the exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs (E2), not exclusively connectivity or resting-state (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), sample is adult (no E5), and although much of the focus is on multivariate RSA, univariate whole-brain contrasts are reported (so E6 does not apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI social processing in healthy adults.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses task-based fMRI to probe social communication/perception (emotional vocal processing), includes a healthy adult sample (N=22, ages 19–36), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (the voice localizer contrast [vocal > non-vocal] producing extended bilateral STG/STS activation) clearly derived from the healthy/control group. Whole-brain results are reported in the text and figures (voice localizer); univariate task-evoked contrasts are presented. Although the main experiment used ROI analyses with small-volume correction for TVA and amygdala, this does not preclude inclusion because a group-level whole-brain map is provided (voice localizer). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI of social processing (empathy/sympathy), includes healthy adult participants within the sample (ages 7–40, thus adults 18–40 present), and provides group-level whole-brain univariate activation contrasts (PCS–NPS and PCO–PCS) with thresholding and reported coordinates/figures. Whole-brain random-effects analyses and coordinates are reported in the text and figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group results. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Although the sample is mixed-age and adult-only subgroup results are not presented separately, the sample includes healthy adults and the reported whole-group healthy participant analyses are clearly described, meeting inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria were met.

This paper reports task-based dyadic fMRI (dfMRI) during a social eye-contact task (meets I3). Sample is 19 pairs (38 healthy adults), ages 18–33, with group-level results for healthy participants (meets I4). The study presents group-level, whole-brain GLM activation maps and paired t-test contrasts, probabilistic atlas labeling, cluster table with voxel counts and MNI coordinates (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E2–E7) apply. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study used a social-related task (Thatcher Illusion face discrimination) that probes social and emotional processing of faces (I3). It reports a healthy adult control group (NT; ages ~25.8) with results reported separately from the ASD group (I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, within-group activation analyses and maps for the control group (within-group whole-brain activation for NT is described and thresholded), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). Reporting of whole-brain results appears in figures and text/tables, satisfying I6. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or missing healthy-group whole-brain maps) are met.

This fMRI study examines implicit processing of emotional faces (a social communication/perception task) and reports results for an age-matched healthy adult control group (n=19). The paper presents group-level whole-brain task effects for controls (text describes control t-maps and specific activations for fearful and neutral faces and contrasts vs baseline), satisfying the requirement for univariate, whole-brain healthy-group activation maps. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and limitations, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only reporting, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social processing (trustworthiness appraisal) and includes a healthy adult control group; it reports whole-brain analyses and coordinate tables. However, the manuscript does not clearly present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or contrast that is explicitly and separately identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Most whole-brain results appear to be reported across all participants or as between-group contrasts, and the explicitly reported control-group effects are given via ROI analyses. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and falls under exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/combined analyses without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task map).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interaction task (multiround trust game) and reports whole-brain, voxel-wise task activation maps. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=21, ages 18–47) with group-level activation maps displayed for benevolence and malevolence (Figure 2A) and whole-brain second-level ANOVA and regressions reported. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, adult sample, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self/other/reflected social evaluations) that includes a healthy adult sample (young adults ages 22–31). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group analyses (2×4×3 ANOVA) with voxel-wise and cluster-extent correction (AlphaSim) and presents group-level results in tables and figures, meeting the requirement for univariate whole-brain healthy-group task effects. No exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports an empirical fMRI study of socially-induced cognitive emotion regulation (Social-Reg) — a social-related task (affiliation/attachment and social cognition), satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults (female participants aged 22–32; final N reported after exclusions), satisfying I4. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., Social-Reg > Social-Look) with cluster-wise FWE correction and provides tables/figures of activation peaks, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This fMRI study examines social-emotional conflict processing using naturalistic film scenes (social cognition/perception of others). Sample comprises healthy adults (25 analyzed, mean age 26.3). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses (mixed-effects group regression, voxelwise thresholding and cluster correction) with coordinates/figures and conjunction/PPI results described for the healthy group. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI during an emotional face-matching task (social perception), in a healthy adult sample (n=98, ages 18–30).
