Group-level voxelwise analyses are reported: ROI and exploratory whole-brain univariate analyses linking OXTR methylation to faces>ovals activation (with FDR correction) and accompanying tables/figures (including whole-brain PPI and unmasked whole-brain results referenced in Tables S1–S2 and figures). The paper therefore provides a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from healthy participants and reports coordinates/figures acceptable under I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and sample is adult). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (fearful face perception) that includes a separate healthy adult control group (n=13) and reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps for the control group (main effect of faces vs scrambled; linear contrasts). Whole-brain GLM analyses are described and control-group activations are reported in tables/figures (with small-volume correction applied to a priori ROIs). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion E6 applies: the paper reports group-level whole-brain multivariate maps (searchlight RSA / representational similarity analyses and related MVPA results) but does not report an univariate, group-level task-evoked whole-brain activation contrast for the healthy adult group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: mental simulation / perception and understanding of others) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 18–27). Inclusion criterion I5 (report of at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map in the form required for pooling univariate activation foci) is not met because the available whole-brain maps are multivariate only, which is explicitly excluded by E6. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This fMRI study uses a social-related task (implicit facial emotion processing) and includes a healthy adult control group, so it meets I3 and I4. However, the paper does not report any univariate, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. The reported results focus on psycho-physiological interaction (PPI) effective connectivity and between-group connectivity contrasts (patient vs control), with the control group used only to localize a seed region. Therefore it lacks the required healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked activation map (I5 not met). This violates exclusion criteria E3 (reports only effective/connectivity analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task map) and E4 (reports primarily between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E3, E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (allocentric judgements of social hierarchy and alliance) in healthy adult participants (22 right-handed males, mean age 24.2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (SPM2 analyses) with corrected thresholds and provides tables of coordinates and SPM figures for the healthy group. Reporting meets the allowance for coordinates/figures in text/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not non-adult sample, not MVPA-only). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this review. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the sample is children/adolescents (boys), with no separate healthy adult group reported. Inclusion criteria I3 (social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample) are NOT met. The paper does report whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for a healthy control group (satisfying I5) and reports results in standard tables/figures (I6). However, failure to include adult healthy participants and the task being non-social mean the study cannot be included.

This empirical fMRI study used a social/affiliative task (mothers viewing own-infant vs stranger-infant videos), includes healthy adult participants (mothers aged 22–37), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (own infant > stranger infant) with figures/tables describing results. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, refs) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The study used fMRI to measure brain activity during repeated retrieval of autobiographical life events that were social interactions (oral examinations), meeting the review’s definition of social-related processing (perception/understanding of self and social events). Participants were healthy adults. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activations (e.g., retrosplenial cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, hippocampus) with corrected statistics, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are described in text and figures/tables. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6), and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study used task-based fMRI of social action planning (pantomime gestures), which is a social-communication-related construct. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=25) reported separately. The paper reports within-group, whole-brain, task-evoked analyses for planning and execution in both groups (within-group results, whole-brain random-effects analyses, thresholded maps and tables/figures/supplementary material are described). The report is not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or between-group contrasts, and the full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cross-modal person identity recognition in healthy adults (meets I3: fMRI during social-related task—perception/understanding of others—and I4: healthy adult sample, n=16, ages 20–31). However, the paper reports results primarily using ROI-based analyses (FFA, OFA, aTL) with significance assessed using ROI-corrected FWE thresholds; the authors state there were no significant results at P<0.05 FWE-corrected for the whole brain without the covariate. They do not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map (or whole-brain significant contrasts) for the healthy group. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses reported with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E2.

While the study uses fMRI during a social-related task (perception of emotional faces) and includes healthy adult participants (including an independent healthy replication sample), it does not report a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The Norwegian discovery whole-brain analyses combine healthy controls and psychiatric patients (results are not presented separately for the healthy group), and the independent North American replication reports significant effects in a healthy-only sample using an anatomical ROI approach rather than an unmasked whole-brain voxelwise map. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain healthy-group voxelwise result) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examines cognitive empathy (emotional perspective-taking), includes a healthy adult control group (n=24), and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses. However, the paper presents results primarily as between-group differential activation (schizophrenia vs. control) and reports peak clusters from those contrasts and percent signal change by group. It does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map (within-group healthy/control task effect) clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and is excluded under exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain healthy-group task map provided).

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (imagery sentence completion referencing 'My mother' and 'My father') probing affiliation/attachment and social processing. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=15, mean age ~28) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise within-group activations for the control group (Table 2; one-sample t-tests with FDR correction and coordinates reported). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (assessment of self, friends, and strangers — constructs: perception/understanding of others, affiliation/close others). Sample comprises healthy adults (N=98, mean age 20.7). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., self > Bush; friends > strangers) with thresholded whole-brain maps and ROI and whole-brain analyses described in Methods and Results (maps thresholded at p<0.001 uncorrected). Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI social-appraisal task (faces, preference vs gender) and includes a healthy adult control group with group-level whole-brain task activation results. The methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses, and results/tables/figures report within-group activation (controls) and coordinates, satisfying requirements for univariate whole-brain task maps. The sample includes adults and healthy controls reported separately. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is a within-subjects fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=21, ages 21–39) using an explicit social task (social feedback) during whole-brain fMRI acquisition. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (negative social feedback > positive social feedback) with tables, figures, and corrected cluster thresholds; results are clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria. Study is complete and appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of social-related fMRI processing in healthy adults.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult parents (ages 22–37) viewing their own vs. standard infant videos, a clear social/affiliation/attachment paradigm (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants and results for the healthy group are reported (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise second-level GLM contrasts (own-infant > standard-infant) and whole-brain intersubject (voxelwise) correlation analyses with voxelwise thresholds and cluster extents, and provides coordinates and cluster descriptions (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only (whole-brain maps are reported), not a connectivity- or resting-state-only study, not limited to between-group-only contrasts, and is empirical fMRI research in adults. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study reports task-based fMRI of social-emotional processing (compassion/empathy) using the Socio-affective Video Task (SoVT), a clearly social-related paradigm. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=94; females aged 18–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate activation results (e.g., HE vs LE, parametric modulations, and training-related contrasts) with FWE correction and stereotactic coordinates presented in text/tables and figures. Thus it meets the review’s criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and provides qualifying whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of face perception/recognition, which fits the social-related construct 'Perception and Understanding of Others' (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (mean ages in mid-20s; N=20 for the fMRI experiment), meeting the age/sample criterion (I4). The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain face localizer contrast (faces > scrambled) used to define ROIs based on an independent participant group (n=83), which constitutes a task-evoked, voxelwise group map from healthy participants (I5). Results and maps are reported in the main text/figures/tables, satisfying acceptability of reporting formats (I6). Although the main analyses emphasize MVPA/RSA, the presence of the univariate group localizer and clear task-based fMRI methods meet the whole-brain requirement. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; fulltext considered complete.

This study includes an fMRI social task (facial expression discrimination) and reports a healthy adult control sample (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the manuscript reports task results as between-group contrasts (patients > controls) showing amygdala hyperactivation in patients and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (no within-group healthy-task whole-brain map is reported or described). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (and I6 is not met because no healthy-group whole-brain results are provided in figures/tables/text). Exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study uses a social rejection task (Cyberball) and includes a healthy adult group, satisfying I3 (fMRI social task) and I4 (healthy adult participants). However, the paper does not present an unambiguous whole-brain, group-level task activation map reported for the healthy adult group alone. The main whole-brain contrasts reported are across the combined adolescent+adult sample, and the adult-specific results are reported as post-hoc tests and an interaction with small-volume correction (SVC) rather than an unmasked whole-brain adult group contrast. Therefore it fails I5 (no clearly identified adult-group whole-brain voxelwise map) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This study used task-based fMRI to probe detection of visuo-motor/visuo-proprioceptive synchrony (ownership of movement), a construct falling under ‘Perception and Understanding of Self’, a social-related processing domain. The sample comprised healthy adults (16 recruited, 15 analyzed; ages 20–28), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (Aa–As, Pa–Ps, and their comparisons) with cluster- and voxel-level thresholds, plus tables/figures localizing activated clusters, meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; thus fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI investigation of social gaze perception (a social-related task) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–30). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses showing correlations between AQ and BOLD response with whole-brain FDR correction and coordinate tables/cluster peaks. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and provides whole-brain results clearly identified as coming from the healthy sample. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of emotion perception from dynamic avatars (social perception of others). Participants: healthy adults (N=19, mean age 28±4.5). Tasks: explicit social-related tasks (emotion classification, intensity rating) using dynamic/static/morphed avatars. Whole-brain, group-level, task-evoked analyses are reported (random-effects GLM, whole-brain contrast maps, cluster-correction; parametric GLM), with figures and reported voxelwise results. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures and text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, not MVPA-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore INCLUDE.

The paper reports fMRI data collected during tasks that probe social-related processes (self-related processing and mentalizing), with healthy adult participants (ages 18–24). The manuscript includes group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses and reports whole-brain results (SI: Fig. S3 and Table S5) linking task-evoked activity to population-level virality, satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants examining social processing (joint attention) with a task-based fMRI paradigm. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate contrasts (e.g., RJA−RJAc; IJA−IJAc) with FDR-corrected maps and tables of coordinates. The sample consists of healthy adults (n=13 final) within adult age range. The full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (empathic judgments / emotional egocentricity) in healthy adult participants. The paper reports two fMRI experiments with group-level task contrasts (including whole-brain analyses in the pilot fMRI1 and group-level contrasts in fMRI2 with reported coordinates and tables), and provides voxelwise activation coordinates and statistical results for healthy adult groups. Participants are healthy adult (female undergraduate) samples (ages consistent with adults). Whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts are described and reported (coordinates, tables, and figures). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study investigates face/emotion processing (social perception) using fearful faces, a social-related task. It includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (n=25) and reports group-level univariate task activation contrasts. Although primary analyses used ROIs, the paper also conducted whole-brain analyses (see Appendix A, Fig. S1 and Supplementary Table 1) with control-group results described, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults (I3, I4, I5, I6). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion IDs met: E3 (study reports only seed-based/ROI functional connectivity during task-state fMRI without reporting a univariate, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy group) and E4 (results focus on between-group network/connectivity differences without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (the study uses task-state fMRI and analyzes self-referential processing, which falls under ‘Perception and Understanding of Self’). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group is reported), I4 (uncertain/unsupported: although a healthy control group is included, the article does not report ages for the control group to verify they are within the 18–65 adult range). Therefore the paper does not provide the required whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps and is excluded.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (implicit and explicit theory-of-mind) in a healthy adult sample (N=22 analyzed, mean age 24.4). The experiment used task-based fMRI during social (belief) stimuli and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results from the explicit general-belief localizer (false-belief vs false-photograph), with Talairach coordinates and a whole-brain figure (Fig.2A). Thus it provides a healthy-group, univariate, whole-brain task-evoked activation map and meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI social tasks in healthy adults. Although parts of the implicit-ToM analyses used an ROI approach, the paper nevertheless contains qualifying whole-brain group results from the explicit localizer. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-communication task (participants believed they received messages from a friend vs a computer). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (final N=18, ages 19–28). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task contrasts (friend > computer) with cluster-level inference and tables/figures, in addition to MVPA/MVCA results. Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked activation maps from the healthy group relevant to social processing. No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study uses an explicit social-related task (facial emotion identification; FEPT) relevant to perception/understanding of others, includes a healthy adult control group (n=22, ages within 18–65), and reports whole-brain, group-level univariate activation maps for the healthy control group (one-sample ‘faces minus animals’ contrast; figures and tables/supplementary activation foci are provided). Whole-brain analyses and HC group maps are explicitly described (individual group maps, ROI/extraction analyses notwithstanding). The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This task-based fMRI study investigates natural touch delivered by another person in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked activation map or contrast for the healthy group (no GLM-style voxelwise task activation map). The analyses are based on group ICA spatial components and component time courses rather than an univariate whole-brain task contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (and hence provides no qualifying whole-brain result as per I6). Exclusion criterion E3 applies (only ICA-based/multivariate component results without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using a social incentive delay task (social reward/punishment cues) in healthy adult participants (nulliparous women ages 20–42). The paper reports group-level voxelwise statistical analyses (ANOVAs) and describes whole-brain exploratory results at p<.001 as well as ROI-corrected VTA findings; results are presented for the healthy/placebo and oxytocin groups. Full article text (background, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain/voxelwise results reported/explored), and I6 (whole-brain results described and acceptable in text/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (self/other perspective-taking) that includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (TD). However, the manuscript does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. The reported whole-brain results are group comparisons (ASD vs. TD) and combined-group contrasts, along with ROI and seed-based connectivity analyses. Therefore it fails to provide the required healthy-group whole-brain univariate activation map (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI task probing self-referential processing and perspective-taking (social-related constructs: Perception/Understanding of Self), includes a healthy control group (HC; adults present within age range 15–35, acceptable per inclusion guidance), and provides within-group whole-brain task activation results for the healthy group (e.g., VMPFC activation for self>other in HC), with group-level voxelwise contrasts and figures/tables. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This article reports an fMRI task examining neural responses to romantic and sexual images—social/affiliation-related constructs—using healthy adult participants (20 heterosexual men, ages 22–50). The methods describe whole-head (whole-brain) univariate analyses (FSL FEAT, FLAME random-effects) with group-level contrasts (sexual>neutral; romantic>neutral; within- and between-group contrasts) reported in figures and tables, providing voxelwise task-evoked activation maps for the healthy adult groups. Thus the study meets the review objective and the required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-adult sample issues). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–22). The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate task activation contrasts (e.g., CC vs CD; OT/AVP vs placebo) with cluster-level correction and describes these healthy-group results in the text and supplementary materials. Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present, so the full text is effectively complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), and I6 (results described in text/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E2–E7) are met.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using fearful and calm faces (a social-emotional task probing perception/understanding of others), includes a healthy adult control group (n=13) reported separately, and presents group-level whole-brain univariate activation results for the control group (within-group and between-group analyses, tables of stereotaxic coordinates and figures). The paper provides full methods, results and discussion, and whole-brain task-evoked maps/peaks are clearly described for the healthy/control group. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI hyperscanning study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses fMRI during a social joint-attention task) and I4 (healthy adult sample: N=54 analyzed, mean age ~24). However, it does NOT report any group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked statistical maps; the analyses focus on multivariate directed functional connectivity among predefined cortical ROIs, with stimulus effects regressed out. Therefore it constitutes ROI/connectivity-only analyses and lacks the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation map, violating exclusion criteria E2 (ROI-only/no whole-brain results) and E3 (connectivity-only without whole-brain task map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=37, mean age ~24.8) that used a social-evaluative task (viewing approving, disapproving, and neutral social videos). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task activation contrasts (negative>neutral, positive>neutral, conjunction) with FWE-corrected results and tables/figures of coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. All inclusion criteria are met (I3: fMRI social task; I4: healthy adult sample; I5: whole-brain group-level maps reported; I6: whole-brain results presented via tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not non-adult sample, not multivariate-only, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (visual perspective taking / theory of mind) in healthy adults (N=16 analyzed; mean age 22.4). The task is social-related (perspective taking), and the paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., Inconsistent Other > Consistent Other; conjunction analyses) analyzed in SPM8 with cluster-level FWE correction; results are reported in tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related approach–avoidance task contrasting social vs. nonsocial stimuli (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (male students, ages ~21) with group-level analyses reported separately (I4). The paper describes whole-brain (exploratory) analyses and indicates whole-brain results are reported (supplementary/online), and the text includes group-level voxelwise contrasts and coordinates beyond ROI SVC analyses (I5, I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core data appear complete in the article (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (such as ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, patient-only samples, multivariate-only maps, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social reasoning (Wason selection tasks contrasting social exchange, precautionary, and descriptive rules) in healthy adult participants (n=12 analyzed, mean age 24.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (story and card-phase contrasts; clusters and coordinates reported) for the healthy sample, with methods, results, and tables described in the full text. The task probes social-related constructs (theory of mind, perception/understanding of others; social exchange), and whole-brain univariate activation contrasts are clearly reported. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

Facial emotion discrimination is a social-processing task (perception/understanding of others) acquired with fMRI. The study includes a healthy adult control group (N=12) with results reported separately and presents whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (within-group and between-group SPM2 analyses; figures and text describe control-group contrasts, e.g., sad > neutral in controls). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (perception of infant cries and faces — affiliation/social communication; satisfies I3). The sample comprises healthy adult nulliparous women aged 19–29 (N=17 analyzed), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., cry vs. pink noise, happy vs. neutral faces) with corrected thresholds, cluster sizes, coordinates, and figures/tables, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, not outside adult age range, and reports univariate whole-brain activation maps). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social cognition (theory of mind and affective empathy) and includes a healthy adult control group, so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the full text reports second-level ANOVA results emphasizing diagnosis effects and between-group contrasts/conjunctions (patient vs control) and structural comparisons; it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (no within-controls whole-brain activation contrast or table/figure of the control group’s univariate task map is provided). Therefore I5 is not met (and I6 is not satisfied). Per exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect), the study must be excluded.

This paper reports an fMRI task (fMRI-modified Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test) probing theory-of-mind/social perception in a cohort of healthy adults, and presents group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts ("mind minus age") with voxelwise statistical thresholds and cluster results. The healthy-control group is reported separately from the patient group. Although the healthy sample's age range (51–84) includes participants older than 65, the inclusion guidance allows modest extension beyond 65 and the healthy-group whole-brain results are clearly presented. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for task, sample reporting, and whole-brain healthy-group activation maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a theory-of-mind (ToM) task (social cognition) in healthy adult participants (n=109). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation contrasts for the healthy sample (ToM>control; reported at P<0.01 FWE) and provides coordinate tables/figures for activation and genotype effects (FDR-corrected whole-brain). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (emotion recognition and integration of gaze and facial expression), meeting the review objective. It includes at least one healthy adult group (younger adults aged 17–27, which falls within the allowable slight extension beyond 18) and reports whole-brain task-evoked results. The paper presents whole-brain analyses (partial least squares) with reported spatial patterns and tables of peak coordinates and bootstrap ratios for the healthy groups, satisfying the requirement that whole-brain healthy-group activation maps be available (reported in results, figures, and tables). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided content appears complete.

Exclusion justification: E2 met (study reports only ROI-based/interregional correlation and structural covariance analyses across 25 predefined face-processing ROIs; no univariate, whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps for the healthy group are reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related face-processing task: viewing happy/fearful faces) and I4 (healthy adult sample from NFBC 1986, age in 20s). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group is provided). The full text appears complete and includes intro, methods, results, and discussion, but the reported imaging results are ROI-based correlations and structural covariance rather than whole-brain univariate activation maps, so the study must be excluded under E2.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (imitation/observation of communicative gestures) in healthy adults (n=20, mean age 24.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (flexible factorial ANOVA) with cluster-corrected results and peak coordinates (MNI) for contrasts such as IMI>CT and S>NS, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review objective and all listed inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social-emotional approach-avoidance task (social-related processing), uses a healthy adult sample (N=279, ages 18–43), and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses with reported whole-brain and SVC-corrected activation clusters (coordinates and statistical thresholds provided). All inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain univariate results are reported; not limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, MVPA-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=59) using social-related tasks (person knowledge, socially relevant concept words) and modality-matched non-social controls. Group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (social > non-social; social/non-social > baseline) are reported with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction, and peak coordinates are provided. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (participants, tasks, scanning, analyses), Results (whole-brain and ROI analyses) and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

Although this paper uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing (inferring others' social emotions) and includes a healthy adult control group (Experiment 1: 17 typically developing adults), the full text does not present a clear, unmasked whole-brain, group-level task activation map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The reported whole-brain results focus on between-group contrasts (typically developing > ASD) and ROI-based follow-up analyses. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI of social processing), I4 (healthy adult control group present). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain, group-level task map for healthy/control group). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses fMRI during a social joint-attention task (I3) and includes a healthy adult group with results reported for HC-HC pairs (I4). However, the full text does not present or clearly identify an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group (INT>NoINT within HC) — the paper focuses on cross-brain coupling and reports between-group comparisons and null group differences for whole-brain tests, but no standalone HC whole-brain activation map or coordinate table is shown in the provided full text. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).
